The tool used for this was restriction analyzer. It also shows that BamHI cuts at 662 position on
plasmid DNA and HindIII cuts at 632 positions. Since we are using two different enzymes, there
is a better chance that our fragment contains rspL gene.
Discussion
The primary objective of this project was to create a genomic library using a streptomycinresistant strain of E.coli Top10 (4537 bp) as the genomic DNA, incorporating it into a pUC19
plasmid (2686 bp) vector (Cirino et al., 2003). The successful construction of this genomic
library was expected to confer streptomycin resistance to a recipient E.coli strain Mach1
through the functional selection of the rspL gene (Hanahan, 1983). However, throughout the
experiment, several challenges were encountered, leading to changes in the experimental
design and troubleshooting of errors.
An initial gel electrophoresis performed to confirm the presence of the rspL gene after digestion
of genomic DNA with BamHI resulted in no visible bands. This was primarily due to the low
concentration of the originally isolated genomic Top10 DNA (33.2 ng/µL), which was further
diluted during the digestion reaction and loading of the gel (Inoue et al., 1990). This
concentration was below the minimum detection limit required for the INtRON RedSafeTM
nucleic acid stain to work efficiently (50 ng/µL). As a consequence, no bands were detected,
and the experiment had to be repeated with a new and cleaned up genomic DNA sample.
Subsequent gel electrophoresis performed after digesting the cleaned-up genomic DNA with
BamHI showed successful digestion of the genomic Top10 DNA, as evidenced by a shorter
smear in comparison to the uncut band of the genomic DNA (Sorek et al., 2013). In addition, the
plasmid pUC19 showed two very faint bands after digestion with BamHI, indicating appropriate
digestion of the plasmid as well.
Part B write up 15
Jetul and Japneet April 9, 2023
A ligation reaction was set up using a 1:1 ratio for cut genomic Top10 DNA (insert) and cut
plasmid pUC19 (vector) (Chen & Dubnau, 2004). After overnight incubation at 4 °C, the ligated
product was transformed into Mach1 chemically competent cells. The initial transformation
results were inconclusive due to contamination observed in the positive control plate.
Moreover, the second transformation attempt resulted in an unsuccessful transformation due
to inefficient uptake of DNA by the host organism, which might have been caused by several
factors, such as improper preparation of competent cells, issues concerning the ligation
reaction, or the transformation protocol itself (Inoue et al., 1990).
To increase the likelihood of obtaining a fragment containing the rspL gene, a third gel
electrophoresis was performed using HindIII in addition to BamHI for digesting both genomic
Top10 DNA and plasmid pUC19 (Cirino et al., 2003). The use of two different enzymes would
increase the accuracy of the construct and facilitate the incorporation of the desired fragment
into the plasmid (Hanahan, 1983).
Based on the information provided by the restriction analyzer, the BamHI enzyme cuts at two
different sites on genomic DNA (180 and 2865), producing large fragments that appeared as a
smear in the gel electrophoresis images (Sorek et al., 2013). HindIII was introduced to cut at an
additional site (4130) on genomic DNA, increasing the likelihood that the fragment containing
the rspL gene would be successfully incorporated into the plasmid (Chen & Dubnau, 2004).
In summary, the construction of a genomic library using E.coli Top10 genomic DNA and pUC19
plasmid DNA encountered several challenges throughout the experiment, including low DNA
concentrations, contamination, and inefficient transformation (Inoue et al., 1990). The
introduction of the HindIII enzyme in addition to BamHI for restriction digestion was expected
to increase the probability of obtaining a fragment containing the rspL gene (Cirino et al., 2003).
Furthermore, troubleshooting in each area of competent cells preparation, ligation reaction,
and transformation protocol can assist in identifying and rectifying these challenges, such as reevaluating the insert-to-vector ratio, incubation time, and temperature for the ligation reaction
or testing and optimizing various transformation conditions (Hanahan, 1983).
For this experiment, the most likely problem would be with transformation. It could be
optimized and modified by making changes mentioned below:
a. Temperature and duration: Confirm that the heat shock conditions (e.g. 42°C for 30-45
seconds) are appropriate for your cells (Inoue et al., 1990).
b. Recovery duration: Allow adequate time (usually 1 hour) for the cells to recover and express
the antibiotic resistance marker (Sorek et al., 2013).
c. Optimal antibiotic concentration: Ensure the appropriate concentration of streptomycin for
selection is used on the plates. Too high or low of a concentration may result in inadequate
selection (Chen & Dubnau, 2004).
Part B write up 16
Jetul and Japneet April 9, 2023
In addition to the technical challenges faced during the genomic library construction, human
errors could also have contributed to the unsuccessful or inconclusive results. These errors can
occur in sample handling, reagent preparation, equipment usage, and protocol execution. Such
errors may include:
1. Cross-contamination: During handling of samples, there is potential for cross-contamination
between different DNA samples or between the samples and reagents, leading to undesired
results (Inoue et al., 1990).
2. Reagent preparation: Errors can occur while preparing various reagents such as buffers,
enzyme solutions, or antibiotics. These could include inaccurate measurement or mixing of
components, resulting in incorrect concentrations that can affect experimental outcomes
(Sorek et al., 2013).
3. Pipetting errors: Inaccurate pipetting can lead to incorrect volumes being dispensed, resulting
in the incorrect sample or reagent concentration, which affects the outcome of experiments
(Hanahan, 1983).
4. Equipment usage: Improper operation, maintenance, or calibration of laboratory equipment
can generate unreliable or inconsistent results. For instance, inaccurate temperature settings
for incubation or heat shock can affect the transformation efficiency (Chen & Dubnau, 2004).
To minimize human errors, it is essential to maintain good laboratory practices, maintaining
proper organization of the workspace, labeling samples accurately, and double-checking
reagent concentrations. Additionally, regularly calibrating and maintaining equipment,
following established protocols carefully, and incorporating appropriate controls into
experiments will help reduce the occurrence of human errors and enhance the overall success
of the genomic library construction process.
Future experiments can investigate alternative restriction enzymes, plasmid vectors, and
competent cell strains to improve the overall success of the genomic library construction
process (Cirino et al., 2003). Moreover, ensuring a suitable recovery time for transformed cells,
providing a nutrient-rich medium during recovery, using appropriate plating methods and
conditions, and including positive and negative controls in each transformation experiment will
aid in enhancing the efficiency of the genomic library construction and subsequent functional
selection of the streptomycin resistance-conferring rspL gene (Hanahan, 1983).
Conclusion
Part B write up 17
Jetul and Japneet April 9, 2023
In conclusion, the construction of a genomic library using E.coli Top10 genomic DNA and pUC19
plasmid DNA proved to be challenging due to several factors, including low DNA
concentrations, contamination, and inefficient transformation. Optimization of the
transformation process, selection of alternative restriction enzymes, plasmid vectors, and
competent cell strains could enhance the overall success of the genomic library construction
and subsequent functional selection of the streptomycin resistance-conferring rspL gene.
Future experiments should also emphasize proper controls, recovery conditions, and nutrientrich media to improve the efficiency of this process.

"Item #: SCP-205

Object Class: Euclid

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-205-1 and SCP-205-2 are contained within Chamber 52 at Site-23, under regular observation via the adjoining observation room. SCP-205-1 and SCP-205-2 are to be supplied with power and face the white projection screen on the wall opposite the observation window at all times. Chamber 52 requires monthly maintenance to ensure the continued operation of both SCP objects, their power supply and remote activation controls. Replacement parts and bulbs are kept on hand in the chamber. Maintenance is suspended during the final month of the SCP-205 cycle, occurring in April and October of each year. Should power to Chamber 52 fail it is to remain dark and sealed for a period of thirty days before local security enters to re-engage power for continued observation and containment.

During maintenance it is critical that only one of the SCP-205 pair is ever turned off at a time. Should both objects lose power or otherwise cease normal operation the chamber must be sealed for a 30 day period before local security may enter to re-engage power and retrieve the remains of any personnel lost in the chamber.

Pending O5 review, testing and observation is to continue before SCP-205 is to be moved to permanent storage.

Description: SCP-205 is a pair of flood lamps used in photography. The light emitted by each lamp behaves in a manner unique to SCP-205 and passes completely through any surface that is not colored white. Once the light contacts a white surface it scatters and reflects as normal and loses any unnatural properties. If the light continues uninterrupted through any matter, otherwise casting no shadow, each lamp will display an unidentified young woman's shadow upon any flat white surface, such as the projection screen in Chamber 52. Whether or not this shadow corresponds to anyone living or dead has yet to be determined, although the shadow appears to re-enact a specific series of events leading up to the woman's death.

Even if the lamps are slightly moved, the shadow remains distinct and does not lose focus or move along with the one lamp or the other. Only one shadow is cast although a physical person standing before two lamps would actually cast two shadows.

When supplied with steady power and maintained, the SCP-205 pair will go through a six month cycle that ends on April 30th and October 31st of each year. Neither the inclusion of an extra day during a Leap Year nor intermittent operation failures change these dates, thus SCP-205's cycle appears to be tied to the standard calendar rather than a set passage of time.

SCP-205 will shut off at midnight on the final day of each cycle. Any persons entering or already inside Chamber 52 when the lamps are both turned off are violently assaulted by forces unseen in a manner consistent with the fate suffered by the shadow woman, regardless of any other light sources in the room.

If the lamps are shut off at the end of a standard six month cycle they can be remotely activated to immediately end the danger and begin a new cycle. If the lamps cease operating for any other reason Chamber 52 will remain dangerous and must remain sealed for at least thirty days regardless of the status of SCP-205 itself. During a dangerous phase any equipment in the room is often ransacked, but although SCP-205 itself has sometimes been moved the lamps are never damaged.

On two occasions [DATA EXPUNGED] were carved into the walls. This strongly implies that [DATA EXPUNGED] displaying an awareness of current containment procedures.

Overview of SCP-205's cycle: For the first month of operation, SCP-205 will display a still image of one woman in a provocative pose. Although variances have been noted in the pose and clothing of the woman, the individual displayed appears to be distinct and consistent through all cycles. During the last week of the first month, the shadow will begin to move slightly as if the individual is shifting her weight or becoming uncomfortable. Her hair and clothing will be observed to flutter in ways that do not correspond to any movement of the atmosphere within Chamber 52. By the end of the first calendar month the shadow will break her pose and spend the next eight hours moving through a series of poses that imply a photography session complete with clothing changes and short breaks, sometimes including a meal.

After this session is over the shadow will constantly be in motion for the next five months, displaying a pantomime of the last days of a young model's life before she is brutally murdered at the end of the cycle. The shadow of the woman never moves beyond the boundaries of the projection screen. The shadows of objects that the woman appears to be interacting with do not appear unless they are being picked up or carried, and with the exception of the final month of the cycle any other individuals that the shadow appears to be interacting with are not seen.

Although the cycle is slightly different each time certain consistencies are observed. The individual portrayed appears to have taken up photography as a hobby in addition to being a fashion model. Her behavior implies a great deal of social interaction although with a lack of intimacy and behavior that indicates living alone rather than with family or a partner. One implied sexual encounter with an unseen partner occurs in the second or third month of the cycle and exactly sixty six explicit sexual encounters occur in the final month of the cycle.

During the last month of the cycle in April and October, shadows distinct from the young woman are displayed. These shadows all have exaggerated nude male physiques and horns projecting from the cranium although no phallus is ever observed, even during the sexual displays that take up the final days of the cycle. Only one shadow appears at first, interacting with the woman in a manner suggesting that they have met at a party or social gathering. The woman does not appear to notice the unusual nature of the other shadow and plays out a series of varying romantic interactions with it. The horned shadow will return to dine with the woman, engage in silent conversations and accompany her on outings. One recurring event involves the horned shadow introducing the woman to at least two other identical horned figures. After the second week of the month the woman will take photographs of one or more of the horned shadows during one of their outings, always with a non-digital camera that has been consistent through all observed viewings of the SCP-205 cycle. After this event explicit sexual encounters will begin between the woman and one of the figures, increasing in intensity and frequency until the end of the third week.

During the final week of the month the woman appears to develop the film in her camera for the first time since photographing the horned shadow(s). Her reaction to the photographs is one of shock and horror, and her movements afterward suggest that she attempts to flee and seek shelter behind a locked door, presumably in her home. There she is encountered by multiple instances of the horned shadow figure which assault her repeatedly for the remainder of the week. It is strongly implied that she is killed during this process although the assaults will continue until the end of the cycle.

On the last day of the cycle one of the horned shadows begins to grow larger in a manner suggesting that the figure casting it is approaching the SCP-205 lamps directly. It will eventually overcast all other shadows and at this time both lamps will be physically turned off regardless of any modifications made to prevent a halt in operation.

Addendum: SCP-205-1 has been in the Foundation's possession since ██-██-████; SCP-205-2 is identical in every way, including the serial number. It was discovered in a ransacked motel room in ████, ██ on █-██-████. No sign of the identity or whereabouts of the occupant have been found, although a camera similar to the one displayed in the sixth month of the SCP-205 cycle was also recovered. Most of the contained film was ruined by exposure; see attached photo for the one image that was developed from the camera.

Incident 205-76b: On 10-28-████, SCP-205-2's bulb burnt out. Researcher M. N████████ was sent in to Chamber 52 to replace the bulb during one of the climactic assaults. Upon the opening of Chamber 52's door, all horned shadow figures within view ceased their activity and turned towards the door. Researcher N████████ resealed the chamber and refused to enter to perform maintenance. Shadow figures did not resume their usual activity for approximately three hours.

Incident 205-77a: On 4-28-████, SCP-205-2's bulb exploded. Shadow figures all ceased activity and looked towards the chamber door. No staff were dispatched to replace the bulb, Chamber 52 sealed and abandoned for 30 days according to procedure."

"Item #: SCP-207

Object Class: Safe

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-207 is to be stored in a waterproofed locking metal container measuring 1 m x 0.5 m x 0.5 m. The key is to be issued to the current head researcher of Site-██'s bio-containment area. SCP-207 is to be retained inside this area at all times, and all personnel entering the area should be checked for any food or drink items, in addition to any other searches required. Any staff seen ingesting SCP-207-1 are to be retained for future study, with all Foundation clearance levels removed.

All vending machines in Site-██ are to only dispense clear carbonated beverages; any variation from transparent is to be investigated immediately.

Description: SCP-207 refers to a crate containing 24 Coca-Cola brand cola drinks. The bottles are designated SCP-207-A to -X. SCP-207-B is currently the active bottle for testing, and no other bottles are to be opened without authorisation from two Level 4 researchers. All bottles have been clearly labelled to aid identification. The liquid held inside these has been confirmed to be identical across all of SCP-207, and should not be ingested outside of supervised testing. The liquid has been classified as SCP-207-1, and is to be treated as a Class 2 chemical hazard. SCP-207-1 does not appear to alter with age; however, the active testing bottle should have its protective cover kept on outside of removing liquid for testing.

Mass spectroscopy and chemical tests have shown higher than usual concentrations of caffeine and sugars (both natural and artificial), along with [REDACTED]. The practical effect of this is when a subject drinks SCP-207-1, they will effectively no longer require sleep or rest, nor attempt to sleep or rest. This effect is not lessened by any soporific or medication yet tested on test subjects. However, only a quantity larger than five (5) millilitres will cause this effect. The reason for this lower boundary existing has not been found, although it is hypothesised by Dr. C█████ that [REDACTED]. As such, unless authorised by two Level 3 researchers, only five (5) millilitres of SCP-207-1 is to be used for testing. Amounts higher than this have shown no difference in effect, with the exception of the Subject SCP-207 was recovered from (See addendum).

In addition to removing the need for rest, SCP-207-1 also causes an increase in motor, reaction, and psychological functions. The increase is linear in progression, with an estimated 50% increase (measured by standard medical protocols, +/-5%) every 6 hours. The practical application of ingestion is that the subject is able to think, react, and move faster than others who have not ingested SCP-207-1. Mental proficiencies show the IQ of the subject to rise in line with other increases.

However, SCP-207-1 does not alter the body of affected subjects. Physiology remains unchanged, and as such, can rarely support the increase in activity. No subjects have lasted longer than 48 hours during testing, with the cause of death varying from massive internal organ failure to exsanguination due to major artery ruptures. Subjects also begin to show stress after roughly 24 hours, usually making each movement extremely carefully, in order to avoid accidents. Tests SCP-207-Alpha and -Rho have shown that after approximately 24 hours, the increases caused by SCP-207-1 mean subjects can easily underestimate their speed. "Item #: SCP-296

Object Class: Primary object classification: Safe, secondary object classification: Safe/Euclid/Keter

Special Containment Procedures: Armed Containment Site-03 has been in the process of reconstruction since the discovery of SCP-296 in the geometric center of the destruction caused by enactment of Emergency Protocol XT-████ (refer to Document #1E-027, Addendum 1, viewable in ████████████). Re-installation of tactical thermonuclear devices in a primary perimeter between the established 100km quarantine perimeter and the exposed region of SCP-296 has also been initiated. As SCP-296 has already exhibited resilience in the face of annihilation-grade weaponry, it is suggested that the TTN devices be calibrated to deliver a high-yield, low-radius explosion so as to minimize damage to ACS-03's existing structures.

All personnel, agents and researchers assigned to SCP-296 must have no criminal background, prior to and during SCP service. Any incidents approximating criminal behavior, as well as suspicions of possible criminal behavior, are to be considered disqualification for assignment to duties directly relating to SCP-296.

Description: Upon examination of the blast crater occupying ACS-03's previous location, a stone channel was discovered in the crater's geometric center. The stone is of an unknown composition, and was utterly unaffected by the detonations of the fail-safe devices utilized by Emergency Protocol XT-████. It is unknown whether the structure designated SCP-296 existed prior to the annihilation of ACS-03's previous installations. However, the contents of SCP-296's interior suggest it was somehow created in the explosion.

From the exterior, SCP-296's entry channel appears to simply be a set of carved, fitted stones arranged around a vertical, rectangular shaft. They extend into the ground for several feet before light simply ceases to penetrate and it enters into darkness.

Initial attempts to investigate followed standard procedure using Class D personnel. Each maintained contact for a few moments before failing to report back. After several personnel were lost in this manner, robotic surveillance was initiated, and revealed the presence of an amphitheater-type structure, around which were seated fifty-six (56) figures of similar appearance. Each was roughly humanoid and made of a substance similar at first glance to ice. Thermal scans indicated a variety of temperatures, varying from figure to figure, and most did not conform to temperatures low enough to support solidification of water.

Surveillance also discovered the remains of the Class D personnel. The deceased exhibited the following characteristics:

Personnel A: A was found beside a figure, with cylindrical wounds extending through her skull - one each surrounding the previous location of each eye socket; one passing laterally through the skull and excising the ears and all associated organs; one excising the nose; one excising the mouth. Subject's skin had also been removed whole and rested beside the corpse, along with the cylinders of bone, flesh and viscera that have been removed from her skull, which rested atop the skin. Wounds confirmed to match those inflicted by Euclid Class SCP-███, confirmed to have been present at ACS-03 during initial installation's annihilation.

Personnel B: B was found collapsed on the ground beside a second figure with what initially appeared to be total destruction of his skeletal system. Autopsy later revealed the complete liquefaction of all interior bodily systems. Damage confirmed to match those inflicted by Euclid Class SCP-███, also confirmed to have been present at ACS-03 during enactment of Emergency Protocol XT-████.

Personnel C-G: Personnel C through G were found beside a third figure. All five personnel occupied roughly the same space at different angles. Still technically collectively alive, the resulting recombinant creature was quite obviously both insane and irreparably crippled and was later terminated on-site. Analysis of records pertaining to Keter Class SCP-███ indicated conformity to exposure to its exponential recombination effect. SCP-███ was also confirmed to have been contained within ACS-03 at time of annihilation.

Surveillance was forcibly terminated before further information could be gathered. The final image transferred by the robot was that of the figure beside the still-active form of personnel C-G shattering and the form of SCP-███ appearing amidst its debris. 76 Class D personnel, 23 agents and 5 researchers were lost before sufficient information regarding SCP-███ could be dispatched to allow for the forced initiation of its hibernation cycle. SCP-███ has since been relocated to Armed Bio-Containment Area-14 and subjected to containment in following with its original procedures.

No further attempts to investigate SCP-296 have been made as of this time. Proposals for controlled systematic testing of each figure has been suggested by Dr. ██████ █████████, but have been denied on the grounds that the risk of releasing SCP-███, although its presence within the amphitheater has yet to be confirmed, is too great.

Addendum 296-1: Dr. ██████ █████████ has proposed that the SCP objects lost during the destruction of ACS-03's original facility were somehow repositioned within SCP-296's interior. The reason for this is unknown, as is the cause for their apparent containment within the ice figures. The theory is supported by the remarkable similarity between the number of SCP objects thought lost to the detonation and the number of figures within SCP-296; however, the inexplicable fifty-sixth figure poses the significant possibility of a threat. Further investigation is postponed.

Addendum 296-2: Dr. ██████ █████████ was discovered emerging from within the interior of SCP-296 on ██/██/200█. She was immediately apprehended and subjected to questioning, upon which several facts were made clear.

Dr. ██████ █████████ had, against policy, falsified entry documents and passed the security checkpoints necessary to investigate SCP-296's interior. Upon her entry, she reported she had an instant of feeling psychically violated, followed by immediate unconsciousness.

When she awoke, she claims one of the figures contacted her telepathically. She could not identify which one at that time, as there was no corresponding visible stimuli, but she insists it is the fifty-sixth figure - the additional figure not corresponding to an SCP object previously stored within ACS-03.

The figure communicated that it was known, in our language, as "Judgment." The Class D personnel initially admitted to its interior were found, as Dr. ██████ █████████ put it, "guilty," and were summarily executed by way of utilization of the SCP objects contained within the figures. It equated the figures to jail cells, and implied the release of SCP-███ was analogous to early release for good behavior. She related that "Judgment" will allow innocent personnel entry to the interior of SCP-296, but that it would be responsible for ultimate assignment of guilt - or lack of guilt - of the personnel itself.

Addendum 296-3: Communications between Dr. ██████ █████████'s research team and "Judgment" have revealed new information regarding the figures within SCP-296. They have compiled a list of the SCP objects contained within SCP-296's figures - identical to ACS-03's original contents - as well as a "map" of the figures and their correlating objects. "Judgment" has also supplied a number for each figure which he states corresponds to the number of "services" it must perform before release.

It is assumed that the services to which "Judgment" refers are executions. As there is no way to know whether the information provided is accurate besides expending enough personnel to release the concerned object, further testing has been halted pending other possible detection methods.

It is to be noted that SCP-███'s tally is quite low. All personnel are to be reminded that under no circumstances are any personnel with suspected criminal behavioral patterns, past or present, to be allowed access to SCP-296. Failure to adhere to this directive will result in termination for all parties involved. SCP-███ cannot be allowed to be released."

Cappuccino is an incredibly gluttonous and laid-back beige puppy, recognizable from his white mullet and particularly rotund tummy. Due to his constant snacking and near-bottomless stomach, his loads are enormous and frequent, and he often poops himself in his sleep during his routinely naps. He prefers to put another diaper layer over his full one instead of changing out of it due to his laziness, and only ever decides to change when it's obvious the pamp he's wearing can't be filled any further. Only ridiculously large, XXL-sized diapers can accommodate for his gargantuan loads, and usually needs his friends' helping paws to assist changing him both into and out of such ludicrously vast diapers.

A silky brown puppy with pink flowers at the base of her ears, she's a stylish, fashion-loving chatterbox and only sees diapers and wearing them as such, a fashion statement, often pairing them with her elegant dresses and outright refuses to poop in any of hers... though just like the other pups, she inevitably does, after which she will immediately go out of her way to change into a clean one. Chiffon is the tomboy of the bunch, contrasting Mocha's girliness. A light orange puppy with thick, fluffy ears and tail, she's immensely spunky, sporty and energetic, often spending an entire morning and afternoon running around or playing sports outdoors, and wears diapers as a means of relieving herself in the middle of her athletics instead of wasting time and energy finding the nearest bathroom, oftentimes becoming so engaged with a strenuous activity she's doing she doesn't notice her diaper is totally loaded until after she's done. Espresso is a cream-colored puppy with curled ears, the most intelligent of the pups, being well-bred and mild-mannered. A clever mind and a modest gentleman at heart, he is a natural expert at a variety of things, including painting and music, and is extensively knowledgeable on everything to do with diapers, from their varying sizes and respective capacities, as well as the best brands of diapers for any occasion and where to find them, as well as being an excellent and charismatic diaper changer and barista. Infrequently poops in his diapers, and will gladly keep a full one on for a while, even an entire afternoon, before changing himself, to ensure he doesn't go through too many too quickly.
Milk is the baby of the group. A teeny-tiny white pup, he's quite spoiled by the other pups and is never seen without his favorite pacifier in his mouth. Due to being an infant, he wets his diapers near constantly and can only babble the phrase "Ba-boo".
Include an exchange where all of the puppies, excluding Mocha, decide to have a big diaper-filling contest after they all eat an enormous dinner; whoever has the fullest, poopiest diaper wins and gets to smush and nuzzle the losers' packed diapers, as well as sound effects and onomatopoeia for the noisy messes the puppies make whenever they poop in their diapers out of habit (e.g. *FLBORRRRMPHT!*, *BLARRRRRMP!*, *BLORRRTCH!*, etc.), and dialogue from the puppies eagerly anticipating the giant poopies they're ready to unload into their diapers.

Slide 1: Introduction to Acid Rain
- Definition of acid rain: Precipitation with a pH level lower than 5.6, caused by the atmospheric deposition of sulfuric and nitric acids
- Formation process: Emissions of sulfur dioxide (SO2) and nitrogen oxides (NOx) from human activities (e.g., burning fossil fuels) react with water, oxygen, and other chemicals in the atmosphere to form acidic compounds
- Consequences: Acid rain has negative effects on waterways, forests, wildlife, architecture, and human health

Slide 2: Causes of Acid Rain in the Great Lakes Region
- Industrial and power plant emissions: Coal-fired power plants and manufacturing facilities are major sources of SO2 and NOx emissions in the region
- Transportation: Vehicle exhaust contributes to NOx emissions
- Geography and weather patterns: The region’s prevailing winds and lake-effect weather patterns can transport and deposit air pollutants within and across state and international borders
- Lake-air interactions: The Great Lakes influence regional weather by modifying air temperature, humidity, and wind patterns, potentially exacerbating acid rain issues

Slide 3: Impact of Acid Rain on the Great Lakes Ecosystem
- Altered pH levels: Acid rain lowers the pH of water bodies, making them more acidic and potentially toxic to aquatic life
- Forest stress: Acid rain can leach nutrients like calcium and magnesium from the soil, weaken trees, and make them more susceptible to pests, disease, and climate stressors
- Wildlife impacts: Changes in vegetation, water chemistry, and food availability can disrupt ecosystems and harm species dependent on the affected habitat

Slide 4: Impact on Human Health and Recreation
- Toxic metals: Acid rain can promote the release of naturally occurring toxic metals (e.g., mercury, lead) from the soil, contaminating water sources and fish
- Drinking water: Acidic water sources can corrode pipes and release harmful metals like lead, posing risks to human health
- Recreation across the Great Lakes: Swimming, boating, and fishing activities can be affected by water quality, with fish consumption advisories due to contamination

Slide 5: Acid Rain Regulations and Policy
- The Clean Air Act (CAA): U.S. legislation aimed at reducing emissions of air pollutants, including SO2 and NOx
- Amendments to the CAA: The 1990 amendments established the Acid Rain Program, a cap-and-trade system designed to reduce national SO2 and NOx emissions
- International cooperation: The Canada-United States Air Quality Agreement (1991) aims to address transboundary air pollution, including acid rain-causing emissions


Slide 6: Solutions and Future Challenges
- Clean energy transition: Shifting toward renewable energy sources (e.g., solar, wind, nuclear) can help reduce emissions contributing to acid rain
- Technology advancements: Improved methods for reducing emissions from existing sources, such as carbon capture and storage or scrubber technology
- Ecosystem recovery: Reforestation and ecosystem restoration efforts can help recovery from acid rain damage, though long-term monitoring is necessary

Slide 7: Conclusion
- The importance of maintaining and strengthening regulations to address SO2 and NOx emissions for the protection of human health, ecosystems, and recreational activities in the Great Lakes region
- The potential exacerbation of acid rain issues due to climate change, requiring continued attention and enhanced, cooperative efforts
- Ongoing collaboration between industry, government, communities, and international partners is crucial for effective acid rain mitigation and ecosystem recovery

introduction:

When viewed by a sentient observer, SCP-305 appears to be a mobile, animate humanoid of indeterminate sex. This manifestation is formed of cracked rock similar to SCP-305’s physical form, and while it is faceless, subjects report that the cracks all over SCP-305’s surface begin to resemble human lips and ears as it moves.

Human subjects who make visual contact with this manifestation hear “whispering” voices, although recording equipment in the area picks up nothing and the phenomenon is observed even in subjects who are deaf from birth. SCP-305 will initially ingratiate itself with the subject by whispering compliments. During this phase the subject experiences feelings of friendliness and trust toward SCP-305. “You have beautiful eye-sockets.”
“[REDACTED] every one of your fingers”
“Your neck appears unusually flexible.”
In the second phase, the subject begins to hear many voices emanating from SCP-305. At this point the whispers become critical, attempting to insult the subject or undermine the subject’s self esteem, especially by playing on the subject’s guilty conscience. Like the compliments, these insults make little sense when recounted, but have a profound psychological effect, driving the subject to suicide before the final phase in 20% of cases. If the subject is removed from SCP-305’s presence during phase two, the subject will hallucinate that these insults are emanating from mouth-like cracks that appear to form on the ground, walls and ceiling.

In the third and final phase, the voices will abruptly stop. 2 to 10 hours from the cessation of hallucinations, SCP-305’s humanoid manifestation will appear and kill the subject. Causes of death are varied but include severe cardiac infarct, muscle spasm leading to severing of the spinal column, diaphragm paralysis and [REDACTED].

A subject who dies of any cause after the beginning of the second phase [DATA EXPUNGED] followed by the emergence of an instance of SCP-305-1 from the corpse. In subjects who have entered stage two, manifestation of SCP-305-1 can only be prevented by removal of 80% [DATA EXPUNGED].

"Step 1: Design of the Method
In this step, we will focus on designing a robust, scalable, and efficient computational machine learning pipeline for drug repurposing. We will explore the state-of-the-art techniques in machine learning, specifically deep learning approaches, and tailor them to address our specific needs in drug repurposing. Our core methodology will be the development of a graph embedding function that can preprocess various types of graphs (e.g., chemical structures, protein-protein interaction networks, disease-drug associations, etc.) and convert them into a suitable format for serving as input to neural networks. The design phase will involve reviewing relevant literature in graph representation learning, comparing different graph embedding techniques, and determining the most suitable architecture of neural networks (e.g., Graph Convolutional Networks, Graph Attention Networks) to be employed in the pipeline.

Step 2: Development of the Method
Once the pipeline design is finalized, the focus will shift towards the development of the method. This phase will involve the implementation of the chosen machine learning models and graph embedding functions, along with the creation of a user-friendly interface for researchers to interact with the pipeline. We will also need to preprocess and curate a large-scale dataset containing information on drugs, diseases, and their molecular interactions. Our goal will be to create a high-quality, well-annotated dataset that can be used for training and testing the machine learning models. Finally, we will develop the necessary data processing and input/output handling modules that will enable the seamless integration of different components of the computational pipeline.

“The leader motions to his cheek, saying ‘first here’ and the boy kisses his cheek and gives him a hug. The leader then puts his forehead to that of the boy’s, before sticking out his tongue, saying ‘and suck my tongue.’ As some people laugh, the boy sticks his tongue out before withdrawing a little, as does the Dalai Lama.” You can see part of the moment here.

After that, the Dalai Lama counsels the boy to look to “good human beings who create peace and happiness.”

can you write me a lengthy, highly detailed, and grammatically professional essay with a range of topics and an embedded harvard references and a harvard reference section answering: “What are the ethical implications surrounding the employment of mass surveillance for data collection in contemporary society?”

Summarize the following in 250 words: Ever since its initial introduction in the mid-1960s, the technology behind public facial recognition has increased exponentially in complexity and accuracy to where it is in 2023. Although the software has many positive benefits associated with it including stronger security measures, far more efficient shopping, and protection against identity theft, it comes with its fair share of costs such as the potential for data vulnerabilities or technology manipulation. Arguably its most important cost is its threat to individual and societal privacy, personal freedoms, and personal rights. Utilized all around the world by many countries, including the United States, in a variety of different contexts, China is undoubtedly the country with a facial recognition system that is the most pervasive in society, with a huge database of faces. In China, public facial recognition allows access to certain types of private information, which can be used to maintain a semblance of control over the general public, however, it can also be used to protect their livelihoods. 
One example of its use in China is Beijing’s Temple of Heaven installing face scanners to catch toilet paper thieves. In China many public restrooms aren’t equipped with toilet paper, however, Beijing’s Temple of Heaven was one of the few places where there was toilet paper available for patrons to use. In an attempt to curb the theft from the building, facial scanners were installed to only supply patrons with limited supplies. This has caused complaints from many people, stating that the quantity isn’t enough and also that it’s too slow as it takes around 30 seconds to fully print out the paper (Andrews, 2021). A second example of this surveillance is found in many public schools, where cameras have been installed above the blackboards whose sole purpose is to monitor a student’s facial expressions. Every 30 seconds the cameras feed the data to a machine-learning model that analyzes the facial expressions and determines whether the student is focused or not (Chan, 2018). It then sends this information to the professor and the professor grades them per the results that are returned. Not only does the system take in facial expressions, but it also monitors students’ actions and functions as a replacement for student IDs as students can buy things in the local campus store with just their faces (Tone, 2022).
These are only two examples of the advancements that China has made with its facial recognition system, but between 2010 and 2018, the number of face scanners installed in China grew by over 800% (Tone, 2022).  This ever-expanding increase in its usage raises and highlights a myriad of ethical concerns. According to G2, a peer-to-peer review site, the top six ethical concerns related to these systems in the US are racial bias due to testing inaccuracies, racial discrimination in law enforcement, data privacy, lack of informed consent and transparency, mass surveillance, and data breaches and ineffective legal support (Gangarapu, 2022). Although these considerations were written with the US in mind, all six of these can be translated into the ethical issues in China’s case. While some are more direct, such as mass surveillance and data privacy issues, others take on a different meaning. For example, while racial discrimination in law enforcement in the US mostly disadvantages African Americans, in China the software is being used to discriminate against Uighur Muslims. On the counterargument side, there are benefits to this massive increase, namely protection against identity theft and security, that should be weighed against the cost to ethically examine the issue at hand. Overall, public facial recognition can bring positive and negative effects to society which becomes a complex ethical issue that can be analyzed from different perspectives such as Deontology, Utilitarianism, and Virtue Ethics. 
Beginning with deontology, it is mainly associated with Immanuel Kant who bases the correctness of actions on fulfilling the duties of the individual performing such actions (Taylor. R.M, 2013). Therefore, by understanding the duties of the people performing facial recognition on a large scale; deontological ethics can help us understand the ethical implications of China's use of facial recognition technology. Such analysis must determine if the use of facial recognition adheres to the categorical imperative, the formula of humanity, the universalizability principle, and the overall moral worth of actions. 
From a deontological perspective, the formula of humanity states that individuals have inherent value and dignity, and they should be treated as ends in themselves, rather than as mere means to achieve some other goal (Kant, 1993). The use of facial recognition technology in public places such as airports, train stations, and shopping malls in China may be considered a violation of this principle since it treats individuals as mere means to achieve security and surveillance objectives (Dou. E, 2021). Facial recognition technology invades individuals' privacy by tracking their movements and activities in public places, without their consent or knowledge. Therefore, individuals are not being treated as autonomous agents capable of making their own decisions and living their lives autonomously. Instead, they are being monitored and controlled by the state, which undermines their dignity and freedom. 
Additionally, the use of such technology in public places in China may be considered unethical due to the idea of categorical imperatives. According to Kant, an action is good only if it conforms with a maxim that should be unquestionably universalized (Kant, 1993). In other words, an action is ethical as long as it follows rules that can become a universal law. China's use of facial recognition technology violates this principle because if it were to become a universal law, it would result in a world where everyone is constantly under surveillance, with no privacy or freedom.
Furthermore, facial recognition technology poses ethical concerns regarding the risk of bias and discrimination, as the accuracy of the system is not equal for all individuals, with higher error rates for people with darker skin tones and women (Mozur. P, 2019). From a deontological perspective, the use of facial recognition in law enforcement and security contexts may perpetuate existing biases and discrimination against certain groups of people. This issue is exacerbated by China's use of facial recognition technology, as the government has utilized the system to monitor and suppress the Uighur Muslim minority in Xinjiang province (Mozur. P, 2019). This kind of use of facial recognition technology further violates the categorical imperative, as it creates a moral dilemma wherein one cannot imagine the maxim of such an action becoming a universal law. Moreover, such utilization of facial recognition lacks moral worth because the action is not performed from a sense of duty, which is the necessity of acting from respect for the moral law. Instead, the action is performed for the purpose of improving security measures in China. Finally, the arbitrary detention and persecution of individuals based on their identity, as enabled by facial recognition technology, is a clear violation of the formula of humanity as it treats the victims as means to achieve better security measures. 
In addition to the categorical imperative and formula of humanity, deontological ethics dictates that actions should be judged based on their adherence to moral principles, rather than their outcomes. Kant describes a duty as the necessity of respecting the law; therefore, actions with moral worth must always adhere to the law regardless of its purpose. However, China's use of facial recognition technology is a prime example of actions that lack respect for the law. This is largely due to the lack of transparency and accountability in the deployment of the technology. Additionally, the lack of transparency around how this technology is used and who has access to it undermines the principle of transparency and accountability which are crucial in modern justice systems. These actions lack moral worth simply because they do not adhere to fundamental ethical principles and prioritize the interests of the state over the rights and dignity of the individual. Ultimately, a balance must be struck between security and privacy for facial recognition to be deployed; such balance must be achieved by adhering to moral principles and respecting humanity by treating Chinese citizens as ends in themselves. 

While deontology focuses on the actions themselves, utilitarianism cares more about the consequences of said actions. In its purest form, act utilitarianism operates under the simple principle that actions should produce the greatest good for the greatest number of people no matter what it takes to commit those actions. A modified form of utilitarianism that takes into account the idea that sometimes the action associated with the greatest good is extremely corrupt or immoral is rule utilitarianism. Under this framework, actions seek to follow general rules that produce the greatest good for the greatest number. The ideal of the greatest good for the greatest number can be measured in terms of the utility associated with outcomes, i.e. the total satisfaction or value of the benefits subtracted by the value of costs for outcomes. In the context of China, weighing the ethicality of their FRT systems requires weighing its perceived benefits, mainly increased safety, against its perceived costs, such as invasion of privacy and rights.
Those following the ideals of act utilitarianism would unequivocally support China’s use of public facial recognition technology as its benefits outweigh the costs in terms of citizen utility. Ironically, utilitarianism ideals have been part of the backbone of the decision-making process for the Chinese government following World II. For instance, the Lowy Institute, an independent foreign policy think-tank based out of Australia, states that “late Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping replaced dogmatic Maoism with pragmatic utilitarianism…(for) one objective - economic growth” (Yu, 2018) when he came to power in 1978. From there, “utilitarianism created China’s economic euphoria, and with it the delusion that it may surpass fundamental human moral challenges”. Although the idea may not be as ever-present under Xi Jinping’s orthodox communist regime, utilitarian ideals certainly pervaded its way into Chinese society, especially in the form of helping to make the country better, no matter the cost to its citizens.
 As aforementioned, FRT in China is mainly used as a form of state surveillance, as it “races to become the first to implement a pervasive system of algorithmic surveillance” (Diamond and Mitchell, 2018). One example of the way they seek to achieve this is by developing a “citizen-score” to incentivize good behavior through a series of cameras. With an invasion of privacy at its costs, it comes with the benefit of deterring citizens from stealing, breaking traffic laws, murdering, selling drugs, or committing other petty or serious crimes. Society as a whole would be better off with this change under act utilitarianism, where the ends justify the means, as the citizen score helps keep citizens safe without them even having to think about it. For a hypothetical case of the citizen score in action, consider “a 17-year-old teenage boy (walking) into a liquor store” to buy beer with a fake ID (Carzo, 2010). Currently, in the United States, this is a scenario that happens far too often and easily, as fake IDs become more realistic. However, in a situation such as the one China is in the process of implementing, instantly “an FRT system…alert(s) the clerk behind the counter”, making it impossible for the boy to buy alcohol and thus making the world as a whole safer. FRT’s positive consequences are the prevention of the child breaking the law, preventing the “potential over-consumption of alcohol”, and improving the happiness of those close to him by keeping him safe, all with an associated cost of decreased privacy. 
Rule utilitarianism’s perspective on China’s increasing FRT usage holds a similar opinion to act utilitarianism with a caveat. The main difference between the set ethical theories is that while rule utilitarianism always seeks the greatest good for the greatest number, individuals must also commit actions limited by a general code of conduct. For example, consider two Chinese citizens A and B. A murders B in broad daylight in the middle of a city street and using their widespread facial recognition technology, A is caught on the other side of the city and arrested for him. Under both act and rule utilitarianism, this would be an acceptable use of the technology as it was used to prevent a potential serial killer from murdering again without violating a code of conduct. Now consider the toilet paper theft example. Here act utilitarianism would argue in favor of its usage, as it is allowing as many people as possible to have access to toilet paper, while also preventing the potential theft of it. Meanwhile, rule utilitarianism’s perspective is not as crystal clear, as a potential “general rule” for the code of conduct could be that individuals should have unlimited access to basic needs, such as toilet paper. Overall, China’s FRT is in line with the ideals of act utilitarianism across the board, while rule utilitarianism says it likely goes too far. On a different side of the ethical spectrum, virtue ethics views the situation in a different light.
Virtue ethics is a moral philosophy that focuses on the character of the individual and their morals rather than focusing on the actions themselves or the outcome of the action. The benefit of this is that it doesn’t rely on a rigid moral code and universal principles. Virtues are qualities of one’s character that are considered to be morally good. Examples of virtues are courage, justice, wisdom, and compassion. Analyzing the Chinese surveillance state through the lens of virtue ethics shows that while it may not be virtuous, it encourages the citizens to be more virtuous.
In Virtue ethics, the Golden mean principle refers to finding the right balance between deficiency and excess between different virtues. This can be applied to China’s use of facial recognition as privacy and security are two virtues which are opposing each other. While security does get enhanced due to criminals being easier to catch and the system itself being a crime deterrent, privacy gets sacrificed as widespread surveillance is required to ensure security and that criminals won’t be able to sneak into blind spots in the system and effectively disappear. The promotion of the virtue of security is visible when three citizens with a previous criminal history checked into a hotel at the same time, the police were notified of a potential crime risk. (Mozur et al. 2022) This level of risk mitigation and tracking is notorious enough that when citizens with a previous criminal history turn off their cell phones, police may show up at their houses to check for the individual. A clear example of a violation of privacy is that they monitor their actions without their permission. It also reduces their autonomy and individuality as citizens are being coerced to behave how the government wants them to with little room to maneuver. When citizens are being arbitrarily held in detention or generally punished without any particular evidence, it promotes fear, where people are afraid to engage in activities that may be deemed inappropriate by the government. This approach can lead to a lack of trust between citizens and the government, which can be detrimental to society's stability and so a potential virtuous solution would be to promote clarity within the surveillance system where the citizens wouldn’t need to fear it as much as they would know the rules to follow.
	Another core concept in Aristotelian Virtue ethics is the notion of eudaimonia which translates as happiness or welfare but can be understood to mean achieving happiness through the pursuit of virtues. In other words, happiness or pleasure is the result of a virtuous life. From the perspective of eudaimonia, China’s use of facial recognition software can be seen as ethical as it promotes the general happiness of the population. This is because the Chinese Surveillance system has implemented strict regulations that citizens must follow, and they are monitored to ensure compliance. This system has helped to create an orderly society, where people feel secure and harmonious, increasing eudaimonia in the process. This approach helps maintain social cohesion, which is essential to promoting stability and prosperity. For example, the use of facial recognition technology has been successful in catching criminals and reducing crime rates in China. A man was caught in a crowd of 60,000 people thanks to facial recognition technology, and another case where a man was arrested for fraud after being caught by a facial recognition system in a train station. (BBC, 2018) These successes suggest that the surveillance system has contributed to public safety and security in China. A woman with mental illness left her house, and the camera installed by her records her movements so the police can track her in case something happens to her.  (Mozur et al. 2022) This promotes safety where individuals that may not be able to take full care of themselves can be protected without having a constant presence near them.
In contrast, eudaimonia would also identify that the Chinese Surveillance State is potentially unethical as it enables the government to abuse its power, as the government has the power to punish citizens for activities it deems inappropriate, without any transparent or fair judicial process. This approach can lead to unjust and unfair treatment of citizens, which goes against the virtues of justice and fairness and promotes widespread negativity. Citizens with only the potential of protesting may get notified by the police when they start traveling to protest-heavy places.  (Mozur et al. 2022)
While the Chinese government's implementation of surveillance technology has led to a safer, more orderly, and more efficient society, it also violates privacy and autonomy, promotes conformity over individuality, and promotes fear over trust. Additionally, the system enables the abuse of power, which can lead to unjust and unfair treatment of citizens. If a system of checks and balances were implemented and the system became more transparent, the system could become more ethical. Especially since that virtues are context dependent and what is seen as virtuous in some countries may not be seen as important in others. The Chinese government needs to balance the benefits of surveillance technology with the virtues of its citizens.
Regardless of which moral standpoint is taken when discussing government surveillance in China, several things may arise from this. These range from more minor things like making it easier for parents to keep track of their kids to the worry of having a government abuse the power that this gives them.
On one side there are benefits to having a widespread facial recognition system. As mentioned previously parents will be able to keep track of their kid's location to ensure they're safe. The police and other figures of authority can use it to track down kidnapped or lost children/people. It can be used to make transactions more secure, similar to how some schools are using a facial recognition system to sell products to students. Or, as shown with the toilet paper, it can be used to help prevent theft. All of these are things that will generally be seen as beneficial to society as a whole as it helps keep people safe and helps lower the crime rate and the number of criminals that escape the authorities. However, there are still some drawbacks to such a system.
The main drawback, and the easiest to see, is the power that this would give a government. Widespread facial recognition makes it so that the government, or whoever controls the system, will always have access to where individuals are and what they have been up to. Having such a system with a more tyrannical government in power would be highly detrimental to that country's society as it could very easily be used to maintain control and fear over the population. In addition, such a system removes the possibility for privacy that a lot of people like. It'd be even easier to keep track of someone's routines and to know what they are up to and at what time which is something that many people would rather keep private.
Another impact that this can have would be in the court. It’ll be easier for people to be convicted because there will be video evidence of the theft happening, paired with the system that identifies the criminal as you. However, this leads to a lot of problems, especially with an inaccurate system. It’d be impossible to make a system that always identifies a person correctly so this could lead to someone being wrongly convicted, an issue that is already happening today but that could be aggravated by a system like this. Especially if the system is more inaccurate with a specific race or skin color. Assume that the system is trained with mostly Caucasians. It would understand very well what the key differences are between different faces of white people but if we then test it on a group of Asians it’d be possible that it can’t find those key differences in them and underperforms. This is something that already happens to real people where non-Asians state that “All Asians look the same.” This is simply due to not knowing what to look for that distinguishes people.
	While the Chinese surveillance state has its immediate benefits such as a safer, efficient society, however, when it gets analyzed through various ethical frameworks, the issue becomes more nuanced. From deontology, China’s use of facial recognition raises concerns about privacy violations and abuse of power, violating principles of treating individuals as ends in themselves under the Formula for Humanity, universal rules under the Universalizability Principle, and respect for the law while lacking transparency and authority. From an act utilitarianism perspective, the use of this surveillance system is undoubtedly bringing more pleasure than pain to society, whereas a rule utilitarianism perspective is a little grayer and depends on the context surrounding the specific case at hand. Finally, when analyzed from the perspective of virtue ethics, the ideals of golden means between deficiency and excess and eudaimonia also disapprove of its continued utilization. In conclusion, the use of a widespread facial recognition system brings up a lot of ethical dilemmas when observed through different lenses; however, if it is properly regulated we can minimize or resolve most of those dilemmas and allow the community to use the benefits safely.

在科技飞速发展的时代，大数据、云计算、物联网、区块链、人工智能等尖端技术已经渗透到世界的各个角落。为了帮助青少年更好地了解这些技术以及它们在现实生活中的应用，本书将以简明扼要、通俗易懂的语言向青少年介绍这些技术的原理和实践，培养他们的科学素养。

二、目的和意义
本书旨在激发青少年对科技的兴趣，提高他们对科技变革趋势的认识，培养科学素养。通过学习相关内容，青少年将对科技领域有更深刻的认识，为他们将来成为掌控科技变革的有为青年奠定基础。

三、读者对象
本书主要针对12-18岁的青少年，尤其是对科技、互联网和人工智能有兴趣的青少年。

四、内容策划
本书将分为五大部分，详细介绍大数据、云计算、物联网、区块链与人工智能方面的知识和应用，结构清晰，层次分明。

第二部分：云计算的崛起
1. 什么是云计算？
2. 云计算的三种服务模型：IaaS、PaaS、SaaS
3. 云计算的部署模式：公有云、私有云、混合云
4. 云计算带来的便利与创新
5. 云计算的现实挑战与未来发展

第三部分：物联网的智能网络
1. 物联网：让万物互联的科技革命
2. 物联网的基本概念与技术架构
3. 物联网在智能家居、智能交通等领域的应用
4. 物联网的安全与挑战
5. 物联网的未来趋势

第四部分：区块链：颠覆传统的技术力量
1. 什么是区块链？

4. 区块链的安全及监管问题
5. 区块链的潜在发展前景与可能的挑战

第五部分：人工智能的奥秘
1. 人工智能简介：从梦想到现实
2. 机器学习：让机器自主“成长”

5. 人工智能在现实生活中的应用与影响

请帮我把以下内容用视频文案的形式写出来，要求口语化、节奏合适、吸引人观看，500字以上:相信爱读书的朋友或者居家办公的朋友都知道，一个舒适的工作和读书环境有多么的重要。那么这个环境是否舒适，就取决于我们书房的布置，尤其是写字台的布置。另外，写字台的布置也与风水息息相关，所以要分外谨慎。接下来就为大家揭秘哪些布局是有利于书房风水的吧。书房书桌布局的角煞和横梁压顶每个房间都会有窗户，这是正常的，那么在布局上也就要注意书桌与窗户的位置，要注意窗外十公尺以内其它房屋射入的尖角，尖角距离越远影响越小，越近影响越大。书桌同样忌讳横梁压顶，如果实在无法避免也要装设天花板将之挡住。当然，更忌横梁压在坐者的头顶或书桌上，否则事业的经营必然困难重重，也会对孩子或者成人的心理和身体造成双重伤害。书桌适合放置在文昌位，文昌位在风水位中代表着学业、事业，并且在风水上文昌方位主事业成功、主学有所成，因此你若是期望书房的风水气场旺盛，期望自己的事业发展顺利，可以尝试将书桌放置在文昌位上，这样摆放书桌可以高效的提升我们的事业运势、学业运程，也有利于克服工作瓶颈，平步青云。书桌摆放不宜背对窗户关于书桌与窗户的相对位置还有一点注意，那就是切忌让书桌背对着窗户，这样容易形成“背水面山”之不利地形。书桌摆放背对窗户肯定是不科学的，这样摆放不利于自然光源照进书房，形成背光之势，在这样的光线条件下看书，对眼睛健康非常不好。设计过不少因为空间受限制的原因，窗户太小，甚至书桌没法放到窗户附近，这时就需要我们弥补光线的不足了。

标题：东鹏瓷砖：刘擎×李雪琴南山对话，寻味陶渊明的悠然生活

3月9日东鹏瓷砖发布潮系列新品，并携手品牌挚友刘擎和李雪琴演绎短片《见南山》。片中两人以陶渊明的诗为引子，结合现代生活探讨新时代如何保持一颗悠然之心。
开篇，刘擎由“采菊东篱下，悠然见南山”发问：“现代的人，还找得到去南山的路吗？”李雪琴回复：“来的时候我也这样问司机了，他说去深圳得加钱。”两人心领神会地相视一笑，正式拉开南山对话的序幕。
短片共分为四个章节，每个章节名皆源于陶渊明的诗句。

第壹折·久在樊笼里，复得返自然
这一段，李雪琴和刘擎针对“是归隐还是逃避”展开讨论。
李雪琴：有时候我也想像陶渊明一样，回南山种地。您说他是真的享受归隐呢，还是在逃避呢？
刘擎：其实你不是想问陶渊明，而是在问你自己。
 这也恰好对应了当代许多人“心有田园”而“实不可至”的现状。

第贰折·种豆南山下，草盛豆苗稀
本段对话围绕“焦虑”展开。
李雪琴：所谓焦虑，就是怕自己做得不够好吧。
刘擎：但人的本能，就是会把自己和他人做区分。
 焦虑、同伴压力，同样作为被人们热议的话题，在这里，刘擎老师一针见血地击中焦虑本源——比较心。

第叁折·行行失故路，任道或能通
关于焦虑、迷茫，刘擎和李雪琴进一步给出解答——
刘擎：所以我们总是容易被眼前的东西困住，但有的事情离得太近反而看不清楚。
李雪琴：就像雪化了之后不是水，而是春天。
 原来，困住我们的是眼前的视角、态度。

第肆折·此种有真意，欲辨已忘言
南山到底在哪？它不一定是一座物质意义上的山，而可能一直在我们心中，等待被看见。
刘擎：今天我们说起陶公，我们羡慕他，为自己垒了一座南山。
李雪琴：那是一座平静的南山，平静地面对自己的高峰，但也诚实地面对低谷。
刘擎：羡慕这座坦诚的山，比起他人的评价，更在乎自己的内心。
李雪琴：当然，也是一座不管风雨的南山。从此不再执念对错，也不再去追问因果。
刘擎：他决定留下一片松林，一片竹影。过时代更迭，也许陶公早就明白，世事再无常，也敌不过一颗平常心。

最后，短片以“在心里垒一座南山，也为自己安放一座「见南山」”点题，也和产品进行关联。又以陶渊明的“山气日夕佳，飞鸟相与还”与“归家”做连接，也点出了东鹏陶瓷的品牌特性。

def preprocess(text):

As far as I know, the usual air route from London to Auckland/Tāmaki Makaurau goes via Singapore and is roughly 19 290 kilometres, which is about five percent further, though still not exactly halfway round the world, which ought to be exactly 20 000 kilometres due to the way the metre is defined but is in fact not. Consequently Singapore is actually slightly north of east of London, but predominantly east even though it’s in the Southern Hemisphere and London is in the northern half of the Northern one. Once again this is counterintuitive. The difference between the two distances is almost exactly the same as London to Lerwick. You can almost fit a whole “British Isles” in that distance. Sadly, this still isn’t very much compared to the whole distance. However, if one were to walk from Land’s End to John O’Groats, which again is almost exactly that distance, it would be considered far more ecologically sound than travelling by plane. It’s like “one death is a tragedy, a million deaths is a statistic”.
