小型无人机具有成本低、体积小、发现难、速度慢等诸多优势，加之传统的防空手段“看不见”、“拦不住”、“打不起”，被视为战场“游戏规则改变者”，尤其在在俄乌冲突中更是得到了空前的应用。亦常见有各类民用无人机闯入机场、码头的报道。无论和平还是战争时期，反无人机成为要地防御亟待解决的全新课题。

采用传统防空武器拦截无人机成本极高，因此国内外正在大力研究新型的武器作为反无人机的手段，如无线电磁压制武器、激光武器、微波武器等。
1.	无线电磁压制武器；其基本原理为将一束大功率的无线电波对准拦截的无人机的区域。通过电磁压制设备干扰无人机的遥控链路以及卫星定位信号。对于民用无人机，当遥控链路中断时，通常会启动“返航”程序，卫星定位信号丢失则会启动“着陆”程序。这种压制手段对于民用无人机效果较好，且不会造成损毁。缺点是当前智能水平较高的无人机，可在无卫星定位、无遥控链路条件下自主飞行，此时电磁压制手段将将面临失效。
2.微波武器；与电磁压制相类似，但微波射束能量更高，可以破坏无人机的机载电路从而实现对无人机功能毁伤。微波武器的缺点是对于电磁屏蔽防护的无人机将会失效；另外激光武器在毁伤无人机的同时，其他落入其作用范围的电子系统也会受到损害，这使得它在人口和设备密集地区的使用受到限制。此外，操作人员的电磁安全以及高功耗也是需要考虑的问题。
3.激光武器；激光武器的作用原理是集中能量对无人机进行持续照射，从而产生热毁伤。据了解，国外大约使用或正在研制三百种激光系统和无人机反制设备。美国、以色列、中国、英国、法国和德国都拥有先进的激光武器系统。比较典型的如Raytheon公司的High Energy Laser Weapon System最大输出功率50千瓦，射程可达3公里；Lockheed Martin ADAM系统，最大输出功率10千瓦，射程可达2公里； Boeing公司的Compact Laser Weapon System，最大输出功率10千瓦，射程可达1.5公里；其价格均在百万美元以上。国产“寂静狩猎者”在沙特展开激光拦截器首次实战，取得首次在实战中击落无人机的世界纪录。但仍有诸多缺点难以克服：
1)	能源消耗大：激光武器需要大量的能源支持，增加了其使用成本，限制了使用范围。
2)	难以在短时间内进行连续射击；受制于储能、散热等问题，导致激光难以连续使用。
3)	受天气影响大：大雨或大雾等恶劣天气会影响其使用效果。
4)	对高速机动目标拦截效果差：击落一架无人机需要使激光束在目标上保持照射0.5-15秒。当无人机进行机动时，会使拦截变得相对困难。
总的来说，微波、激光武器的优点是可以以较低成本快速高效地摧毁无人机，但此类装备部署成本很高且需要大量的能源消耗。另外，它们需要提前预设阵地，类似于高射炮打飞机的思想，机动性差、所能够保护的区域有限，且预设阵地易被对方飞机躲避，另外对小型低空飞行的目标拦截效果不佳。
无人机的一个显著优势是低成本，可以大规模部署发动消耗战，所以还需要更低成本的反制手段。近年来也有一些国家开始尝试采用人工遥控无人机拦截无人机的方式，如2019年，英国皇家空军使用人工操纵的无人机成功拦截了一架试图进入英国伦敦希思罗机场的飞行禁区的无人机。2020年，美国海军使用人工操纵的无人机成功拦截了一架试图进入美国航母附近的海域的无人机。2021年，以色列国防军使用人工操纵的无人机成功拦截了数架试图从叙利亚进入以色列领空的无人机。
但人工遥控受制于操作人员的限制，也有诸多缺点难以克服：
1. 人工操纵无人机拦截无人机需要操作人员具有专业的技能和经验，且需要在高压和高风险的环境下操作，因此风险较高。
2. 在复杂的环境中，人工操纵无人机难以做出最优的决策，因此需要多次调整和优化，从而影响拦截效率。
3. 对于一些高速、机动路线难以预测的无人机，人工操纵无人机可能无法进行有效拦截。
4. 人工只能操纵单架飞机，无法应对大规模的无人机蜂群进攻。
随着飞行控制以及人工智能技术的成熟，使得构建全自主截击无人机成为可能为进一步降低成本，可在民用无人机上加装目标识别摄像机以及自主拦截控制器制。
基于自主控制技术的“以蜂制蜂”的反无人机思想，以及发展截击型无人机的设想，作为现有反无人机手段的有力补充。具体做法为，通过在低成本民用无人机基础上加装小型摄像头并通过人工智能算法识别标靶，利用先进的攻击导引飞控技术让低成本无人机变身为高速截击机，可直接撞击目标或近距离释放拦阻网进行拦截。在目标指挥引导方面，可采用远距地面引导“+”近距自动攻击的模式：
 
截击型无人机所具有的独特优势如下：
1. 成本低、免维护；硬件可选用速度较高的穿越机进行改装，软件核心在于智能算法，一经设计成功，后续可零成本复制。
2. 机动性好、保护面广；目前的多旋翼无人机航程可达10 km，在地面可灵活部署，在空中亦可机动拦截，可在更大范围内实施防御。
3. 主动出击、一机多用；通过修改识别算法，不仅可以拦截入侵无人机，也可主动出击攻击其他目标。
4. 可蜂群对抗、抗饱和打击；当遇到对方释放大量蜂群实施饱和攻击时，我方仍可以对应增加截击无人机数量实施蜂群对抗。

import json

ACCESS_TOKEN = ""

def get_post_id(timestamp: str, media_id: str, post_creation_dates: List[str]) -> str:
    date = datetime.strptime(timestamp, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z').strftime('%Y%m%d')
    post_id = f"{date}_{post_creation_dates.count(date)+1}"
    post_creation_dates.append(date)
    return post_id

def get_media_data(media_id: str) -> Tuple[str, str]:
    media_url = f"https://graph.instagram.com/v12.0/{media_id}?fields=media_type,media_url,timestamp&access_token={ACCESS_TOKEN}"
    response = requests.get(media_url)
    response.raise_for_status()  # Raise an exception if there's an error in the response
    media_data = response.json()
    return media_data["media_url"], media_data["timestamp"]

def get_username_and_picture(user_id: str) -> Union[Tuple[str, str], Tuple[None, None]]:
    user_url = f"https://graph.instagram.com/v12.0/{user_id}?fields=username,profile_picture_url&access_token={ACCESS_TOKEN}"
    response = requests.get(user_url)
    if response.status_code != 200:
        return None, None
    user_data = response.json()
    return user_data["username"], user_data["profile_picture_url"]

def get_total_counts(count_type: str, media_id: str) -> int:
    if count_type not in ["likes", "comments"]:
        return 0
    count_url = f"https://graph.instagram.com/v12.0/{media_id}?fields={count_type}.summary(true)&access_token={ACCESS_TOKEN}"
    response = requests.get(count_url)
    response.raise_for_status()  # Raise an exception if there's an error in the response
    summary_data = response.json()
    return summary_data["summary"]["total_count"]

def extract_data(response: requests.models.Response) -> pd.DataFrame:
    if response.text:
        response.raise_for_status()  # Raise an exception if there's an error in the response
        data = json.loads(response.text)["data"]
        return pd.DataFrame(data)
    return None

ACCESS_TOKEN = ""

def get_post_id(timestamp: str, media_id: str, post_creation_dates: List[str]) -> str:
    date = datetime.strptime(timestamp, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z').strftime('%Y%m%d')
    post_id = f"{date}_{post_creation_dates.count(date)+1}"
    post_creation_dates.append(date)
    return post_id

def get_media_data(media_id: str) -> Tuple[str, str]:
    media_url = f"https://graph.instagram.com/v12.0/{media_id}?fields=media_type,media_url,timestamp&access_token={ACCESS_TOKEN}"
    response = requests.get(media_url)
    response.raise_for_status() # Raise an exception if there's an error in the response
    media_data = response.json()
    return media_data["media_url"], media_data["timestamp"]

def get_username_and_picture(user_id: str) -> Union[Tuple[str, str], Tuple[None, None]]:
    user_url = f"https://graph.instagram.com/v12.0/{user_id}?fields=username,profile_picture_url&access_token={ACCESS_TOKEN}"
    response = requests.get(user_url)
    if response.status_code != 200:
        return None, None
    user_data = response.json()
    return user_data["username"], user_data["profile_picture_url"]

def get_total_counts(count_type: str, media_id: str) -> int:
    if count_type not in ["likes", "comments"]:
        return 0
    count_url = f"https://graph.instagram.com/v12.0/{media_id}?fields={count_type}.summary(true)&access_token={ACCESS_TOKEN}"
    response = requests.get(count_url)
    response.raise_for_status()  # Raise an exception if there's an error in the response
    summary_data = response.json()
    return summary_data["summary"]["total_count"]

def extract_data(response: requests.models.Response) -> pd.DataFrame:
    if not response.text:
        return None
    response.raise_for_status()  # Raise an exception if there's an error in the response
    data = json.loads(response.text)["data"]
    return pd.DataFrame(data)

# Install required libraries
install.packages(“forecast”)
install.packages(“nnet”)
install.packages(“anfis”)
install.packages(“fracdiff”)
install.packages(“MSwM”)

# Load libraries
library(forecast)
library(nnet)
library(anfis)
library(fracdiff)
library(MSwM)

Next, you can load the Brent Crude Oil dataset:

# Load Brent Crude Oil dataset (use your own dataset’s file path)
brent_data <- read.csv(“brent_crude_oil.csv”)

# Time series
prices <- ts(brent_data$Price, start = c(1970, 1), frequency = 12)

1. Develop an ANFIS model:

# Create training and testing sets
train_ANFIS <- window(prices, end = c(2010, 12))
test_ANFIS <- window(prices, start = c(2011, 1))

# Train the ANFIS model
ANFIS_model <- anfis(train_ANFIS, numMFs = 3, numEpochs = 50)

# Forecast with the ANFIS model
ANFIS_forecast <- forecast(ANFIS_model, h = length(test_ANFIS))

2. Develop an ARFIMA model:

# Estimate ARFIMA model
ARFIMA_model <- fracdiff(train_ANFIS)

# Forecast with the ARFIMA model
ARFIMA_forecast <- forecast(ARFIMA_model, h = length(test_ANFIS))

3. Develop a Markov-Switching model:

# Estimate Markov-Switching model
MSM_model <- msmFit(train_ANFIS, order = 1, sw = 2, model = “MarkovAR”)

# Forecast with the Markov-Switching model
MSM_forecast <- forecast(MSM_model, h = length(test_ANFIS))

Use Multi-objective Genetic Algorithm (MOGA) for weighting:

# Compute weights with MOGA
weights <- compute_weights_moga()

# Weighted hybrid forecast
weighted_forecast <- (weights[1] * ANFIS_forecast) +
(weights[2] * ARFIMA_forecast) +
(weights[3] * MSM_forecast)

Display the resulting forecasts:

# Plot forecasts
plot.forecast(weighted_forecast,
main = “Hybrid Model for Brent Crude Oil Prices”,
xlab = “Time”,
ylab = “Prices”)

目的：本研究旨在确定母亲使用HTP是否与后代过敏有关，并评估潜在的剂量-反应关系。
方法： 在这项基于网络的横断面调查中，我们于2021年7月至8月在日本调查了5688对产后妇女和婴儿(<3岁)。研究报告了婴儿哮喘、鼻炎、结膜炎或过敏性皮炎等的临床诊断。使用多水平Poisson回归，我们估算了按孕期对HPT吸烟类别交叉分类的婴儿过敏性疾病的患病率比值（PRs）和95％置信区间（CIs），并对潜在的协变量进行了调整，包括母亲吸烟和伴侣的吸烟状况。非吸烟者作为参考组。
结果：总计有2.4%的女性在怀孕期间吸食加热烟草产品（HTPs）。7.8%的婴儿出现了过敏。在怀孕期间吸食HTPs的母亲的后代中，过敏的患病率达到了15.2%（PR = 1.98，95％ CI 1.28-3.05）；这种关联在怀孕前三个月中最为明显，但在怀孕前和产后有所减弱。观察到剂量-反应的相关性，例如，在孕期每天吸食HTPs的剂量增加一个单位，将增加5％的过敏发生率。排除妊娠期吸烟者的亚组分析以及使用《儿童哮喘和过敏国际研究问卷》进行的敏感性分析显示了类似的模式。
结论：母亲在怀孕期间使用加热烟草制品与后代过敏有关。

Mask R-CNN model setup
Mask R-CNN relies on region proposal networks (RPNs) for identifying objects and is therefore a two-stage detector system. The three main steps (Figure 3) of the model are as follows: An RPN is used to decide where to search to reduce the computational requirements of the overall inference process; the region proposals are transformed by means of classification and creating of bounding boxes; and finally, the creation of segmentation masks, in which the algorithm takes positive regions of interest (ROIs) as input and creates 28 × 28 pixel floating-point value masks, which are then scaled up. For the inference process, the algorithm uses a multitask loss function: L = Lcls + Lbbox + Lmask (He et al., 2017). The developed model is based on a present implementation by Matterport, Inc. and released under an MIT licence, which is itself constructed based on the open-source libraries Keras and TensorFlow. In our study, we started by using weights obtained from the Microsoft Common Objects in COntext (MS COCO) dataset (Lin et al., 2014). However, a preliminary test showed unsatisfactory results caused by the specific domain-related problem of our dataset, that is, the occurrence of small objects. To counter this issue, we modified the anchor scale to values of 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128. We also modified the training anchors per image to values of 64 and 128, allowing for a large number of detected objects. We trained the model for 15 epochs using the stochastic gradient descent (SGD) method with a momentum of 0.9 and starting with a scheduled learning rate to speed up the training process. Furthermore, we compared the training results and training time for the adaptive gradient method with the dynamic bounds of the learning rate (AdaBound) (Luo et al., 2019) and the SGD optimization method. To reduce overfitting, we applied a weight decay since this parameter adds an L2 penalty to the cost, which can effectively lead to smaller model weights. The model runs under the deep learning development framework of TensorFlow and Keras, with an Nvidia 1080 GPU, an Intel® Core™ i7-8700k CPU and 16 GB memory. For model validation purposes, we divided the 200 training maps into a training subset (80% of the images) and a validation subset (20% of the images).

Job Posting:
Full Job Description
Gloo was founded as a mission-driven organization with the goal to release the passion in every person to Champion the growth of another so they can be all they were born to be.

Today, organizations of all sizes in the faith space use Gloo’s products to become more informed, better connected, and fully equipped to overcome their greatest challenges and achieve powerful outcomes, helping people progress through their personal growth journeys.

By building a common platform, we are creating a shared infrastructure that removes friction, promotes collaboration, and equips leaders with the right tools to galvanize personal growth and change lives. We are a fast-moving and passionate team that is looking for more talented professionals who are driven to make a positive impact.

The Opportunity:
As the newest member of our team you'll be helping us develop and perpetuate the Gloo brand through video storytelling. You’ll work closely with our corporate marketing team and cross-team stakeholders to bring the Gloo story and our platform utility to life for our core customers. Your experience conceptualizing and executing imaginative, future-forward, yet accessible video all using your own innovation and skillset is the secret to your success. You'll be telling stories and teaching viewers through video in both the tech and faith categories, so leveraging any tech and faith experience background will help you convey compelling stories.

The Team:
Our corporate marketing team is passionate about building a stable brand narrative and equipping our people and the ecosystem to tell Gloo’s story well. Our team members are drivers-moving swiftly into action in response to market and team needs, and are personable, innovative, and aspire to live out Gloo’s mission. The culture of our team is extremely important to us. We want you to be engaged in your projects, we want you to voice your ideas, and we want you to be proud of your accomplishments toward our shared company goals.
What You'll Be Doing:
Collaborating with the corporate marketing team and cross-team stakeholders to develop and execute video concepts that align with our brand messaging and business objectives
Edit and produce videos from raw footage, adding visual effects, sound design, and other elements needed to enhance the quality and impact of your videos
Develop, maintain, and manage production timelines-from pre-production to post production, delivering high-quality videos on-brand and on-time
Optimize video content for our variety of platforms - from the Gloo platform to social media, websites, mobile, events, zoom, and more
Stay up to date with industry trends and best practices, continually improving your skills in editing and up-leveling in areas like animation and sound design.
What We're Looking For:
A Bachelor's Degree (BA/BS) in Video Production, Film, Video Communications-commensurate experience may substitute for degree requirements
A minimum of 3 years of experience in an agency or video production organization
Expert proficiency in video editing software. Adobe Premier is Required
Experience in color grading is Required
Experience in motion graphics required, visual effects experience is a bonus!
Strong project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and deliver high-quality work within tight deadlines
Advanced level competency with Google Suite
An intense curiosity for how storytelling and educational content can serve the learning journey
A deep commitment to delighting your customers
Excellent communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively with cross functional teams and inputs from stakeholders
Ability to empathize with and successfully integrate constructive feedback
Ability to deliver meaning and intent in video, sound, writing and in your personal communication skills
A positive and energetic demeanor with the flexibility to work with ambiguity and emerging strategic explorations

Compensation: $55,000 - $70,000
Our Team Members Enjoy:
Compensation and bonus commensurate with experience
Plenty of time off to keep you balanced
Medical benefits with multiple plan offerings, HSA contribution, and Dental and Vision plans
A dynamic, talented team, dedicated to changing the world and building an incredible business
Onsite and virtual social events to keep us connected in our hybrid work environment
Beautiful office space in downtown Boulder on Pearl Street, steps from coffee shops and blocks from hiking trails
Applicants offered employment will be required to provide evidence of authorization to work in the United States, and will be required to work from a physical location within the United States in accordance with Gloo’s Remote Work Policies.

Introduction:  
Green Air (GA) is the second-largest airline in the United Kingdom. The airline, which has its headquarters in London, operates short, medium, and long-haul flights all over the world, with most of its flights departing from Heathrow Airport. GA was founded in 1980 to compete with National Airways, the then-state-owned airline. Beginning with a fleet of only 12 planes, the firm has grown to a fleet of 272 planes and travels to an impressive 191 destinations. In addition, GA was a founding member of the OneStar alliance in 1997, when it decided to work closely with four other worldwide airlines.
Historically, GA was seen as a highly appealing job that provided competitive pay and benefits, particularly when compared to other UK airlines. However, the growth of the business in the United Kingdom, as well as increased worldwide rivalry, has altered the nature of work and leadership strategy. Nonetheless, GA has a dedicated client base and is one of the most recognised UK companies.

Overview of HR issues:
Staff acted in 2005 when the contracts of 780 employees were not extended, and they were replaced with agency employees. Strike action was narrowly avoided in 2007 as the corporation reversed suggestions for pay freezes. Although these issues were formally settled, they appear to have had a long-term detrimental influence on employee morale and public perception. In 2018, a strike was called in reaction to poor working conditions for flight attendants. 
Flight attendants have always worked in a defined group or team, with the same contracts and awards. However, to be more flexible, several flights began using’ mixed fleet crews,' which meant that flight attendants were frequently working with different colleagues with different tenure and, as it turned out, separate employment contracts. Prior to 2015, employees were discovered to be on contracts with substantially better remuneration packages and shift arrangements. According to Unite the Union, some flight attendants employed after 2015 on newer contracts are on 'poverty wages,' with many sleeping in their cars between shifts and struggling to afford gasoline, housing fees, and food. Another concern has been the rigorous sick policy imposed on all flight attendants. Employees do not receive sick pay over the legal minimum. Because they cannot afford to take time off without compensation, flight attendants have been forced to work while unwell. The strike action launched in 2018 did not settle these concerns and is one of the longest ongoing contentious in recent times in the UK.
There is also a broader issue of low morale within the firm. Even though many of the conflicts have been resolved, employees continue to express unhappiness in the most recent annual employee survey. Sick leave policies, a lack of authority over working hours, and poor compensation are listed as major motivators. The leadership team is afraid that if they do not adjust, they would have employee shortages throughout the firm, reducing the number of flights that can be flown and eventually preventing them from recouping the losses of the previous years.
Another issue that the leadership team has noticed is the company's negative public impression. Many consumers have complained about extended delays, bad service, and a lack of customer assistance. While this isn't exactly a people management issue, it might be influenced in part by low morale. A negative public reputation is also likely to hinder their capacity to recruit persons to apply for GA jobs. They have never had problems recruiting people to the organisation and, as a result, do not have a solid recruitment plan.

Understanding Contemporary People Management:
According to the case study, In the past, especially in comparison to other UK airlines, GA was thought of as a very attractive company that offered excellent benefits and employment contracts. Nevertheless, prior to 2015, the employees were discovered to be engaged under contracts that offered significantly more favourable compensation and shift patterns. But nonetheless, the growth of the sector in the UK and the increase in global competitiveness have altered the nature of work and leadership tactics at GA.
However, there are three trade unions representing the employees at GA, the company might need to place a higher priority on effective communication and negotiation with these groups in order to preserve positive work relations. Stakeholder theory highlights that any group or person has the potential to have an impact on or be impacted by the company's goals (Thornock, 2016). Nonetheless, in the case of GA, Due to the dissatisfaction of one of the stakeholders which is the workforce, the company may have to negotiate with these unions on various employment issues, such as pay and working conditions, and there might be potential for confrontation between the unions and the management. 
Moreover, the ‘mixed fleet crews’ concept which was designed for extra flexibility faced a strike in 2018 due to unfair working contracts of flight attendants. Promoter region binding of Efg1 in diverse C. albicans clinical isolates.
There is extensive variation in the Efg1-responsive transcriptome among five C. albicans clinical isolates (13). These isolates represent five different clades and vary in ability to produce hyphae and biofilm (11, 13). Genome sequence analysis by Hirakawa et al. (11) indicated that the average genome-wide nucleotide diversity between any two isolates is ~0.37%. To increase confidence in gene expression differences among these isolates, we repeated triplicate RNA-seq assays for the five clinical isolates and efg1Δ/Δ derivatives after hyphal induction for 4 h in RPMI plus fetal bovine serum (RPMI+FBS) at 37°C (see Data Set S1 in the supplemental material, all genes). Analysis of the pooled data sets defined a set of 200 genes that presented significant Efg1-responsive RNA levels in all strains (>2-fold change between efg1Δ/Δ and WT; adjusted P < 0.05). We refer to these 200 genes as core Efg1-responsive genes (see Data Set S1, down and up data). Data set comparisons also identified 1,051 genes with Efg1-responsive RNA levels in only one or a few strains. We refer to these 1,051 genes as strain-limited Efg1-responsive genes (see Data Set S1, down and up); they represent natural variation in the Efg1 regulatory circuit. We sought to determine the basis for this natural variation.
One possible explanation for variation in Efg1-responsive genes is that Efg1 binds to distinct genomic loci in each strain. Differences in the binding spectrum would lead to different consequences for loss of Efg1. To identify loci to which Efg1 binds, we conducted chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (ChIP-seq) analysis of epitope-tagged Efg1-hemagglutinin (Efg1-HA) in each clinical isolate background. Samples were prepared after hyphal induction for 4 h in RPMI+FBS at 37°C. Efg1-HA presented consistent binding loci in all five clinical isolates (Fig. 1A; see also Data Set S2). Pearson's coefficients for 500-bp bins across the genome indicated that samples correlated strongly, with R values ranging from 0.85 to 1.00 (Fig. 1B). Computed Efg1 binding motifs for each clinical isolate showed that bound regions were associated with the canonical Efg1 binding motif, 5′-TGCAT-3′ (Fig. 1C). These results argue that Efg1-target binding is largely uniform among the five C. albicans isolates.

Efg1 core network of direct target genes.
We merged RNA-seq and ChIP-seq data to identify genes that were both differentially expressed in efg1Δ/Δ mutants and bound by Efg1. This analysis showed that 218 to 299 genes were regulated directly by Efg1 in each clinical isolate, and 110 genes were regulated directly by Efg1 in all five clinical isolates (Fig. 2; see also Table S1, Efg1 direct target gene ID and core direct Efg1 targets). The 110 genes, which we call core direct Efg1 targets, included 85 Efg1-activated genes and 25 Efg1-repressed genes (Fig. 3A). Core direct targets were enriched for functions related to adhesion and biofilm formation (adhesion of symbiont to host, P = 1.48e−06; single-species biofilm formation, P = 8.87e−06), in keeping with the observation that Efg1 is required for biofilm formation in all clinical isolates tested (13).
Examination of binding peaks surrounding specific genes indicated that Efg1 binding differences were not the cause of regulatory differences among strains. For example, core direct targets UME6, ALS3, and HGC1 were under positive control by Efg1 in all strains examined (Fig. 3B; see also Table S1, core direct Efg1 targets). The 5′ regions of these genes were uniformly bound by Efg1 (Fig. 1D). In contrast, AAF1, ALS7, and ECM331 were regulated by Efg1 in some strains and not in others (Fig. 3B; see also Table S1, differential expression). The 5′ regions of these genes were also uniformly bound by Efg1 (Fig. 1E). Therefore, differences in Efg1-responsive expression of genes cannot be explained by differences in Efg1-promoter region binding.

Strain-limited promoter response to Efg1.
To determine whether strain differences in Efg1-responsive gene expression reflect sequence differences in promoter or regulatory regions, we focused on the CHT2 gene. Its RNA levels were repressed by Efg1 in strain SC5314 but activated slightly by Efg1 in strain P75010 (see Table S1, differential expression). To assay activity of the same promoter sequence in both strains, we fused a 1,743-bp fragment from the SC5314 CHT2 5′ region to a lacZ reporter gene and introduced the construct into each wild type (WT) and its derived efg1Δ/Δ mutant (Fig. 4A and B). Measurement of β-galactosidase indicated that the reporter gene was repressed by Efg1 in strain SC5314 and unaffected by Efg1 in strain P75010 (Fig. 4C). These assays were conducted after hyphal induction for 24 h in RPMI+FBS at 37°C, allowing time for β-galactosidase to accumulate. Repression required the CHT2 promoter region (Fig. 4C). These results showed that identical C. albicans promoter sequences respond differently to Efg1 in these two strain backgrounds.

Sculpting of Efg1 transcriptional target space by partner TFs.
To explore the basis for strain variation in Efg1-responsive gene expression, we focused on the two strains SC5314 and P75010. SC5314 is the type strain for C. albicans and was isolated from a patient with a generalized Candida infection (http://www.candidagenome.org/Strains.shtml). P75010 is a bloodstream isolate (14). We hypothesized that differences in expression or activity of TFs that are functionally related to Efg1 may explain natural variation in the Efg1 regulatory response (Fig. 5A). TF genes that were expressed at higher levels in SC5314 than in P75010 (Fig. 5B; see also Table S2) included WOR1 (regulator of white-opaque switching), ZFU2 (regulator of cell adherence), ADR1 (regulator of carbon metabolism), and TEC1 and BRG1 (regulators of biofilm and hyphal formation). We increased dosages of individual TF genes in P75010 to test whether their increased expression altered Efg1-responsive gene expression.
Each TF gene, PCR-amplified from strain P75010, was integrated into the genome in P75010 EFG1+/+ and efg1Δ/Δ strains. Integration was targeted to the MDR1 locus. (An mdr1Δ/Δ mutation lacking an inserted TF gene did not alter gene regulation in our assays [Fig. 5C, P75010+empty; see also Table S3, ectopic strains efg1 versus EFG1.]) Gene expression was assayed after hyphal induction for 4 h in RPMI+FBS at 37°C (Fig. 5C; see also Table S3). Dosage increases yielded 2- to 10-fold increased TF gene expression (see Table S3, WOR1-BRG1-TEC1 relationship). Increased dosage of the known biofilm and hyphal regulatory gene BRG1 in strain P75010 caused Efg1-responsive regulation of ECM331, HGT1, ECE1, and HYR1 to resemble more closely that in strain SC5314. Increased dosage of the biofilm and hyphal regulatory gene TEC1 had similar effects on ECE1 and HYR1. Increased dosage of ZFU2 and ADR1 had little effect (see Table S3, ADR1-ZFU2 data). Increased dosage of WOR1 in P75010 also caused Efg1-responsive regulation to resemble that in SC5314 (Fig. 5C; see also Table S3, ectopic strains efg1 versus EFG1). For example, ECM331 and HYR1 were under negative control by Efg1 in P75010 but under positive control in SC5314 and the increased-dosage strain, P75010+WOR1. Conversely, CHT2 was under positive control by Efg1 in P75010 but under negative control in SC5314 and P75010+WOR1. Although the range of genes assayed was limited, increased dosage of WOR1, BRG1, or TEC1 in strain P75010 caused features of Efg1-dependent gene regulation to resemble those in strain SC5314.
To determine whether the gene expression effects of increased TF gene dosage depend upon Efg1, we compared gene dosage impact in P75010 EFG1+/+ and efg1Δ/Δ backgrounds (Fig. 6; see also Table S3, ectopic strains versus empty). Increased BRG1 dosage had significant effects on 10 genes (adjusted P < 0.05; excluding BRG1 itself) in the EFG1+/+ background, and those effects were abolished in the efg1Δ/Δ background. Therefore, effects of increased BRG1 dosage on these genes depend upon Efg1. Increased TEC1 dosage had significant effects on 15 genes (excluding TEC1) in an EFG1+/+ background, and only some of those effects were abolished in an efg1Δ/Δ background. Therefore, effects of increased TEC1 dosage are partially independent of Efg1. Increased WOR1 dosage had significant effects on 10 genes (excluding WOR1) in the EFG1+/+ background, and those effects were abolished in the efg1Δ/Δ background. Therefore, effects of increased WOR1 dosage on these genes depend upon Efg1.

Positive control of biofilm formation by Wor1 in P75010.
We hypothesized that the gene expression impact of increased WOR1, BRG1, or TEC1 dosage may translate into biological phenotype. Strain SC5314 is a stronger biofilm former than P75010 (13). We observed that increased dosage of WOR1, BRG1, or TEC1 in P75010 drove greater biofilm production (Fig. 7A), based upon either depth or volume (Fig. 7C). We concluded that differences in WOR1, BRG1, or TEC1 expression levels between strains can account for differences in both biofilm formation ability and Efg1-responsive gene expression.
The Efg1-Wor1 physical interaction in vitro depends upon the Wor1 PrLD, a region that is required for Wor1 function in the white-opaque switch (10). We hypothesized that the Efg1-Wor1 functional interaction in gene expression and biofilm formation may also be PrLD dependent. In our increased dosage assay, PrLD-disrupted WOR1 mutants (DE-to-A or YF-to-S) had much less impact than wild-type WOR1 in Efg1-responsive regulation of ECM331, HGT1, ECE1, CHT2, or HYR1 (Fig. 5D; see also Table S3, ectopic strains efg1 versus EFG1) or biofilm production (Fig. 7B and C). Therefore, integrity of the Wor1 PrLD is required for Wor1 to impact both Efg1-responsive gene expression and biofilm formation.
If Wor1 promotes biofilm formation through interaction with Efg1, then an efg1Δ/Δ mutation should abrogate the stimulation of biofilm formation by increased WOR1 dosage. We observed that an efg1Δ/Δ mutation blocked biofilm formation in strain P75010 regardless of increased WOR1 dosage (see Fig. S1). Therefore, the impact of WOR1 dosage on biofilm formation, like its impact on Efg1-responsive gene expression, depends upon Efg1.
In order to understand the scope of the impact of WOR1 gene expression, we conducted RNA-seq analysis on P75010+empty vector and P75010+WOR1 strains. Increased WOR1 dosage altered expression of 396 genes (293 upregulated, 103 downregulated; fold change, >2; adjusted P < 0.05 [see Data Set S3]). Upregulated genes were enriched for adhesion functions and included many genes associated with biofilm or hyphal growth (ALS1, HYR1, SAP4-SAP5-SAP6, and UME6). The 396 genes with significantly altered expression were enriched for Efg1-bound genes (P < 10−5, Fisher’s exact test [see Fig. S1]). EFG1 RNA levels were not significantly affected (see Data Set S3). Therefore, increased WOR1 dosage has a narrow effect on gene expression under these growth conditions. Based on WOR1 dosage effects on gene expression and biofilm formation, our findings support the model that Wor1 acts in part through Efg1 to modulate gene expression.

THE INFLUENCE OF THE NATURAL SCIENCES ON THE SOCIAL SCIENCES

IN THE COURSE of its slow development in the eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries the study of economic and social phenomena was guided in the choice of its methods in the main by the nature of the problems it had to face. It gradually developed a technique appropriate to these problems without much reflection on the character of the methods or on their relation to that of other disciplines of knowledge. Students of political economy could describe it alternatively as a branch of science or of moral or social philosophy without the least qualms whether their subject was scientific or philosophical. The term "science" had not yet assumed the special narrow meaning it has today, nor was there any distinction made which singled out the physical or natural sciences and attributed to them a special dignity. Those who devoted themselves to those fields indeed readily chose the designation of philosophy when they were concerned with the more general aspects of their problems,3 and occasionally we even find "natural philosophy" contrasted with "moral science."
During the first half of the nineteenth century a new attitude made
its appearance. The term science came more and more to be confined
to the physical and biological disciplines which at the same time
began to claim for themselves a special rigorousness and certainty
which distinguished them from all others. Their success was such that
they soon came to exercise an extraordinary fascination on those
working in other fields, who rapidly began to imitate their teaching
and vocabulary. Thus the tyranny commenced which the methods
and technique of the Sciences 4 in the narrow sense of the term have
ever since exercised over the other subjects. These became increasingly concerned to vindicate their equal status by showing that their
methods were the same as those of their brilliantly successful sisters
rather than by adapting their methods more and more to their own
particular problems. And, although in the hundred and twenty years
or so, during which this ambition to imitate Science in its methods
rather than its spirit has now dominated social studies, it has con-
tributed scarcely anything to our understanding of social phenomena,
not only does it continue to confuse and discredit the work of the
social disciplines, but demands for further attempts in this direction
are still presented to us as the latest revolutionary innovations which,
if adopted, will secure rapid undreamed of progress.
Let it be said at once, however, that those who were loudest in
these demands were rarely themselves men who had noticeably enriched our knowledge of the Sciences. From Francis Bacon, the Lord
Chancellor, who will forever remain the prototype of the "demagogue of science," as he has justly been called, to Auguste Comte
and the "physicalists" of our own day, the claims for the exclusive
virtues of the specific methods employed by the natural sciences were
mostly advanced by men whose right to speak on behalf of the scientists were not above suspicion, and who indeed in many cases had
shown in the Sciences themselves as much bigoted prejudice as in
their attitude to other subjects. Just as Francis Bacon opposed Copernican Astronomy, and as Comte taught that any too minute investigation of the phenomena by such instruments as the microscope,
was harmful and should be suppressed by the spiritual power of the
positive society, because it tended to upset the laws of positive science, so this dogmatic attitude has so often misled men of this type
in their own field that there should have been little reason to pay too
much deference to their views about problems still more distant from
the fields from which they derived their inspiration.
There is yet another qualification which the reader ought to keep
in mind throughout the following discussion. The methods which scientists or men fascinated by the natural sciences have so often tried
to force upon the social sciences were not always necessarily those
which the scientists in fact followed in their own field, but rather
those which they believed that they employed. This is not necessarily
the same thing. The scientist reflecting and theorizing about his procedure is not always a reliable guide. The views about the character
of the method of Science have undergone various fashions during the
last few generations, while we must assume that the methods actually
followed have remained essentially the same. But since it was what
scientists believed that they did, and even the views which they had
held some time before, which have influenced the social sciences, the
following comments on the methods of the natural sciences also do
not necessarily claim to be a true account of what the scientists in
fact do, but an account of the views on the nature of scientific method
which were dominant in recent times.
The history of this influence, the channels through which it operated, and the direction in which it affected social developments,
will occupy us throughout the series of historical studies to which the
present essay is designed to serve as an introduction. Before we trace
the historical course of this influence and its effects, we shall here
attempt to describe its general characteristics and the nature of the
problems to which the unwarranted and unfortunate extensions
of the habits of thought of the physical and biological sciences have
given rise. There are certain typical elements of this attitude which
we shall meet again and again and whose prima facie plausibility
makes it necessary to examine them with some care. While in the
particular historical instances it is not always possible to show how
these characteristic views are connected with or derived from the
habits of thought of the scientists, this is easier in a systematic
survey.
It need scarcely be emphasized that nothing we shall have to say
is aimed against the methods of Science in their proper sphere or is
intended to throw the slightest doubt on their value. But to preclude
any misunderstanding on this point we shall, wherever we are concerned, not with the general spirit of disinterested inquiry but with
slavish imitation of the method and language of Science, speak of
"scientism" or the "scientistic" prejudice. Although these terms are
not completely unknown in English, they are actually borrowed
from the French, where in recent years they have come to be
generally used in very much the same sense in which they will be
used here. It should be noted that, in the sense in which we shall
use these terms, they describe, of course, an attitude which is decidedly unscientific in the true sense of the word, since it involves
a mechanical and uncritical application of habits of thought to fields
different from those in which they have been formed. The scientistic
as distinguished from the scientific view is not an unprejudiced
but a very prejudiced approach which, before it has considered its
subject, claims to know what is the most appropriate way of investigating it.
It would be convenient if a similar term were available to describe
the characteristic mental attitude of the engineer which, although
in many respects closely related to scientism, is yet distinct from it
but which we intend to consider here in connection with the latter.
No single word of equal expressiveness suggests itself, however, and
we shall have to be content to describe this second element so
characteristic of 19th and 20th century thought as the "engineering
type of mind."

crea flashcard domanda-risposta, parola-definizione basandoti su: APITOLO 3 PERSONE, MOTIVAZIONI E COMPETENZE
I prospetti informativi delle aziende che entrano in borsa hanno un paragrafo dedicato
alle risorse umane, quindi questo interessa agli arresti finanziari e anche gli investitori.
Sono informazioni che orientano il mercato ma anche le decisioni del management.
L'insieme delle persone che costituiscono organico può essere considerato sotto diverse prospettive: 
1 riguarda le caratteristiche direttamente percepibili, si tratta di caratteristiche demografiche ma anche di comportamenti lavorativi.
2. classifica le informazioni rispetto alla posizione o ruolo ricoperti e introduce elementi di valutazione soggettivi come l'adeguatezza e il commitment.
3. si considera la persona in sé.

3.1 La motivazione
È complesso far collaborare in un'azienda persone di diverse generazioni.
Le loro aspettative sono diverse e si evolvono nel corso del tempo.
Per capire quali sono le spinte che guidano i comportamenti dei lavoratori e alimentano la loro volontà di contribuire, ci riferiamo alle ricerche sulle motivazioni.

La motivazione è il processo dinamico che finalizza l'attività di una persona verso
un obiettivo.
Le sue caratteristiche sono
È uno strumento interiore dell'individuo.
Ha in sé un elemento di scelta e di spinta al compimento di azioni finalizzate.
È un concetto composito.
Può modificarsi nel tempo.
Il profilo motivazionale di ciascuna persona è unico.

I modelli motivazionali possono essere analizzati secondo due criteri.
In base ai contenuti, cioè le ragioni che spingono ad adottare un comportamento.
In base al processo, cioè alla dinamica attraverso cui si passa da bisogni a una linea di condotta.

Comunque, possiamo considerare la relazione tra bisogni individuali e ricompense organizzative stimando il peso che le persone assegnano a riconoscimenti per il lavoro svolto.
La conoscenza del sistema motivazionale è essenziale per scegliere strumenti di incentivazione, ma anche per creare migliori condizioni di valorizzazione della specificità di ciascuno.

I contenuti della motivazione: il modello di Maslow
Secondo Maslow, il contenuto delle motivazioni all'azione si origina dall'insoddisfazione.
il bisogno è una carenza di oggetto desiderato.
I bisogni si distinguono in funzione dell'oggetto cui sono rivolti:

I bisogni fisiologici sono le necessità fondamentali, la premessa di ogni altro desiderio.
I bisogni di sicurezza,
i bisogni di appartenenza sono il desiderio di crearsi una rete relazionale
in cui si è riconosciuti ed apprezzati.
I bisogni di stima sono i bisogni di autostima e di eterostima (cioè il desiderio di essere riconosciuti dagli altri per il proprio lavoro)
i bisogni di autorealizzazione.
I primi due ordini di bisogni sono chiamati primari, i secondi tre sono chiamati superiori.
I bisogni formano una gerarchia: una persona non sarà motivata da un bisogno che ha ciò trovato a soddisfazione, coloro che hanno soddisfatto i bisogni primari sentono i bisogni di realizzarsi e non saranno soddisfatti nel ricevere sempre lo stesso tipo di riconoscimento.

Questa teoria è stata criticata perché l'ordine e l'intensità con cui i bisogni si manifestano non sono uguali per tutti.
i bisogni superiori presentano un'elevata variabilità tra individui.
Essi potrebbero modificarsi in funzione del momento e delle circostanze.

In fine, la scala di Maslow non spiegherebbe situazioni come quella del Starving Artist, cioè chi è disposto a sacrificare i propri bisogni primari pur di autorealizzarsi.

Tra potere e affiliazione: il contributo di McClelland
 secondo lui ci sono tre ordini di bisogni.
I contenuti delle motivazioni che spingono le persone all'azione sono:
il successo, achievement need e il bisogno di affermarsi tramite lo sforzo individuale.
Le persone con un forte desiderio di successo, 
tendono a evitare situazioni ad alto rischio ma anche a basso rischio.
Preferiscono lavorare da soli con persone simili.
Hanno bisogno di feedback frequenti.
Tendono a prendersi la responsabilità individuale per la riuscita di un compito.

il potere, power need, il bisogno di possedere uno status riconosciuto ed essere in grado di influenzare gli altri, la fonte del desiderio può essere personale o istituzionale. Queste persone sono attratte da posizioni gerarchicamente elevate, una prevalenza squilibrata  di questo bisogno può condurre all'autoritarismo.

L'affiliazione, affiliation need, è il bisogno di stabilire e mantenere o ristinare un rapporto personale con gli altri. Chi ha questo bisogno desidera lavorare in gruppi nei quali si senta accettato e tende a instaurare legami confidenziali anche sul lavoro, il prevalere di questo bisogno può generare un atteggiamento di dipendenza.
PAG 69-75
Ogni persona possiede tutti questi bisogni, ma solo uno è prevalente in un dato momento, agisce sulla scelta del comportamento.

Mcclelland afferma che i bisogni non sono statici nel tempo.

Nella gestione delle risorse umane, è molto importante la distinzione tra high achiever e low achiever.
Gli high achievers hanno un'alta autonomia, capacità di gestire uomini e risorse per raggiungere l'obiettivo. potrebbero essere spinti a comportamenti dannosi per loro stessi,
come una continua percezione di adeguatezza, ma anche per i loro colleghi, come una scala tendenza a delegare.
I low achievers hanno bassa autostima e tendono a attribuire i loro successi a cause diverse dalle proprie capacità.

Alla ricerca di soddisfazione: lo studio di Herzberg

spostiamo l'attenzione a fattori dell'organizzazione che generano soddisfazione.
Herzberg arriva due importanti conclusioni:
Uno, soddisfazione e insoddisfazione sul lavoro non sono agli estremi opposti, ma sono distinte (Il contrario della insoddisfazione è l'assenza di soddisfazione) e sono alimentate da gruppi diversi di fattori.
Due, gli elementi che generano insoddisfazione sono strettamente legati al contesto organizzativo, invece quelli che generano soddisfazione riguardano il contenuto del lavoro.
I primi sono fattori igienici, 
i secondi fattori motivanti.


Il processo motivazionale: la teoria delle aspettative di Vroom.
Ricerca su un meccanismo attraverso cui le istanze motivazionali influiscono sulle azioni.
Secondo Vroom, l'assunto di base è che le persone utilizzano i loro sforzi verso comportamenti e azioni che portano a ricompense desiderabili.

Abbiamo la teoria delle aspettative, che è una teoria sulle decisioni.
Prima di fare uno sforzo lavorativo si valuta quanto la ricompensa vale e quali comportamenti si dovrà attuare per ottenerla.

Il processo motivazionale che spinge ad agire:
Si esamina la valenza della ricompensa. Ci sono motivi che possono rendere la ricompensa attraente, indifferente o non desiderabile.
Al termine di questa valutazione si decide il livello di sforzo.
Questo è condizionato anche da una valutazione del modo in cui il maggior sforzo si tradurrà nel risultato atteso.
Questa si chiama aspettativa ed è condizionata da fattori esogeni, organizzativi ed individuali.
L'aspettativa è una valutazione di probabilità che varia da 0, se si ritiene che nonostante gli sforzi non si raggiungerà la prestazione attesa e 1 quando si è certi.
Adesso rimane un ultimo elemento da considerare, la strumentalità.
Questo elemento è relativo al legame tra il risultato ottenuto e la ricompensa.
Permangono elementi di incertezza individuali e organizzativi che condizionano lo sforzo.
Il livello di strumentalità va da 0 quando non c'era una relazione chiara tra obiettivo e ricompensa a più 1 (Lavoratore certo che otterrà il premio).
A questo punto ha tutti gli elementi per scegliere tra le alternative di comportamento.
Sceglie Quelle con la forza motivazionale più elevata (Forza motivazionale uguale, valenza per l'aspettativa per strumentalità)

La soddisfazione non dipende solo dalle entità delle ricompense ma anche dalla percezione secondo cui queste vengono somministrate.
Qua abbiamo la distinzione fondamentale tra 
l'equità procedurale: riguarda quanto l'individuo ritiene giusto il processo attraverso cui vengono assegnate le ricompense a fronte dei contributi individuali.
e l'equità distributiva: è relativa all'entità delle ricompense assegnate che potrebbero non essere valutate come giuste rispetto a uno standard di riferimento.

Quantificare una popolazione aziendale in termini di motivazioni è fondamentale per segmentare le politiche e i sistemi operativi usati e dotare gli interventi in modo da aumentare la soddisfazione di ciascuno.

请写出一篇本章小结，根据以下内容：第2章　关键技术介绍

本章对线上商城系统使用的技术进行详细的介绍，

2.1 信息加密算法——MD5

MD5是一种广泛应用于数据加密的密码散列函数，其全称是"Message-Digest Algorithm 5"，即信息摘要算法。它可以生成一个128位（16字节）的输出，通常以32位十六进制的方式表示。MD5算法是一种不可逆的加密技术，即通过对明文进行一系列迭代的算法操作，最终生成一个摘要，而无法逆向还原原始数据。
MD5算法的安全性和可靠性已经受到了广泛的认可和应用。不同于SHA-1或SHA-2算法，MD5算法主要特点是速度更快，摘要也更短，但是它的易破解性也更高。因此，在一些非安全性较高的应用场景中，MD5算法还是具有一定的实用价值。
在实际应用中，MD5算法被广泛应用于密码加密和一些数字签名验证等方面，例如在密码学安全性较弱的应用中，网站可以使用MD5算法对用户密码进行加密存储，以增强密码的安全性；此外，在一些数据传输应用中，MD5算法也通常被用于验证数据的完整性，以确定是否存在数据被篡改或损坏的情况。

2.2 相关技术概述

2.2.1 SSM框架
SSM框架是目前比较流行的Java Web开发框架，它由Spring、Spring MVC和MyBatis这三个独立的框架整合而成，因而得名SSM。SSM框架集成了Spring的依赖注入、AOP等特性，同时也集成了Spring MVC的MVC框架和MyBatis框架的ORM特性，因此使得Java Web开发更加方便和高效。
Spring框架是一个轻量级的Java开发框架，它提供了丰富的容器和管理组件，能够最大限度的帮助开发者减少代码量，提高开发效率；Spring MVC是一种基于Java的Web MVC框架，可以进行轻松的构建Web应用程序并维护这些应用程序的不同页面；而MyBatis框架则能够将Java对象映射到数据库中的记录。由此，SSM框架在实现Java Web开发的全栈解决方案时，既可以完成业务逻辑、数据控制层的开发，同时又能快速实现在页面交互方面的开发，显得特别的灵活和高效。
具体来说，SSM框架有以下几个方面的特点和优势：
1.灵活的设计模式
SSM框架的组成模块都采用了成熟和先进的设计模式，因此能够快速响应业务逻辑的变化，从而保证了开发的灵活性。
2.高效的依赖注入
Spring框架自身就强大的依赖注入能力，加上MyBatis框架的智能型ORM机制，也进一步增强了对数据的操纵。
3. 简化了DAO层的编写
MyBatis框架的出现，在很大程度上简化了开发人员DAO层的编写。MyBatis有着强大的SQL查询功能，支持更加复杂的SQL查询，并能够封装所有的SQL查询，简化了DAO层的开发。
4. MVC的分层结构
Spring MVC框架采用了分层的MVC结构，将Web层、数据控制层和业务层进行了很好的解耦，代码的可读性和可维护性得到了较大的提高。
5. 集成各种开源库
Spring MVC和MyBatis都吸收集成了大量优秀的第三方开源库，如MyBatis-Spring、Spring-Data-JPA、MyBatis-Plus等，丰富了框架的功能模块。
总而言之，SSM框架是一种成熟、强大和高效的Java Web开发框架，它整合了Spring、Spring MVC和MyBatis三个流行的框架，具备优雅、灵活、高效等特点，能够极大地提升开发效率，降低了开发人员的工作量。近年来，随着JavaEE的流行，SSM框架在Java Web开发领域中的优势和应用越来越受到广泛的认可和应用。
2.2.2 Vue框架
Vue是一种流行的前端框架，可用于构建单页面和复杂的Web应用程序。Vue提供了一种简单而强大的开发方式，通过组合成组件实现复杂的UI交互和逻辑。
Vue具有以下特点：
1. 渐进式框架：Vue可以逐步采用，只需要将其添加到现有Web应用程序中，不需要重写整个项目。
2. 组件化开发：Vue使用组件来构建应用程序。组件是可重用的代码块，具有自己的状态和行为，可以嵌套在其他组件中。
3. 虚拟DOM：Vue使用虚拟DOM来实现高效的渲染。当组件更新时，Vue会计算出需要更新的最小化DOM操作，并进行最小化的DOM更新。
4. 响应式数据绑定：Vue使用数据绑定来处理模板中的数据和UI。当数据更改时，所有依赖于该数据的组件都会自动更新。
5. 非常简单的API：Vue提供简单，易于理解的API，允许快速构建应用程序，无需复杂的配置文件。
Vue具有强大的插件系统，可以轻松地添加第三方插件来扩展其功能。它还支持CLI工具，允许快速创建新项目和组件。它在开发者社区中非常流行，有大量的文档，示例和库。
总的来说，Vue是一个功能强大且易于使用的前端框架，适用于各种应用程序的开发。它的生态系统非常丰富，有许多优秀的库和组件，便于扩展和构建Vue应用程序，使其成为开发者和企业的理想选择。
2.2.3 Redis
在开发过程中，通常使用基于关系型模型的数据库管理系统，例如MySQL和Oracle等。这些数据库的增删查改操作可以通过Web提供的数据库驱动来连接实现。关系数据库中的数据通常保存在硬盘中，数据库部署在硬件上。当只使用关系型数据库高效地存储数据时，通常需要优化SQL语句来提高网站的处理速度。但这仍然难以应对大量请求和访问，这对数据库的性能造成极大压力，导致响应能力降低。为了缓解这种压力，需要使用缓存技术，减少对数据库的频繁访问和更新操作[11]。这样可以降低数据库的压力，以提高应用程序的性能。常见的缓存技术包括内存缓存和分布式缓存，前者常用于单个应用程序，而后者可用于多个应用程序之间共享数据。通过有效使用缓存技术，可以充分利用系统资源，提高数据库的性能和整体响应能力。
本项目使用了Redis缓存技术。Redis是一个开源的内存数据结构存储系统，可用作数据库、缓存和消息代理。它具有快速、稳定和高度可扩展的特性，成为流行的数据存储解决方案之一。Redis的特点如下：
1. 高速存储和访问：Redis将键值对存储在内存中，因此可以快速读取和写入数据。此外，Redis还支持持久化到磁盘，以便在重新启动时重用数据。
2. 多种数据结构：Redis支持多种数据结构，如字符串、哈希、列表、集合和有序集合。这些数据结构允许Redis执行各种复杂的数据操作，例如搜索、排序和分组。
3. 高度可扩展性：Redis通过分区、复制和集群等分布式技术来实现高度可扩展性。这意味着Redis可以处理大量的数据，并支持水平扩展。
4. 支持多种编程语言：Redis支持多种编程语言，如Java、Python、C#、Node.js等。这意味着开发人员可以在他们熟悉的编程环境中使用Redis。
5. 支持多种应用场景：Redis可以作为缓存、消息队列、计数器、排行榜、实时统计和分布式锁等多种应用场景。
2.2.4 Mysql数据库
MySQL是一个开源的关系数据库管理系统，被广泛用于Web应用程序开发。MySQL具有稳定的性能、兼容性好和易于使用的特点，被广泛认为是最流行的关系数据库之一。
MySQL具有以下优点：
1. 可靠稳定的性能：MySQL的架构和存储引擎优化了读写性能，并且在负载高的情况下依然能够保持稳定。
2. 开源免费：MySQL是一个开源平台，完全免费使用。这使得它成为世界各地开发者的首选，尤其是在一些开源项目中。
3. 实用的兼容性：MySQL提供了跨平台的兼容性，支持多种操作系统，包括Windows和Linux等。
4. 简单易用的管理和监控：MySQL提供了丰富的工具和应用程序来管理和监控数据库，从而简化了管理和运营的过程。
5. 大社区和完善文档：MySQL拥有庞大的社区和完善的文档资源，可以快速解决问题和学习新特性。
除此之外，MySQL还具有高度可靠的复制和备份，支持多种存储引擎以及良好的安全性等特性，这些特性使得MySQL成为非常适合在生产环境中使用的数据库。MySQL已经被广泛运用于一个大量的系统中，尤其是在大型数据驱动系统中，如Facebook、Twitter、阿里巴巴等。因为MySQL的性能、兼容性和可靠性，以及其灵活的体系结构，使得它非常适合在不同角色的系统中使用，如Web应用程序后端、商业中间件和云计算环境等。

Crea flashcards domanda-risposta, parola-definizione: Dalle motivazioni alle competenze. 
Le motivazioni possono essere ricomprese nelle competenze.
Il termine competenza ha un doppio significato:
designa il diritto o il dovere di conoscere una certa situazione e di occuparsene.
la capacità di occuparsene in maniera professionalmente adeguata.

Possiamo distinguere tra 
competenze professionali, che sono abilità tecniche e contestualizzate, soggette a obsolescenza che si usurano col passare del tempo se non vengono aggiornato o riconvertite,
e tra competenze comportamentali più trasversali e suscettibili di essere asportate da una situazione o un'altra. Sono destinate a permanere e ad accentuare nel tempo le loro caratteristiche.

Il movimento delle competenze ha preso l'avvio dagli studi di McClelland, che rivelano come gli strumenti usati per predire le performance lavorative basate su test e risultati scolastici erano inaffidabili.
Questi risultati lo spinsero a mettere a punto uno strumento diverso, basato sul confronto tra gruppi di persone con elevate prestazioni.
SI isolavano schemi cognitivi e comportamenti operativi causalmente correlati al successo lavorativo e definiti competenze.

McClelland e Daily useranno una tecnica definita BEI, Behavioral Event Interview, che si basa sulla ricostruzione e interpretazione analitica di situazioni di lavoro portate a termine con successo e di altre finite con insuccesso.

PAG 75-81
Le competenze professionali 
sono conoscenza, abilità, sapere, atteggiamenti, qualità, esperienza.

Di ogni elemento si può valutare il grado di padronanza, di assimilazione, di approfondimento.

L'acquisizione si ha attraverso
 un processo formativo-scolastico aziendale 
o attraverso l'esperienza che può essere strutturata e finalizzata alla loro costruzione come un tirocinio oppure non strutturato.

Anche i processi di socializzazione e di acculturazione nella comunità di appartenenza possono essere fonte di competenze professionali.

Le competenze di questo tipo comprendono:
1. le conoscenze che permettono di capire come funziona un certo processo o una certa attività.
Tipicamente si acquisiscono attraverso la formazione e sono conoscenze in iniziative, sapere che, e conoscenze procedurali, sapere come.

2. il sapere empirico. Consiste in  routine che vengono espresse attraverso la pratica e sono difficilmente trasmissibili.
Tipicamente si acquisiscono con l'esperienza.

3. le metaconoscenze. Sono conoscenze sulle proprie conoscenze e consentono la crescita e lo sviluppo nella successione delle diverse esperienze e dei cambiamenti di contesto.

Si possono avere forme di certificazione delle competenze con procedure interne aziendali o di enti certificatori.
In Italia abbiamo l'associazione italiana dei direttori del personale.

A trarne vantaggi possono essere i processi di crescita dei lavoratori nell'azienda, le proposte normative delle scuole e le scelte di sviluppo professionale dei giovani.

Le competenze comportamentali.
Boyatzis definisce la competenza come una caratteristica intrinseca causalmente correlata a una prestazione efficace.

Distingue in due tipi di competenze.
Competenze di soglia, sono minime e essenziali.
Competenze distintive o discriminanti, che creano differenze nella prestazione e le portano a un livello superiore.

Modalità di manifestazione delle competenze.
1. Motivazione: sono schemi mentali, bisogni che orientano e inducono le azioni dell'individuo.

2. Tratti: caratteristiche fisiche e psichiche.
E' una generale disposizione a comportarsi o a reagire in un certo modo.

3. Idea di sé: atteggiamenti, valori adottati, per esempio valore assegnato all'autonomia sul proprio lavoro.

4. Conoscenze: informazioni, teorie, concetti su un determinato campo disciplinare.
O meglio, un insieme dei saperi specifici e generali per realizzare una certa attività.

5. Skill: capacità di mettere in atto un sistema o una sequenza dei comportamenti funzionanti, funzionalmente coerenti con l'obiettivo di prestazione desiderato.

Le motivazioni e i tratti sono difficili da valutare e sviluppare.
La conoscenza e le skill sono più visibili e modificabili con la formazione e l'esperienza.

L’Idea di sé, è in una posizione intermedia, perché i valori possono essere cambiati dal confronto con gli altri e dalla pressione sociale.

Le competenze individuali sono un potenziale: alcune conoscenze e abilità possono dare origine a prestazioni elevate in un'azienda o nulle in un'altra. Il loro valore, in un contesto, dipende dal loro ruolo nei processi che determina la performance aziendale.

Manager e imprenditori: competenza e passione.
Accanto all'approccio basato sulle competenze comportamentali si sono sviluppati modelli che hanno tentato di capire le doti fondamentali di manager e imprenditori di successo.

capacità di problem solving, presa di decisioni in situazioni complesse e gestione delle relazioni, tutte insieme.

I limiti delle competenze 
Percorsi formali di studio e di apprendimento hanno un ruolo fondamentale per misurare risultati lavorativi.
La ricognizione delle competenze in termini psicologico-individuali le considerano necessarie per coprire un certo ruolo.

Le conoscenze e abilità sono il processo tecnico della competenza individuale, ma la
modalità del loro utilizzo dipende dal motore interno costituito da tratti e motivazioni personali.
E' questa la constatazione alla base del modello AMO (di BOXALL), abilità, motivazione e opportunità, sviluppato per spiegare la relazione tra politiche di gestione del personale, comportamenti individuali e prestazione aziendale.

Le attività di gestione del personale, per esempio reclutamento, selezione e formazione, migliorano le abilità dei lavoratori.
Questi ultimi non adotteranno comportamenti in linea con le attese organizzative se non in presenza di una forte motivazione, che può essere sostenuta con sistemi di valutazione sviluppo, piani di carriera, politiche retributive incentivanti.

Maggior impegno dei lavoratori si tradurrà in maggiori prestazioni aziendali solo in presenza di modelli di organizzazione del lavoro che offrono l'opportunità di partecipare e implementare quanto appreso.

Un altro limite dell'approccio psicologico individualistico è di considerare le singole
persone come isolate, trascurando situazioni in cui si creano aggregati con comportamenti collettivi con obiettivi relativamente autonomi, che non sono la semplice somma di obiettivi individuali.

Continue this story: Rick Grimes and Shane Walsh stood side-by-side, peering up at the faded billboard. EAT AT JOE’S. Faded black letters against a sun-scorched white background. The painting was chipped along the edges, remnants of a time when this highway had life thrumming through it; nineteen-wheelers thundering down the asphalt, carrying loads of tin from Lithia to Atlanta and beyond, kids laughing in the backs of minivans, bound for Orlando and a week of wonder in Mickey’s Kingdom. The paint around the left eye of the smiling tomato on top of the pizza (eat your veggies, the sign seemed to say) was peeling, and birds had built nests in the crook of Joe’s elbow. Joe appeared to be caught in the middle of a hearty laugh, head tilted back just enough to show off his double-chin, bushy red mustache hiding what was left of his teeth.

It had been Joe’s Diner in another life. He didn’t know Joe personally, but he’d heard stories. That was the way things worked in this part of Georgia—places like Lithia Springs and Austell—what Shane called “the real country.” You heard stories. People talking about people over the fencepost. Two men who’d lost their wives swearing vengeance on the police who couldn’t catch the SOB that tossed them over the bridge. The teenaged twins who discovered the body in the woods and only cried when they told their friends about it. The eight-year-old girl clutching her white teddy bear behind the bushes, watching, as the town rallied together in the wake of tragedy.

Now all that was left were the stories.

“D’you ever think about it?” Rick asked, voice choked with a strange mix of anticipation and shame. “Before, I mean.”

“Before?” Shane responded, laughing through his nose. “How the hell am I supposed to remember that far back?”

Rick turned his gaze away from the billboard and squinted at his friend. “You know, before. Before all…this.” He waved his arm, encompassing the empty fields that surrounded them, dotted with trees deader than Lazarus, before Jesus got to him.

Looking into Shane’s eyes, he could see the memory form, a hazy dream of a time before blood and bodies piled like logs, before the dead could walk and the living recoiled in terror. An unblemished moment, where life wasn’t just a daily struggle of survival, but something meaningful.

A smile formed on Shane’s lips, slow and wistful. “Yeah,” he said. “I remember.”

The friends crouched by the stream, strong sun beating down on their backs like a drummer boy gone mad, shirts tied around their waists and jeans rolled up over their knees. Eventually, they gave in to the relentless heat, and laughter faded into content silence, the gentle flow of water and their breathing in harmony.

Rick was the first to break the silence. “Remember that time we ditched school and came out here?”

Shane turned to look at him, eyebrows raised. “You mean the day we spent fishing, with a cooler full of your mama’s PBR?”

“Yup. That’s the one.” Rick dipped his fingers into the water and let it flow over his knuckles. “I thought we had such a great escape plan, lying to our folks about study groups and projects. We’d been waiting for the perfect day for months, and then it all came together.”

Shane shook his head, grinning. “We didn’t plan for old Mr. Jackson to catch us red-handed, though.”

“No,” Rick agreed, “we just planned on wading in this here stream, fish swimming past our legs, the sun beating down, and cold beers to keep us hydrated.”

“Well, we had most of that, except Mr. Jackson chased off any fish within a mile of us. I still think we’d have caught something for dinner if it wasn’t for him.”

A comfortable silence settled over them like a shroud, as they remembered a brief moment of the world that was; the America they grew up in.

“Wanna find some fish?” Shane asked, standing up with a groan.

“No thanks,” Rick replied, eyes distant. “I think I enjoyed our memories enough for now.”

They got up, the water dripping off their jeans, leaving trails in the cracked dirt as they walked back to the station wagon Shane still swore he could fix, like that time two kids with just as much hope and determination had left behind footprints of their own, a lifetime ago

# Further split the validation set into validation and test sets
x_val, x_test, y_val, y_test = train_test_split(x_val, y_val, test_size=0.5)

# Convert the outputs to a numeric data type and one-hot encode them
y_train = to_categorical(y_train.astype(np.float32))
y_val = to_categorical(y_val.astype(np.float32))
y_test = to_categorical(y_test.astype(np.float32))

# Create a neural network model
model = keras.Sequential([
    keras.layers.Dense(64, input_shape=(2,), activation='relu'),
    keras.layers.Dense(16, activation='relu'),
    keras.layers.Dense(8, activation='relu'),
    keras.layers.Dense(3, activation='softmax')
])

# Compile the model with eager execution enabled
model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='categorical_crossentropy', metrics=['accuracy'], run_eagerly=True)

# Train the model on the training data and validate on the validation data
history = model.fit(x_train, y_train, epochs=900, validation_data=(x_val, y_val))

# Evaluate the model on the test data
test_loss, test_acc = model.evaluate(x_test, y_test)
print('Test accuracy:', test_acc)

# Save the model to use with TensorFlow Lite
converter = tf.lite.TFLiteConverter.from_keras_model(model)
tflite_model = converter.convert()
open("/home/model.tflite", "wb").write(tflite_model)

#Plot the training and validation accuracy
plt.plot(history.history['accuracy'])
plt.plot(history.history['val_accuracy'])
plt.title('Model Accuracy')
plt.ylabel('Accuracy')
plt.xlabel('Epoch')
plt.legend(['train', 'validation'], loc='upper left')
plt.show()

退化性膝關節炎是常見的年長者問題，由於膝關節長期承受重力、曾經受過外傷，導致關節軟骨磨損退化、失去彈性，進而使膝關節疼痛、腫脹、僵硬、變形，導致活動受限，影響生活品質。尤其患者上下樓梯的疼痛感會加劇，休息後感到關節僵硬，當氣候變化時也會使膝關節疼痛，嚴重時，甚至無法站立。

女性鈣質流失 症狀比較嚴重
退化性膝關節炎常見於55-65歲的中老年人或肥胖者，由於女性停經後雌激素分泌大幅下滑，導致骨骼鈣質流失量增加，所以女性的退化性膝關節炎症狀較嚴重。

目前退化性膝關節炎的治療方式可分為保守治療及手術治療，保守治療包括服用止痛劑、非類固醇類藥物，或直接注射玻尿酸到膝關節內保養軟骨，也可以透過熱敷、穿戴護膝、超音波、短波照射、運動貼紮、股四頭肌運動等物理治療方式改善症狀。

當早期退化性膝關節炎治療不見效時，則會進一步透過關節鏡，在膝蓋上打2-3個0.5公分的傷口，當關節鏡進入關節腔內後，檢查關節腔受損情形，若需要治療，則可以直接清除骨刺和磨損脫落的軟骨碎屑。

置換人工關節 治療最後防線
退化性膝關節炎治療的最後一哩路，則是置換人工膝關節，清除已經磨損的軟骨和骨頭，並以人工膝關節取代。

from selenium import webdriver
        from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By
        
        driver = webdriver.Chrome()
        driver.get("https://www.example.com")
        
        # Get element with tag name 'div'
        element = driver.find_element(By.TAG_NAME, 'div')
        
        # Get all the elements available with tag name 'p'
        elements = element.find_elements(By.TAG_NAME, 'p')
        
        # Print the text of the last element in the list
        print(elements[-1].text)

En este caso, el método find_elements devuelve una lista de elementos, y [-1] selecciona el último elemento de la lista. Luego, el método text se utiliza para imprimir el texto del elemento seleccionado.

flask python cargar plantilla html

Para cargar una plantilla HTML en Flask, primero debes asegurarte de que la plantilla se encuentre en la carpeta de templates en tu aplicación Flask. Por ejemplo, si tu aplicación Flask se llama "mi_app", debes tener una carpeta llamada "templates" dentro de la carpeta "mi_app".

Dentro de la carpeta "templates", debes crear un archivo HTML con el contenido de tu plantilla. Por ejemplo, si tu archivo se llama "mi_plantilla.html", el contenido del archivo podría ser similar a esto:

<!DOCTYPE html>
        <html>
        <head>
            <title>Mi Plantilla</title>
        </head>
        <body>
            <h1>Bienvenido a mi plantilla</h1>
        </body>
        </html>

Luego, en tu archivo de aplicación Flask (por ejemplo, "app.py"), debes importar la clase render_template de Flask y usarla para cargar la plantilla en la ruta deseada. Por ejemplo:

from flask import Flask, render_template
        
        app = Flask(__name__)
        
        @app.route('/')
        def index():
            return render_template('mi_plantilla.html')
        
        if __name__ == '__main__':
            app.run()

En este ejemplo, la función index() carga la plantilla "mi_plantilla.html" usando la función render_template(), que busca el archivo de plantilla en la carpeta "templates" y lo renderiza en el navegador.

jinja2.exceptions.TemplateNotFound: mi_plantilla.html

El error "jinja2.exceptions.TemplateNotFound: mi_plantilla.html" indica que Flask no puede encontrar la plantilla HTML que estás intentando cargar.

Esto puede ocurrir por varias razones, pero las más comunes son:

  1. La plantilla HTML no está ubicada en la carpeta "templates" de tu aplicación Flask. Asegúrate de que la plantilla esté ubicada en la carpeta "templates" y que el nombre del archivo y la extensión sean correctos.

  2. La ruta del archivo de plantilla es incorrecta. Asegúrate de que la ruta de la plantilla sea correcta y esté escrita correctamente en la función render_template().

Para solucionar este error, revisa la ubicación de tus archivos de plantilla y la ruta que estás utilizando para cargar la plantilla en la función render_template(). Asegúrate de que el nombre del archivo y la extensión sean correctos y que la ruta de la plantilla sea correcta. Recuerda que la ruta debe ser relativa a la carpeta "templates" y que no debes incluir la extensión ".html" en la función render_template().

中国特色马克思主义：中国化时代化的新征程

摘要：中国特色的社会主义道路在多年的实践中形成，并在中国共产党的领导下不断发展壮大。在当代中国，面对复杂多变的社会变局，我们需要将马克思主义进行中国化和时代化的创新，以适应中国社会发展的需要，推动中国特色社会主义事业全面发展。该思想不仅符合中国推进现代化的实际情况，还能够为世界提供有效的经验。将马克思主义中国化时代化，我们应当坚持中国特色社会主义理论创新、注重融入全球化进程、注重民族文化的传承。

关键词：马克思主义，中国特色，现代化，全球化，民族文化

引言
马克思主义是一种世界观和方法论，它是在19世纪工业资本主义条件下产生的，是一种为了推动社会进步而诞生的思想体系，在1919年的五四运动中，中国知识分子开始接触和传播马克思主义，并在1921年，中国共产党成立，正式倡导和推广马克思主义，成为中国社会主义运动的旗帜。自此之后，马克思主义逐渐在中国普及和深入，成为指导中国革命和建设的指导思想。但不变马克思主义已经不能适应中国复杂的社会环境，以及中国快速的发展，在过去的几十年里，中国在发展中逐渐形成了自己独特的经济、政治和文化特点，并建立了一个科学稳定的现代化国家，这就得益于我们走中国特色社会主义道路，坚持发展有中国特色现代化的马克思主义，这种马克思主义思想适应了中国实际情况，注重实践，以科学发展观为指导，确保了中国经济稳步增长和社会进步。

本文旨在阐述在当今时代我们要如何将马克思主义更好的中国化时代化，以及当代青年能做些什么。

一、坚持中国特色社会主义理论创新
中国特色社会主义是在马克思列宁主义、毛泽东思想、邓小平理论、三个代表重要思想和科学发展观基础上形成的新时代中国特有的发展道路、发展模式和发展理念。中国特色社会主义具有鲜明的时代特征和中国特色，需要我们以中国化的眼光和方法来解决现实问题，进一步加强对马克思主义理论的创新和应用。实践是检验真理的唯一标准，我们要将马克思主义与中国社会发展相结合，探索适合中国国情的马克思主义发展路径。

（1）为什么马克思主义更好的中国化时代化要坚持中国特色社会主义理论创新
坚持中国特色社会主义理论创新可以更好地发挥马克思主义在社会主义中的指导作用，适应中国的现状，赋予马克思主义新的时代内涵和中国特色。中国特色社会主义理论创新是对马克思主义理论的创造性发展，对中华民族对世界对人类社会具有重要的历史意义与现实意义。中国特色社会主义理论创新，可以深入挖掘和拓展马克思主义这一科学思想的内涵和，更好地解决中国特殊的社会和发展问题，提出符合中国实际的最新理论成果同时，中国特色社会主义理论创新不仅是符合马克思主义基本原理的创造性发展，而且也是马克思主义中国化和时代化的一种必经之路。只有通过创新，才能使马克思主义理论与中国实际相结合，与时俱进，具有时代性，为实现中国特色社会主义事业提供更加有效的指导。

（2）当代青年如何坚持中国特色社会主义理论创新
作为新时代的青年，要以中国特色社会主义作为重要的指导思想，既要秉持传承，又要坚持创新，以下就是我们青年坚持中国特色社会主义理论创新的方法
1.增强对中国特色社会主义的理论学习和认识
坚持中国特色社会主义理论创新，首先需要对中国特色社会主义有深入的认识和学习。我们可以通过学习中央重要讲话精神、报纸、网站等途径，了解新时代下中国特色社会主义的最新成果，学会理论分析。积极参加各种形式的学习活动，如讲座、研讨会、实践观察等，不断加强对中国特色社会主义理论的学习与理解，打牢理论基础。
2.提高创新思维能力，拥有创新思维
我们可以积极参加一些创新竞赛，如互联网+竞赛、大学生创新创业大赛等等以此来提高创新思维能力，拥有创新思维，同时可以创新的思考中国特色社会主义理论提出一些创新的看法。
总之，当代青年要坚持中国特色社会主义理论创新，应当更加深入学习中国特色社会主义的理论体系，加强创新思维培养，提高创新能力为中国特色社会主义事业作出更大的贡献。

二、注重融入全球化进程。
 随着全球化进程的不断加速，中国已经成为国际社会的重要一员。我们需要将马克思主义与中国的对外关系相结合，推动中华文化的国际传播，把马克思主义融入全球化进程中，发扬光大中国特色社会主义理论体系，在全球范围内推动人类社会的进步和发展。

（1）为什么马克思主义更好的中国化时代化要注重融入全球化进程。
在当今全球化的进程中，中国加入全球化进程是十分有必要的，因为全球化能够为中国提供更广阔的市场和更多的机会，融入全球化能帮助中国更好的发展，同时融入全球化进程必须考虑国际环境和国际趋势的变化，这能使得马克思主义具有时代性，最终实现与全球经济和政治体系的有机融合，从而推动中国实现更快、更好、更可持续的发展。

（2）当代青年如何更好的注重融入全球化进程
当代青年是未来的希望，他们需要更好地注重融入全球化进程，掌握全球经济与文化的趋势和发展动态，增强个人的全球化思维和素质，以下是一些建议
1.学习外语。
全球化的一个重要表现就是语言交流的增加。学习一门外语，特别是英语是非常重要的。这样可以更好地了解国际发展动态与文化趋势，交流和合作。
2.了解国际流行文化。
了解并接触不同国家的流行文化可以拓宽视野，提升自己的文化素养。学习外国电影、音乐、时尚和饮食等，也可以促进跨文化交流与理解。
3.参与国际化的教育项目或交流。
学习或实习在国际化的教育项目或跨国企业中，可以学习到国际化的理念、技能和经验，更好地适应和融合全球经济和文化。
总之，年轻人在提高自身全球化素养的同时，也应该把握融入全球化进程的机会，积极参与国际事务。这将为自己以及国家的全球发展带来更多的机遇和挑战。

三、注重民族文化的传承
随着全球化进程的不断加快，民族文化正在被冲击和威胁。因此，中国化的马克思主义应该更加关注中华文化的传承和创新，使马克思主义“中国化”与中华文化“现代化”得以融合，实现文化的自主性和民族性，让中国的文化与全球化背景下世界的马克思主义接轨。
（1）为什么马克思主义更好的中国化时代化要注重民族文化的传承
首先，民族文化是中国文化独有的重要组成部分，是中华民族的精神和文化基因。民族文化的传承不仅是保护中华民族的文化传统和生态环境，也是马克思主义更好的中国化时代化的重要基础和前提。马克思主义在中国的实践中，需要与中华民族的文化结合，发挥中华民族文化对中国社会主义现代化建设的积极作用。只有充分挖掘利用中华民族的文化中的优点，马克思主义才能更好地中国化时代化，实现中国特色社会主义新发展。

（2）当代青年如何注重民族文化的传承
民族文化是国家和民族的精神财富，它是民族的标志，当代青年作为中华民族的接班人，应该注重民族文化的传承。以下是一些建议。
1.深入了解民族文化
可以通过阅读相关书籍、看电影、听音乐等多种途径了解民族文化，了解中华文化的丰富内涵，学习中华民族的传统美德等。
2.传承优秀传统文化
传统文化是通过代代相传的方式保留下来的。当代青年可以学习和传承中华民族的优秀传统文化和民族艺术，如诗词、绘画、音乐等。通过学习和传承，可以让经典之作得到延续和发扬。
3.积极参与民族节日
了解传统节日积极参与，也可以了解一些少数民族的传统节日并积极产加，提高自己的民族认同感同时也可以提高自身的文化修养。
总之，当代青年应该重视和注重民族文化的传承，以此为基础，推动中华民族的文化繁荣和创新，让中华文化在新时代展现出更加灿烂的光芒。

HashMap<K, V> Class – Milestone 2 (80%)
•	Must implement the Map interface.
•	IMPORTANT NOTE: You must *NOT* mention the StringKey or Item classes from within the HashMap class code! Instead, use K or V appropriately.
•	The default CAPACITY is 11
•	The default LOAD_FACTOR is 0.75 (75%)
•	Contains a public property used to contain our entries: Entry<K,V>[]  Table 
•	Maintain an average complexity of 1! 
o	O(1) for Get(), Put(), Remove() 


HashMap()	Constructor, initializes Table to default size and load factor to default size
HashMap(int initialCapacity)	Constructor, initializes Table to size passed and assigns load factor to default value.
HashMap(int initialCapacity, double loadFactor) (5%)	Constructor, initializes Table to size passed and assigns load factor to value passed.
int Size()	Returns current size (note, this DOES NOT include placeholders) May be a smart property in C#.
bool IsEmpty()	Returns true if number of active entries in the array is 0.
void Clear()	Wipes out the array and all placeholders
int GetMatchingOrNext
AvailableBucket
(K key) Looks for the next available bucket based on the key passed, (Uses linear probing for collision handling, will return to the 0 index and continue searching if array length is reached). Note, if the key exists, it returns the bucket of the matching key. 
DO NOT LOOP THROUGH EVERY ENTRY FROM 0 TO ARRAY LENGTH IN THIS METHOD. Start from the starting bucket and use linear probing. It may end up going through many indexes, but in practice it will never do that because you have a threshold and there are many empty array spots.
V Get(K key) Returns the value located at the bucket found by hashing the key. This may return null if no matching key exists at this bucket. Note that this must handle collisions through linear probing. (use GetMatchingOrNextAvailableBucket()). 
DO NOT LOOP THROUGH EVERY ENTRY FROM 0 TO ARRAY LENGTH IN THIS METHOD.
V Put(K key, V value) Adds or Updates the bucket found by hashing the key.  If the bucket is empty insert a new entry with the passed key and value pair and return null.  If the bucket is not empty, override the old value in the bucket and return the old value. Note that this must handle collisions through linear probing. (use GetMatchingOrNextAvailableBucket()). When adding a new entry you must check if you require a rehash first. If the size + placeholders plus the new entry is equal to the threshold, then run rehash (see slides for more details).
DO NOT LOOP THROUGH EVERY ENTRY FROM 0 TO ARRAY LENGTH IN THIS METHOD.
V Remove(K key) Looks up the bucket based on the hashcode of the key. If a value exists at this bucket, set the value to null and increase your placeholder counter by one. If nothing exists at this bucket return null. Note that this must handle collisions through linear probing. (use GetMatchingOrNextAvailableBucket()).
DO NOT LOOP THROUGH EVERY ENTRY FROM 0 TO ARRAY LENGTH IN THIS METHOD.
private int ReSize() During a Rehash, a new array size must be calculated. We start by doubling the original size, adding 1 and finding the next prime number, see theory slides for this algorithm.
void ReHash() Occurs when the threshold (table length * load factor) is reached when adding a new Entry<K,V> to the Table.  Note that placeholders (removed values) count towards this total.  Example:  An array is size 10, the load factor is 0.3 (30%), therefore the threshold is 10*0.3 = 3.  After using Put() twice, the size goes up to 2. When using Remove() once, the size goes down to 1, but the placeholder count is increased to 1.  Now when we use Put() again, the threshold is reached, because 1 size + 1 placeholder is 2 and adding another entry will bring us up to 3, the threshold value. 

Perform a resize to find the new Table array length (see slides for details on resize and prime numbers). Migrate each entry from the old Table into the new table.  IMPORTANT NOTE: When migrating old table buckets, you must recalculate the new table buckets based on the new table length! This is the most common mistake.
IEnumerator<V> Values() Returns an IEnumerator compatible object containing only the values of each Entry in the Table (skip placeholders).
IEnumerator<K> Keys() Returns an IEnumerator compatible object containing only the keys of each Entry in the Table (skip placeholders).

“浙大的数字化理念就是为浙大师生提供一流的数字化环境，提供高效便捷的数字化服务。钉钉的出现，让我们的理念实现了更快的落地。”张紫徽告诉界面。他是浙江大学信息技术中心的总工程师，“同时，钉钉也让学校有了新的‘内生力量’。”

地处杭州的浙江大学，不仅有百年的历史底蕴，更有西子湖畔的优雅，是一所传承与创新兼具的综合性大学。

作为人才培养的摇篮，前沿精神、最新科技的汇聚地，浙江大学始终走在探索创新的前列。它在探索高校数字化转型上的经验，对于其他高校和企业来说，都具有非常大的借鉴意义。

01、百年名校背后的数字化变革

在云计算、大数据、人工智能等新技术快速发展的今天，传统行业正在通过加速拥抱数字技术，全面实现转型升级，高校也不例外。但高校在数字化建设的过程中，也遇到许多具有共性的挑战：

高校在业务管理上最大的痛点是“各自为主”，部门间缺少协同，即以高校的各个部门为主，根据自己的实际需要建设各自的系统应用，在建设中很难顾及到数字化的全局，尤其在顶层设计的能力上较为薄弱。

其次，缺少平台支撑。在信息化建设的过程中，特别是早期探索的时候，所有开发的应用，很多都是偏向于一个短期的系统开发或者流程设计，它能发挥的作用是非常有限的，缺少跟未来其他系统之间连接的能力，存在数据孤岛，需要从底层逐步打通。

以浙江大学为例，数字化建设早期，校内各服务中心、多校区之间协同沟通比较分散，各类校园系统也越来越多，导致内部工作信息分散，既无法保障数据流转的安全性，又需要频繁切换系统处理消息，耗时耗力；同时，学校的日常工作开展，比如重要通知，多媒体教学活动，各项审批等，有的还需要在PC端进行。

有同样难点的还有地处重庆的西南大学。过去，学校业务办理或学生管理的重要信息传递面临平台不一、时效性差的问题，校内各个系统之间相互独立，总是错过重要消息的待办。

在这样的背景下， 钉钉的出现及时地顺应了教育数字化的需求。经过疫情三年的加速，钉钉也早已经成为教育领域数字基建底座一般的存在。

浙江大学信息技术中心总工程师张紫徽认为，想要用好钉钉，要先认识到钉钉的价值。他认为钉钉有三大核心价值：首先，它是一个超级强大的通讯工具；第二，它是一个强大的组织中枢，或者叫组织管理工具；第三，它是一个非常好的叫协同工具。

基于对钉钉核心价值的理解，2018年6月，浙大和钉钉开始合作。2019年6月份，依托于钉钉底座拥有强大通讯能力的APP“浙大钉”上线App Store。自此，浙大拥有能够在一个端口集成所有应用服务入口的能力,为实现部门间的高效协作打下基础。同时，基于钉钉开放的技术底座，对接校内第三方数据接口，在一个“浙大钉”内打造任务中心、办事中心、应用中心，资讯中心、填表中心、日程中心、个人中心，实现咨询一屏晾晒、消息一键掌控，服务“一站式”办理。

现如今，找同学找老师，接收学校重要通知，进出校门打卡、吃饭刷卡等，不管是获取校园信息，还是查找校园服务，获得教学服务，只需一个钉钉就够了。 可以说，钉钉作为一个每天高频使用的工具，已经跟浙大的基因完全的融合在了一起。

除了上述钉钉在浙大的数字化“落地”，在西南大学学校管理、师生服务方面所实现的高效协同、即时通讯等，钉钉也发挥了巨大的效用。

西南大学和钉钉联合打造的“数智西大”首先解决多头登录的问题，通过钉钉开放的底座能力，统一登录认证，整合校内30多款应用接入到“数智西大”，建成涵盖学工、招生、迎新、科研、人事、采购、教务等多项服务在内的统一综合服务门户。同时，通过钉钉通讯录、即时通讯、在线文档等原生功能，形成了大家新的工作习惯，有什么业务提醒第一反应到钉钉上操作，形成统一的消息平台，打通工作协作沟通路径，通知效率明显改善。

西南大学信息化建设办公室主任贾韬谈到：“钉钉为学校的数智化转型提供了稳定开放的数字底座，更在教育数字化建设中发挥了基础核心作用。”

钉钉，培育新的“内生力量”

近期，《数字中国建设整体布局规划》发布，提及打造试点示范，推进高等教育数字化战略走深走实。 2023年全国教育工作会议进一步指出，全国教育系统要坚定“统筹推进教育数字化”重点任务。教育数字化转型已经进入到深水区。

以浙江大学为例，其数字化发展大致分为三个阶段：2013—2017 年是第一个阶段，建立了校务服务网和行政办事大厅，服务师生“最多跑一次”；2017—2020年是第二个阶段，也是数字化转型1.0的阶段； 2020年后，基于钉钉对教学模式的改变，浙大的数字化转型也进入到了第三个阶段：“数字化改革阶段”。

钉钉对浙大业务数字化的改变，是它更大的价值体现。通过集成在钉钉端的学在浙大、智云课堂，借助阿里云强大的空间支持，实现了线上线下相融合的教学体系。随着教学模式的改变，倒逼教学质量的提升。

在浙大的教室里，有常态化的直播跟录播系统，学生可以在教室听，也可以在线上听，也可以随时回看。如果遭遇突发状况，可以马上切换到线上教学。所有师生全到钉群里去做教学，钉群是常态化维持在那里的。

在钉钉端的教学活动，主要依托“学在浙大”和“智云课堂”两个应用。前者是教学平台，里面有很多教学工具，比如点名，随堂测试，布置作业等。“智云课堂”属于是直播工具，教师可以在里面直播上课。

张紫徽也讲了一个特别有趣的故事。浙大钉上的智云课堂，打破了所有教室的边界，你可以在任何一个时间进入到任何一个教室里，去听任何一个老师的任何一门课程，这是它的价值。在他们最早上线智云课堂的时候，非常担心会遭到老师的全体吐槽。

出人意料的是，这种无边界的教学模式不仅方便了学生的学习，还倒逼了教师们的“自我进步”。一位法学院的老师向信息中心反馈，一位学生表示自己在军训期间就把一整个学期的课程学完了。更多老师听到这个故事之后，纷纷表示自己应该重新制作自己的课件。

“智云课堂就像是一个大舞台，把所有老师和他们的课程内容，都放在了聚光灯下，倒逼着老师们不断精进自己的课程内容，真正地对学生负责。看上去的确是遭到了几位老师的投诉，但是他们却让整体的教学质量提升了，”张紫徽说到，“钉钉的出现，让学校老师们有了新的‘内生力量’，也对日后的数字化建设有了更强的信心。”

北京理工大学当前正处于中关村、良乡两校区“双核运行”的状态，师生教学活动存在线下沟通不便的问题。另外，顺应新冠肺炎疫情期间“停课不停学”的需求，线上教学逐渐成为了主流的教学模式。

结合当下的需求， “i北理”APP为北理工师生提供了通讯录、群聊、直播、视频会议、群联播等功能，并且打通了教务系统和钉钉群。老师通过钉钉工作台上的教学班查询就可获取教务系统中的选课信息，一键创建教学群并进行管理，然后通过群直播的方式上课，多群联播功能也满足了多个班级同时教学的需求；课后，学生可以观看回放进行复习。教学活动可以随时随地开展，打破了教与学的时空限制，北京理工逐步实现了“时时可学、处处可学”的目标。

从内生力量到能力输出

钉钉赋能高校数字化，不仅是推动了高校管理的高校和学生生活的便利，更重要的是它让每一所学校都能享受到公平的教育资源，充分享受数字化的红利。

浙大一直在探索新式办学空间，结合浙大自身丰富的知识资源，挖掘具有普世价值的优质内容，通过钉钉，降低学习门槛，不断打破学校边界，让更多的人有机会学习更多优质的教学内容。

比如，2022年暑期开办的“全球暑期学校”，惠及全球81个国家和地区的师生。借助钉钉由内到外走出去，为更多的学校提供社会服务。

张紫徽带领的浙大信息技术中心也联合浙大工会，不断策划优质主题讲座，比如，儿童身体发育，家长课堂，女性健康等，并将这些视频内容，在钉钉上免费向所有钉钉用户开放。

未来，浙江大学数字化改革会坚持以“以学生成长为中心”，在教育技术加数据智能双轮驱动下，把学校理想中的知识、能力、素质、人格的培养模式，与学生真正想要和需要的内容，完美融合。钉钉的技术工具和生态能力也将不断深化，让这个目标变得更加切实可行。
