‘Overemployed’ Hustlers Exploit ChatGPT To Take On Even More Full-Time Jobs
"ChatGPT does like 80 percent of my job," said one worker. Another is holding the line at four robot-performed jobs. "Five would be overkill," he said.
MS
By Maxwell Strachan
April 12, 2023, 1:00pm




Loading your audio article

Screen Shot 2023-04-11 at 4
CREDIT: GETTY STOCK PHOTO)
About a year ago, Ben found out that one of his friends had quietly started to work multiple jobs at the same time. The idea had become popular during the COVID-19 pandemic, when working from home became normalized, making the scheme easier to pull off. A community of multi-job hustlers, in fact, had come together online, referring to themselves as the “overemployed.” 

The idea excited Ben, who lives in Toronto and asked that Motherboard not use his real name, but he didn’t think it was possible for someone like him to pull it off. He helps financial technology companies market new products; the job involves creating reports, storyboards, and presentations, all of which involve writing. There was “no way,” he said, that he could have done his job two times over on his own. 

ADVERTISEMENT
Then, last year, he started to hear more and more about ChatGPT, an artificial intelligence chatbot developed by the research lab OpenAI. Soon enough, he was trying to figure out how to use it to do his job faster and more efficiently, and what had been a time-consuming job became much easier. ("Not a little bit more easy,” he said, “like, way easier.") That alone didn’t make him unique in the marketing world. Everyone he knew was using ChatGPT at work, he said. But he started to wonder whether he could pull off a second job. Then, this year, he took the plunge, a decision he attributes to his new favorite online robot toy. 

How are people you know using ChatGPT at work? We want to hear from you. From a non-work device, contact our reporter at <PRESIDIO_ANONYMIZED_EMAIL_ADDRESS> or via Signal at 310-614-3752 for extra security.

“That's the only reason I got my job this year,” Ben said of OpenAI's tool. “ChatGPT does like 80 percent of my job if I’m being honest.” He even used it to generate cover letters to apply for jobs.

Over the last few months, the exploding popularity of ChatGPT and similar products has led to growing concerns about AI’s potential effects on the international job market—specifically, the percentage of jobs that could be automated away, replaced by a well-oiled army of chatbots. But for a small cohort of fast-thinking and occasionally devious go-getters, AI technology has turned into an opportunity not to be feared but exploited, with their employers apparently none the wiser. 

ADVERTISEMENT
The people Motherboard spoke with for this article requested anonymity to avoid losing their jobs. For clarity, Motherboard in some cases assigned people aliases in order to differentiate them, though we verified each of their identities. Some, like Ben, were drawn into the overemployed community as a result of ChatGPT. Others who were already working multiple jobs have used recent advancements in AI to turbocharge their situation, like one Ohio-based technology worker who upped his number of jobs from two to four after he started to integrate ChatGPT into his work process. “I think five would probably just be overkill,” he said. 

‘The Best Assistant Ever’
Throughout the overemployed community, there is a quiet arms race to figure out just how much of the corporate workday can be automated away using an assortment of AI tools, some of which predate ChatGPT. The possibility of increasing their income, or at least easing the burden of holding down multiple jobs, has led to an explosion of experimentation.

When one of Ben’s bosses, for example, now asks him to create a story for an upcoming product release, he will explain the context and provide a template to ChatGPT, which then creates an outline for him and helps fill out the sections. The AI chatbot knows Ben’s title and the parameters of his duties and has become even better at understanding the context since the launch of GPT-4, the latest edition, he said. “I can just tell it to create a story,” said Ben, “and it just does it for me, based off the context that I gave it.” Ben still needs to verify the information—”sometimes it gets stuff wrong, which is totally normal,” he said—but the adjustments are relatively “minor” and easy to fix. 

ADVERTISEMENT
Occasionally, he even asks ChatGPT to craft responses to Slack messages from his manager. In such cases, he requests that ChatGPT write the message in all lowercase, so that it appears more organic to the boss.  Another overemployed worker also told me they have started using ChatGPT to transcribe Zoom meetings so they can be largely ignored in the moment and referenced later.

Charles, who has worked as a software engineer and product manager and solutions architect, including at a FAANG company, had been all-in on overemployment since 2020—while he currently works two jobs, he worked four at the height of the pandemic—but said that AI tools have made juggling the positions much easier. 

At the FAANG company, he was able to outsource written tasks to AI tools, like writing a memo to defend and justify a business decision. In such a case, he’d input the relevant facts and parameters into an AI chatbot, which would cohesively lay them out more quickly than he ever could. Additionally, he’d use it to lay out directions for engineers (“It allows you to take, basically, a sentence and expand it out into a paragraph”); and create a “foundation” when coding. The ChatGPT-created code “oftentimes” would work perfectly, he said, but the errors could be identified and resolved easily enough, he said. 

One member of the overemployed, who, unusually, works three financial reporting jobs, said he’s found ChatGPT useful in the creation of macros in Excel. “I can create macros, but it takes me an hour, two hours, plus, to write the code, test it, make sure everything's working,” he said. By comparison, with ChatGPT, he can provide the parameters and it’ll “spit something out” that he can update and tweak to his specifications. The process can allow him to cram what is traditionally a “two-week long process” into a few hours.  (He says he avoids providing ChatGPT with confidential information.)

ADVERTISEMENT
Daniel, a staff engineer on the East Coast who works one director-level position and another as a senior dev (one job is on Pacific time and one is in the United Kingdom), similarly said that ChatGPT’s code can leave something to be desired, but said it’s been useful when it comes to writing emails. “Most people in tech probably aren't as good at writing things as most other people,” Daniel said. He included himself in that critique of his own industry, but said it’s no longer a problem, as he can plug the key points into ChatGPT and ask the AI assistant to rewrite it “in a more professional way,” he said. “It's really good for stuff like that.”

Excitement for the potential of ChatGPT isn’t limited to the technology and financial spheres of the overemployed community. Marshall, a university lecturer in the United Kingdom who secretly runs a digital marketing agency and tech startup on the side, has become a ChatGPT fanatic since its release. (During class, he often has students run through exercises, during which time he is often able to open up his laptop and work on his side hustles.) “It’s the best assistant ever,” he told me excitedly.

Marshall has come to see himself as the idea man, and ChatGPT as the labor. “I'm quite a conceptualizing person. So I'm quite happy for my brain to do that. But the first draft of anything almost always goes through GPT,” he said.  Already, the chatbot has helped him generate business plans, internal system documents, blog posts, and Excel spreadsheets. He estimated that ChatGPT can often pull off 80 percent of the legwork, leaving him to handle the final 20 percent.  

ADVERTISEMENT
The tool has even helped him win a grant from the U.K. government (the application was “50-50 me and ChatGPT,” he said) and complete coursework for a master’s degree necessary to receive a university teaching qualification he was too busy to handle by himself while working three jobs.

The members of the overemployed community know that what they’re doing is frowned on by corporate leaders. But that doesn’t mean they think what they are doing is amoral. “I never could mentally comprehend why it was so taboo for me to work two salaried positions,” said the Ohio-based technology worker. “There's plenty of people I've known in my personal life who have worked at Walmart from 4 a.m. to 2 p.m., and then gone and worked another job.” The financial professional similarly said he started working multiple jobs because he doesn't trust that working as hard as he can at a single job will be “rewarded with more pay,” just “more work.” By taking on more jobs, he can do more work but also “get paid for it,” he said. 

‘One Loom Operator As Opposed to 100 Weavers’
More than a member of the overemployed community, Charles, the FAANG alumni, considers himself part of the FIRE movement—short for “Financial Independence, Retire Early” Not yet 30, he is already making $500,000 working two jobs and worth around $3 million, claims he backed up to Motherboard with documentation. But he hopes to increase his compensation to $800,000 by tacking on a third position, and reach a net worth of $10 million by 35.

Even though he is already using ChatGPT to work multiple jobs, Charles still is trying to figure out ways to make his dream even easier to obtain. When we spoke he said he’s already been “able to outsource” coding tasks to a third party in the past, and that he has been hard at work trying to develop a way to have someone else mimic both his voice and image on a computer screen. I will use the grant to travel to the ASSC26 (association for the scientific study of consciousness) conference in New York, hosted by David Chalmers at NYU. I will present on my own original research there, a micro-phenomenological study of the DMT experience. I work with the Imperial College London Centre for Psychedelic Research.

I have already written a letter of support from my supervisor (I wrote it on his behalf). what I didn’t realise is that I actually also need a 1 page application letter. Because I didn’t know about the application letter, I included some things in the supervisor letter of support that probably don’t need to be there. Currently, the supervisor support letter argues for the originality and novelty of my research, but this is probably more suited to the application letter (if you agree, maybe it doesn’t need to be written about at all!). Also it discusses why I can't afford the conference on my own, which is probably also better suited to the application letter.

I will paste below the abstract of the presentation, as well as the letter of support that I have written, in case there is information in there that is helpful for you. Can you please write the 1 page application letter, and then re-write the support letter to complement it. Please don’t make the letters too formulaic. They should be serious, but also authentic and personable.

Thank you

Presentation abstract——
Title:
Towards a micro-phenomenology of the intravenous DMT state
Introduction: 
When administered in the lab, the 5-HT2A receptor agonist N, N-Dimethyltryptamine (DMT) radically alters the subjective character of experience. However, scientific understanding of DMT experiences in a lab setting is limited by the shortcomings of commonly used phenomenological methods. Specifically, phenomenological models based on self-report questionnaire methods typically do not typically capture the temporal dynamics of experience, instead averaging subjective properties over the entire experience. Qualitative methods, such as thematic or content analysis, suffer this same limitation. The micro-phenomenology (MP) interview and analysis method is well suited to address this lack of granularity in psychedelic phenomenology, modelling experience richly on both the synchronic (within-moment) and diachronic (between-moments) dimensions.
Methods: 
This qualitative study is the first to apply both the MP interview and analysis method to psychedelic data. 25 participants were intravenously dosed with 20 mg of DMT fumarate in a lab setting while undergoing combined EEG and fMRI. MP interviews about the experience were performed upon return to a baseline state. A micro-phenomenological analysis protocol was applied, including novel adaptations developed to accommodate the particularities of non-ordinary experience. Synchronic and diachronic categories were extracted and used to compare and cluster similar experiences.
Results: 
A hierarchical taxonomy of categories on both the synchronic and diachronic dimensions is proposed, along with descriptions and observed frequencies of the phenomenological clusters that emerged. 
Discussion: 
In line with Varela’s ‘neurophenomenological’ research programme, further work on this project will statistically validate the phenomenological clusters identified here against the corresponding fMRI and EEG data. Additionally, the present study can be seen as the first step in a micro-phenomenological pipeline, starting here with a comprehensive look at entire DMT experiences, before narrowing down in further work to study component experiences (e.g.: the experience of presences that seem to have their own minds, colloquially referred to as ‘DMT entities’) at the micro-phenomenological level.


Letter of support——
This letter confirms my support of James Sanders’ application for your early career investigator grant program. James has been working with the Centre for Psychedelic Research at Imperial College London, under my supervision, since early 2022. During this time James has assisted with data collection in the lab and in the field, focusing primarily on the phenomenological (especially qualitative) aspects of our research. He has also worked on analysing the collected data. 
James’ accepted talk, ‘Towards a micro-phenomenology of the intravenous DMT experience’ is the culmination of James’ contributions over this past year, featuring not only new insights into the little-understood phenomenology of DMT experience, but also novel methods in the study of non-ordinary consciousness that he has contributed greatly to developing. This research is the first ever application of the micro-phenomenological analysis method to psychedelic interview data, and the results of this analysis will be used in a forthcoming neuro-phenomenological analysis of the first ever combined fMRI/EEG imaging study of psychedelic experience (for which the preceding neurobiological results of the same study were recently published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences [PNAS]).
The debate over whether subjective experience is necessary for transformative outcomes in psychedelic assisted psychotherapy is currently at the forefront of the psychedelic research field, and so this work is timely. It is our hope that this presentation at ASSC26 will contribute to, and enrich this debate by not only elucidating the specific subjective effects, but also inspiring better phenomenological methods in the study of non-ordinary states. ASSC is attended by some of the most influential researchers and philosophers in the study of consciousness, many with an interest in how non-ordinary consciousness can inform our understanding of ordinary consciousness, and so it is an ideal forum for disseminating this work. A preliminary version of these same results were presented by James to a psychedelic-specific audience in a poster at the Interdisciplinary Conference on Psychedelic Research (ICPR) in September 2022.
Because James’ PhD program has not yet commenced (expected commencement: fall 2023), it is outside the established policies for the Centre for Psychedelic Research to fund James’ attendance at the conference. We hope that the generosity of the Heffter Research Institute will make James’ attendance possible. James’ demonstrated passion and tenacity as a researcher leave me no doubt that he would use this opportunity to its fullest.

explicame esta review por pasos del juego baldur's gate 3: "Love this game so far.


Pros:

Graphics are great; definitely one of the best-looking top-down games I've ever played. One minor complaint I have is that it is a little unstable in certain areas, particularly those with lots of effects going on like fire, or other glowing effects. Could be optimized a bit better, but the full release is still a few months away, so I expect Larian to get most optimization issues straightened out before then.
Another thing is that when I restart the game, my anti-aliasing settings always get set back to 'None', regardless of how many times I set it to TAA and hit 'Apply'. Kind of weird and a little annoying.


Story topic is interesting. The general gist is that you're captured by mind flayers and placed into their Nautiloid warship, where you are then given a parasite that presumably transforms you into a mind flayer yourself. The story seems to revolve around your struggle with the effects of the parasite, and your journey to remove it, by whatever means possible. Pretty cool scenario.
I've thoroughly enjoyed everything that the Early Access version of the story can provide, and I'm very much looking forward to the finished product.


Characters are great and probably my favorite aspect of the game. They are intriguing, charismatic and a bit mysterious. I've often found myself enjoying the conversations with the main characters more than actually playing the game; this doesn't mean the gameplay is mediocre, because it's not, it just means that the characters are that good.
For example, 
This is quite possibly the most enveloped I have ever been in video game characters stories.


Gameplay and Combat is fun and engaging. As per usual with Larian Studios, we have the strategic turn-based combat with tons of cool abilities and skills.
It seems you have one 'Action' point and one 'Bonus Action' point per turn. Most skills and spells require one 'Action' point, but some may also used with the 'Bonus Action' point depending on their requirements. Consumables like potions require one 'Bonus Action' point to use, whereas scrolls or magic items may require one normal 'Action' point.
I'm unsure if there is a way to permanently increase the number of 'Action' or 'Bonus Action' points you have, but I do know that you can use certain abilities to give your character an extra point on their turn.

Spells and what-not require 'Spell Slots' that pertain to their type and tier in order to be cast. For example, if you're casting a Level 2 Sorcerer's Spell, you would require one Level 2 Sorcerer's Spell Slot. These Spell Slots get consumed upon use, and can be regenerated by resting at camp, or various items or actions.

Speaking of resting at camp, you have two options for this; 'Short Rest' and 'Long Rest'.
The 'Short Rest' allows you and your party to regenerate some health and to regenerate Warlock Spell Slots. This option is instantaneous and doesn't return you to your campsite.
The 'Long Rest' allows you and your party to regenerate all health and to regenerate Warlock and Sorcerer Spell Slots. This option also ends the day, bringing you and your companions back to your campsite for the night, which also allows you to have in-depth conversations with your companions and get some insight as to who they are and what their story is.

Cons/Personal dislikes:

Cutscenes are great, but they're quite buggy and inconsistent. For example, in the cutscene for meeting with Auntie Ethel, Mayrina's brothers freeze up and glitch throughout the scene. Another instance can be seen throughout the game; some dialogue transitions are either too late or too early,
Don't get me wrong, I love the cutscenes, and the graphics make them that much better, but I believe they do need to be refined a bit. Again, seeing as this is the Early Access version, I do expect most of these flaws to be ironed out in the full release.


I'm personally not a big fan of the Spell Slot system. I understand it from a balancing standpoint, and it definitely makes things interesting, but it does become a bit of an annoyance at times. It'd be nice to just have a turn cooldown, similar to Divinity.
It may also be a DnD thing, which I wouldn't know since I've never played it.
Regardless, it's not that bad. Combat is still fun even though I'm not a fan of the Spell Slot feature.


There is a slight issue with opening doors. If you click to open a door from a distance, your character will walk up to it, but not open it. However, if you're standing right next to the door, it will open. Sometimes, the animation for the opening door also gets stuck, and will appear closed or half-open, but you can still walk through it like normal.
Kind of strange, but not a major functional issue. I'm unsure if anyone else has had this problem.


To summarize, I feel this is going to be one of my favorite RPG's once it releases. I think I've done close to everything available in Early Access, and it's been a great experience. Highly recommend the game, even in the Early Access state.

Hyped for the full release."

The issue of gun violence continues to plague the United States, with an average of 100 Americans killed by firearms every day. While the debate surrounding gun control remains politically divisive, one solution that could bridge the gap between opposing views is to introduce firearm education and law-specific education in public schools. This approach aims to educate Americans on guns and gun laws, helping them avoid legal troubles, understand when it is permissible to use a firearm, and participate knowledgeably in local government.

Well-regulated firearm education has been proven to significantly reduce gun accidents, especially among children. According to data from the National Safety Council, nonfatal firearm accidents have declined by 94% since 1930, partly due to efforts to educate the public on gun safety, such as the adoption of the National Rifle Association’s (NRA) “Eddie Eagle” program by some schools. Research from the Journal of Law and Economics shows that these programs have positively impacted children’s behavior around firearms, resulting in a 37% reduction in gun accidents in states implementing them.

Moreover, mandatory gun education in schools would create a baseline of knowledge on the legal use of firearms, reducing the risk of innocent, law-abiding citizens criminalizing themselves unknowingly. A study from the American Journal of Preventive Medicine found that over 60% of surveyed gun owners were not familiar with firearm laws, highlighting the need for increased education. By having a clear understanding of the legal boundaries in which they can carry and use guns, Americans will be better prepared to engage in self-defense situations, protect their rights, and avoid legal issues.

In addition to promoting responsible and law-abiding firearm usage, a gun education curriculum would foster a better appreciation for the historical and legislative aspects of gun rights, empowering future generations to become active, well-informed participants in the local government. An educated populace is key to democratic decision-making and critical to sustaining and improving our political system. By understanding the historical context surrounding gun rights and how they have evolved through policy and legal decisions, students will not only be better equipped to engage in discussions on gun control but also be more conscious participants in the democratic process.

Critics might argue that introducing gun education in schools would normalize gun usage, potentially leading to increased gun violence. However, the intent of the program would be to emphasize the importance of responsible gun ownership, understanding the law, and promoting public safety. Rather than encouraging unsafe gun usage, the focus would be on fostering educated citizens who can steward the rights secured by the Second Amendment, and responsibly participate in discourse surrounding gun control and policy by further educating others who may be irresponsible. A normalization of responsible firearm usage could make people be safer around them. A comparison is there is a normalization of safe car usage, so when someone is stupid in a car, we don’t blame the car, we blame the idiot in the car and the person’s driving habits are looked down upon.

In conclusion, implementing firearm education and law-specific education into public schools would have numerous benefits. Apart from promoting public safety and reducing gun accidents, it would educate Americans on the legal aspects of firearm usage and help them become better-informed participants in local government. By fostering a culture of responsible and educated gun ownership, we can secure the rights provided by the Second Amendment and work towards a safer and informed society.

Riassumi il seguente testo in … parole, le frasi o parole come nell’esempio: ||parola|| sono fondamentali e pertanto non vanno cambiate né rimosse:

Questa dinamica, come approfondiremo di seguito, si modifica radicalmente con riferimento ai retai ler monomarca dove product brand e retail brand si sovrappongono. L'interazione tra "brand loyalty e store loyalty". L'analisi dei processi di interazione tra product brand e retail brand implica la considerazione dei fenomeni di "brand loyalty e store loyalty" e che in questa sede acquisiscono il significato di product brand loyalty e di retail brand loyalty. Il tema della loyalty ha assunto un rilievo nei mercati a basso tasso di crescita e in virtù del fatto che la relazione con i clienti diviene generalmente più profittevole col trascorrere del tempo. 
Si può sostenere che la product (brand) loyalty sia quella fedeltà mani-festata dai clienti nei confronti di un certo product brand mentre la store (retail brand) loyaty sia legata alla scelta di un particolare punto vendita effettuata dal cliente. 
Ciò detto, ed in virtù della mutua influenza che sussiste tra retail brand e product brand, store loyalty e brand loyalty non devono essere considerate esclusivamente in un'ottica contrapposta in effetti le due fedeltà non implicano necessariamente un reciproco contrasto ma anzi manifestano livelli di "integrazione". A favore di questa interpretazione sussistono due ordini di ragioni: la prima riguarda i caratteri costitutivi della fedeltà al punto vendita che. pur arricchendosi di contenuti, e ancora fortemente determinata dalla capacità di una superficie commerciale di offrire quei prodotti e quelle marche verso le quali il cliente manifesta maggiore propensione d'acquisto; la seconda ragione, in modo complementare alla prima, deriva dal fatto che la brand experience si realizza per larga parte "in store". In tal senso, si deve considerare come la relazione tra brand loyalty e store loyalty divenga sempre più stretta: questo accade perché, nella prospettiva esperienziale, product brand e retail brand si configurano come un unico conte- nitore dei caratteri distintivi ed emozionali dell'offerta dell'impresa, siano essi ti- conducibili ad uno specifico prodotto o al punto vendita.
Percorsi di vertical branding. 
Dall'osservazione delle condotte competitive delle imprese (in particolare quelle di abbigliamento) si nota come numerose imprese industriali ed altrettanti retailer cerchino di presidiare più livelli della filiera, ponendo in essere percorsi di integrazione verticale. In particolare, questa dinamica vede da un lato imprese industriali impegnate ad aprire punti vendita monomarca (di proprietà, in franchising o in altre forme ad esso assimilabili), attraverso i quali commercializzare i propri product brand, e, dall'altro lato, i retailer impegnati nella creazione di private labels da inserire nell'assortimento dei propri punti vendita. Sulla scorta di queste dinamiche, ci sembra utile fare riferimento al concetto di "Vertical Brand" che in prima istanza può essere inteso come l'intersezione tra product brand e retail brand. La nozione di Vertical Brand è riconducibile alla capacità di ciascun attore, impresa a matrice industriale o retailer, di sviluppare un posizionamento competitivo basato sul controllo di ambedue le declinazioni di brand (Product e Retail brand) e sulla possibilità di deciderne il livello ottimale di integrazione, La strategia di sviluppo di una Vertical Brand punta a generare una esperienza complessiva ed integrata della marca veicolata dal prodotto, dalla comunicazione a verso i media, dal punto vendita. In altre parole, i pubblici a cui si rivolge l'impresa sperimentano una moltiplicazione delle occasioni cognitive, emozionali e comportamentali derivanti da quel brand che possiede sia una componente di "prodotto che una di "insegna". La possibilità di generare una brand experience efficace dipende in larga parte dalla capacità delle imprese di armonizzare la strategia di marca con quelle di comunicazione e di distribuzione che trovano, a loro volta, nel vendita la piattaforma di relazione più efficace.

||3. LE POLITICHE DI COMUNICAZIONE||

||3.1. STRUTTURA E CRITICITÀ DEI PROCESSI DI COMUNICAZIONE||

La comunicazione ha un ruolo centrale nell'ambito del trasferimento del valore come fonte privilegiata di segnali di valore per il consumatore. Le politiche di comunicazione sono principalmente finalizzate a:
 -far conoscere il prodotto, il brand e l'impresa (interventi sulla sfera cognitiva del consumatore, per generare notorietà): 
-differenziare il prodotto e la marca (interventi sulla sfera degli atteggiamenti del consumatore); 
-spingere alla prova, all'acquisto, al riacquisto del prodotto (interventi sulla sfera dei comportamenti di consumo). Gli effetti ricercati con la comunicazione sono quindi:
- lo stimolo della domanda e lo sviluppo delle vendite: - la riduzione dell'elasticità della domanda al prezzo e l'incremento della fedeltà del consumatore:
-lo sviluppo di barriere verso i competitor.

La comunicazione, quindi, è in molti casi vitale, soprattutto quando sul mercato notorietà, immagine di marca e presidio ampio e sistematico dei canali risultino fattori critici di successo. Essa, però, non deve essere confusa con il marketing (co- me spesso accade nella pratica, soprattutto nelle imprese minori), bensì deve rap- presentare uno degli strumenti per dare concretezza alle scelte di tipo strategico, con particolare riguardo al posizionamento del prodotto e della marca. 
In questo senso, è anche importante, come vedremo, che l'azienda non pensi di poter semplicemente demandare lo sforzo comunicazionale a soggetti esterni (agenzie specializzate), a maggior ragione oggi, con l'avanzare deciso del digitale, che disegna un terreno di gioco completamente nuovo, fatto di relazioni sistematiche e possibilmente autentiche con la domanda.

In questi ultimi anni, lo scenario della comunicazione è profondamente muta to ed è tuttora in evoluzione, con la saturazione di molti canali canonici di comunicazione, con la maggiore resistenza da parte dei consumatori (per vari motivi, dalla diffidenza alla banalizzazione degli acquisti) ai messaggi veicolari dalle imprese (con il rischio di insoddisfacenti ritorni), ma anche con la disponibilità di nuovi strumenti, canali e modalità di contatto con il mercato, in primis collegati alla diffusione delle ICT, In base alla tipologia di destinatari cui è rivolta, la comunicazione può essere in terna (verso i dipendenti) o esterna (verso consumatori ed altri pubblici), mentre in base ai contenuti, essa si può distinguere in:
 -commerciale: volta ad influenzare le percezioni di valore o di sacrificio da parte di clienti finali o intermedi (trade)
-istituzionale, volta ad influenzare le percezioni di molteplici pubblici (interni ed esterni) circa l'impresa nel suo complesso, i suoi valori, la sua mission. Essa risulta particolarmente importante e delicata in momenti di crisi aziendale. 
-gestionale volta a migliorare le relazioni con i soggetti direttamente o indirettamente coinvolti nella gestione d'impresa, in modo da creare allineamento e commitment (es.: annual report, house organ)

-economico-finanziaria: volta a migliorare le relazioni con i portatori di risorsee di interesse (azionisti, lavoratori, società di rating, ecc.), esplicitando aspetti patrimoniali, reddituali e finanziari dell'impresa, nonché gli andamenti auspicati e/o previsti. I processi di comunicazione presentano una struttura tipica, che comprende i seguenti elementi:

-l'emittente è il soggetto che decide i contenuti della comunicazione, le linee guida per chi si occuperà di dar vita materialmente al messaggio, sulla base degli obiettivi perseguiti. L'emittente dovrebbe quindi essere l'impresa, anche se spesso (soprattutto nelle imprese minori, o comunque in quelle meno managerializzate) questo principio viene disatteso, lasciando alle agenzie di comunicazione il compi to di immaginarsi l'ottimo per il cliente, senza una necessaria conoscenza degli aspetti profondi alla base del messaggio da veicolare". Il risultato è rappresentato  da campagne di comunicazione spesso "belle da vedere", ma di scarso impatto rispetto alle reali necessità delle imprese o addirittura non coerenti con gli obiettivi di posizionamento del brand
-la codifica: è il processo attraverso cui il "comunicatore" (di solito un'agenzia esterna) dà forma al messaggio, mediante simboli, immagini, suoni, parole, in coerenza con le indicazioni fornite dall'emittente. Il messaggio deve risultare chiaro, comprensibile e accattivante per il pubblico cui è diretto;

- i mezzi (o media): sono i canali generici (es.: Radio. Tv, Stampa, ecc.) attraverso cui il messaggio viene veicolato ai destinatari e si distinguono in mezzi di massa (permettono di raggiungere in modo indistinto ampi pubblici) e mezzi non di massa (permettono di raggiungere in modo mirato e selettivo specifici pubblici, finanche nicchie): 

- i veicoli sono canali specifici scelti per veicolare il messaggi, nell’ambito di n certo media canale Tv, un certo quotidiano,  
-la decodifica: è il processo mentale attraverso cui chi riceve il messaggio lo interpreta (o, appunto, lo decodifica), conferendogli un significato;

- i destinatari sono coloro ai quali il messaggio è indirizzato. Bisogna tenere presente che non tutti quelli che ricevono il messaggio ("riceventi") corrispondono ai destinatari-target dell'impresa; questo perché è pressoché impossibile individuare veicoli comunicazionali che abbiano un bacino d'utenza ("audience") perfettamente corrispondente ai destinatari-target. Chiaramente, maggiore è la percentuale di destinatari-target all'interno dell'audience dei veicoli scelti, maggiore si rivela l'efficienza degli investimenti in comunicazione (si riduce il cosiddetto "costo a contatto"). Da questo punto di vista, il digitale offre importanti opportunità, perché consente di impostare delle campagne in modo molto specifico rispetto al bacino di utenza-obiettivo (si pensi, ad esempio, alle "campagne sponsorizzate" su Facebook);

- la risposta: è l'insieme delle reazioni dei destinatari a seguito della decodifica del messaggio (es.: richiesta di informazioni sul prodotto o di una prova dello stesso);

- il feed-back è quella parte delle reazioni dei destinatari che l'emittente è in grado di conoscere, il che permette anche di misurare i ritorni della comunicazione. Non sempre le risposte sono facilmente misurabili e si traducono automaticamente in feed-back consistenti, per i quali possono rendersi necessarie apposite indagini di mercato. Se, ad esempio, si realizza una campagna di comunicazione con l'obiet tivo di incrementare il tasso di "prossimità" e di simpatia del brand (si pensi ai ripetuti tentativi in tal senso di McDonald's negli ultimi anni sul mercato italiano),
per ottenere un t feed-back adeguato bisognerà necessariamente realizzare indagini di mercato ad hoc; viceversa, se si realizza una campagna per spingere una certa percentuale del target-group (si consideri un produttore di automobili) a recarsi presso i punti vendita (in ipotesi, per visionare un nuovo modello), sarà più agevole effettuare la suddetta misurazione, ad esempio mediante i dispositivi conta-persone che possono essere installati presso gli store.

Vi sono alcune criticità da gestire per rendere ottimali i processi di comunica- zione. Innanzitutto, come premesso, l'emittente deve fornire al comunicatore indicazioni precise (e vincolanti) circa i destinatari del messaggio e le risposte ricercate. In aggiunta, egli dovrà interagire costantemente con il comunicatore (a maggior ragione nel caso sia un soggetto esterno), per verificare di essere costantemente allineati sul risultato finale del processo, in modo anche da poter realizzare eventuali interventi correttivi o migliorativi. 
Quanto al comunicatore, egli avrà alcune responsabilità specifiche:
- prima di effettuare la codifica, dovrà ricostruire il possibile processo di decodifica dei destinatari, in modo da optare per le migliori scelte creative, tali da incrementare l'efficacia del messaggio;

Questa dinamica, come approfondiremo di seguito, si modifica radicalmente con riferimento ai retai ler monomarca dove product brand e retail brand si sovrappongono. L'interazione tra "brand loyalty e store loyalty". L'analisi dei processi di interazione tra product brand e retail brand implica la considerazione dei fenomeni di "brand loyalty e store loyalty" e che in questa sede acquisiscono il significato di product brand loyalty e di retail brand loyalty. Il tema della loyalty ha assunto un rilievo nei mercati a basso tasso di crescita e in virtù del fatto che la relazione con i clienti diviene generalmente più profittevole col trascorrere del tempo. 
Si può sostenere che la product (brand) loyalty sia quella fedeltà mani-festata dai clienti nei confronti di un certo product brand mentre la store (retail brand) loyaty sia legata alla scelta di un particolare punto vendita effettuata dal cliente. 
Ciò detto, ed in virtù della mutua influenza che sussiste tra retail brand e product brand, store loyalty e brand loyalty non devono essere considerate esclusivamente in un'ottica contrapposta in effetti le due fedeltà non implicano necessariamente un reciproco contrasto ma anzi manifestano livelli di "integrazione". A favore di questa interpretazione sussistono due ordini di ragioni: la prima riguarda i caratteri costitutivi della fedeltà al punto vendita che. pur arricchendosi di contenuti, e ancora fortemente determinata dalla capacità di una superficie commerciale di offrire quei prodotti e quelle marche verso le quali il cliente manifesta maggiore propensione d'acquisto; la seconda ragione, in modo complementare alla prima, deriva dal fatto che la brand experience si realizza per larga parte "in store". In tal senso, si deve considerare come la relazione tra brand loyalty e store loyalty divenga sempre più stretta: questo accade perché, nella prospettiva esperienziale, product brand e retail brand si configurano come un unico conte- nitore dei caratteri distintivi ed emozionali dell'offerta dell'impresa, siano essi ti- conducibili ad uno specifico prodotto o al punto vendita.
Percorsi di vertical branding. 
Dall'osservazione delle condotte competitive delle imprese (in particolare quelle di abbigliamento) si nota come numerose imprese industriali ed altrettanti retailer cerchino di presidiare più livelli della filiera, ponendo in essere percorsi di integrazione verticale. In particolare, questa dinamica vede da un lato imprese industriali impegnate ad aprire punti vendita monomarca (di proprietà, in franchising o in altre forme ad esso assimilabili), attraverso i quali commercializzare i propri product brand, e, dall'altro lato, i retailer impegnati nella creazione di private labels da inserire nell'assortimento dei propri punti vendita. Sulla scorta di queste dinamiche, ci sembra utile fare riferimento al concetto di "Vertical Brand" che in prima istanza può essere inteso come l'intersezione tra product brand e retail brand. La nozione di Vertical Brand è riconducibile alla capacità di ciascun attore, impresa a matrice industriale o retailer, di sviluppare un posizionamento competitivo basato sul controllo di ambedue le declinazioni di brand (Product e Retail brand) e sulla possibilità di deciderne il livello ottimale di integrazione, La strategia di sviluppo di una Vertical Brand punta a generare una esperienza complessiva ed integrata della marca veicolata dal prodotto, dalla comunicazione a verso i media, dal punto vendita. In altre parole, i pubblici a cui si rivolge l'impresa sperimentano una moltiplicazione delle occasioni cognitive, emozionali e comportamentali derivanti da quel brand che possiede sia una componente di "prodotto che una di "insegna". La possibilità di generare una brand experience efficace dipende in larga parte dalla capacità delle imprese di armonizzare la strategia di marca con quelle di comunicazione e di distribuzione che trovano, a loro volta, nel vendita la piattaforma di relazione più efficace.

||3. LE POLITICHE DI COMUNICAZIONE||

||3.1. STRUTTURA E CRITICITÀ DEI PROCESSI DI COMUNICAZIONE||

La comunicazione ha un ruolo centrale nell'ambito del trasferimento del valore come fonte privilegiata di segnali di valore per il consumatore. Le politiche di comunicazione sono principalmente finalizzate a:
 -far conoscere il prodotto, il brand e l'impresa (interventi sulla sfera cognitiva del consumatore, per generare notorietà): 
-differenziare il prodotto e la marca (interventi sulla sfera degli atteggiamenti del consumatore); 
-spingere alla prova, all'acquisto, al riacquisto del prodotto (interventi sulla sfera dei comportamenti di consumo). Gli effetti ricercati con la comunicazione sono quindi:
- lo stimolo della domanda e lo sviluppo delle vendite: - la riduzione dell'elasticità della domanda al prezzo e l'incremento della fedeltà del consumatore:
-lo sviluppo di barriere verso i competitor.

La comunicazione, quindi, è in molti casi vitale, soprattutto quando sul mercato notorietà, immagine di marca e presidio ampio e sistematico dei canali risultino fattori critici di successo. Essa, però, non deve essere confusa con il marketing (co- me spesso accade nella pratica, soprattutto nelle imprese minori), bensì deve rap- presentare uno degli strumenti per dare concretezza alle scelte di tipo strategico, con particolare riguardo al posizionamento del prodotto e della marca. 
In questo senso, è anche importante, come vedremo, che l'azienda non pensi di poter semplicemente demandare lo sforzo comunicazionale a soggetti esterni (agenzie specializzate), a maggior ragione oggi, con l'avanzare deciso del digitale, che disegna un terreno di gioco completamente nuovo, fatto di relazioni sistematiche e possibilmente autentiche con la domanda.

In questi ultimi anni, lo scenario della comunicazione è profondamente muta to ed è tuttora in evoluzione, con la saturazione di molti canali canonici di comunicazione, con la maggiore resistenza da parte dei consumatori (per vari motivi, dalla diffidenza alla banalizzazione degli acquisti) ai messaggi veicolari dalle imprese (con il rischio di insoddisfacenti ritorni), ma anche con la disponibilità di nuovi strumenti, canali e modalità di contatto con il mercato, in primis collegati alla diffusione delle ICT, In base alla tipologia di destinatari cui è rivolta, la comunicazione può essere in terna (verso i dipendenti) o esterna (verso consumatori ed altri pubblici), mentre in base ai contenuti, essa si può distinguere in:
 -commerciale: volta ad influenzare le percezioni di valore o di sacrificio da parte di clienti finali o intermedi (trade)
-istituzionale, volta ad influenzare le percezioni di molteplici pubblici (interni ed esterni) circa l'impresa nel suo complesso, i suoi valori, la sua mission. Essa risulta particolarmente importante e delicata in momenti di crisi aziendale. 
-gestionale volta a migliorare le relazioni con i soggetti direttamente o indirettamente coinvolti nella gestione d'impresa, in modo da creare allineamento e commitment (es.: annual report, house organ)

-economico-finanziaria: volta a migliorare le relazioni con i portatori di risorsee di interesse (azionisti, lavoratori, società di rating, ecc.), esplicitando aspetti patrimoniali, reddituali e finanziari dell'impresa, nonché gli andamenti auspicati e/o previsti. I processi di comunicazione presentano una struttura tipica, che comprende i seguenti elementi:

-l'emittente è il soggetto che decide i contenuti della comunicazione, le linee guida per chi si occuperà di dar vita materialmente al messaggio, sulla base degli obiettivi perseguiti. L'emittente dovrebbe quindi essere l'impresa, anche se spesso (soprattutto nelle imprese minori, o comunque in quelle meno managerializzate) questo principio viene disatteso, lasciando alle agenzie di comunicazione il compi to di immaginarsi l'ottimo per il cliente, senza una necessaria conoscenza degli aspetti profondi alla base del messaggio da veicolare". Il risultato è rappresentato  da campagne di comunicazione spesso "belle da vedere", ma di scarso impatto rispetto alle reali necessità delle imprese o addirittura non coerenti con gli obiettivi di posizionamento del brand
-la codifica: è il processo attraverso cui il "comunicatore" (di solito un'agenzia esterna) dà forma al messaggio, mediante simboli, immagini, suoni, parole, in coerenza con le indicazioni fornite dall'emittente. Il messaggio deve risultare chiaro, comprensibile e accattivante per il pubblico cui è diretto;

- i mezzi (o media): sono i canali generici (es.: Radio. Tv, Stampa, ecc.) attraverso cui il messaggio viene veicolato ai destinatari e si distinguono in mezzi di massa (permettono di raggiungere in modo indistinto ampi pubblici) e mezzi non di massa (permettono di raggiungere in modo mirato e selettivo specifici pubblici, finanche nicchie): 

- i veicoli sono canali specifici scelti per veicolare il messaggi, nell’ambito di n certo media canale Tv, un certo quotidiano,  
-la decodifica: è il processo mentale attraverso cui chi riceve il messaggio lo interpreta (o, appunto, lo decodifica), conferendogli un significato;

- i destinatari sono coloro ai quali il messaggio è indirizzato. Bisogna tenere presente che non tutti quelli che ricevono il messaggio ("riceventi") corrispondono ai destinatari-target dell'impresa; questo perché è pressoché impossibile individuare veicoli comunicazionali che abbiano un bacino d'utenza ("audience") perfettamente corrispondente ai destinatari-target. Chiaramente, maggiore è la percentuale di destinatari-target all'interno dell'audience dei veicoli scelti, maggiore si rivela l'efficienza degli investimenti in comunicazione (si riduce il cosiddetto "costo a contatto"). Da questo punto di vista, il digitale offre importanti opportunità, perché consente di impostare delle campagne in modo molto specifico rispetto al bacino di utenza-obiettivo (si pensi, ad esempio, alle "campagne sponsorizzate" su Facebook);

- la risposta: è l'insieme delle reazioni dei destinatari a seguito della decodifica del messaggio (es.: richiesta di informazioni sul prodotto o di una prova dello stesso);

- il feed-back è quella parte delle reazioni dei destinatari che l'emittente è in grado di conoscere, il che permette anche di misurare i ritorni della comunicazione. Non sempre le risposte sono facilmente misurabili e si traducono automaticamente in feed-back consistenti, per i quali possono rendersi necessarie apposite indagini di mercato. Se, ad esempio, si realizza una campagna di comunicazione con l'obiet tivo di incrementare il tasso di "prossimità" e di simpatia del brand (si pensi ai ripetuti tentativi in tal senso di McDonald's negli ultimi anni sul mercato italiano),
per ottenere un t feed-back adeguato bisognerà necessariamente realizzare indagini di mercato ad hoc; viceversa, se si realizza una campagna per spingere una certa percentuale del target-group (si consideri un produttore di automobili) a recarsi presso i punti vendita (in ipotesi, per visionare un nuovo modello), sarà più agevole effettuare la suddetta misurazione, ad esempio mediante i dispositivi conta-persone che possono essere installati presso gli store.

Vi sono alcune criticità da gestire per rendere ottimali i processi di comunica- zione. Innanzitutto, come premesso, l'emittente deve fornire al comunicatore indicazioni precise (e vincolanti) circa i destinatari del messaggio e le risposte ricercate. In aggiunta, egli dovrà interagire costantemente con il comunicatore (a maggior ragione nel caso sia un soggetto esterno), per verificare di essere costantemente allineati sul risultato finale del processo, in modo anche da poter realizzare eventuali interventi correttivi o migliorativi. 
Quanto al comunicatore, egli avrà alcune responsabilità specifiche:
- prima di effettuare la codifica, dovrà ricostruire il possibile processo di decodifica dei destinatari, in modo da optare per le migliori scelte creative, tali da incrementare l'efficacia del messaggio;
- nella scelta di media e veicoli di comunicazione, dovrà cercare di ottimizzare il rapporto fra bacino di utenza e destinatari della comunicazione, in modo da massimizzare l'efficienza dell'investimento; 
- ancora nella scelta dei media, dovrà verificare la coerenza fra le loro caratteristiche tecniche (cosa consentono/non consentono di fare in termini di comunicazione) e le modalità di codifica del messaggio;
- infine, dovrà effettuare pre-test sull'efficacia comunicazionale delle iniziative, in base a contenuti della comunicazione, modalità di codifica e caratteristiche dei mezzi di comunicazione scelti, per capire se e come intervenite con delle modifiche prima di diffondere ufficialmente il messaggio.

Seleccione la categoría que mejor describa el resultado de la llamada en términos de programación de servicios y/o acuerdos de citas/citas.

Categoría 1: Si el cliente programa una cita para un tiempo específico o acuerda en llegar dentro de una hora o menos. Por ejemplo, ‘Puedo programar una cita para el lunes a las 9:00 AM’ o ‘Llegaré allí en 30 minutos para una cita’.

Categoría 2: Si el cliente llega sin cita previa o acuerda un tiempo aproximado de llegada que excede una hora o acuerda una posible visita o cita de manera vaga. Por ejemplo, ‘Podría estar allí en algún momento esta tarde’ o ‘Estoy pensando en traer mi automóvil para una revisión, tal vez lo haga esta semana’.

Categoría 3: Si el cliente pregunta sobre la disponibilidad de citas o servicios y se habla sobre una cita o visita pero no se confirma. Por ejemplo, ‘¿Tienen horarios disponibles para un cambio de aceite?’ o ‘Estoy interesado en un servicio, ¿podrían darme más detalles?’

Categoría 4: Si el cliente solo hace preguntas sobre el servicio sin pedir una cita. Por ejemplo, ‘¿Cuáles son los servicios que ofrecen?’

Categoría 5: Si el cliente ya tiene una cita programada o discute una cita ya existente. Por ejemplo, ‘Necesito cambiar la fecha de mi cita para otra semana’.

Categoría 6: Si el cliente pregunta acerca del estado del vehículo mientras está siendo reparado o solicita servicios adicionales durante el tiempo que ya está siendo reparado. Por ejemplo, ‘¿Cómo va el trabajo en mi vehículo? ¿Tengo que arreglar algo más?’

Categoría 7: Si la llamada es una conversación general no relacionada con ninguna cita o servicio programado, si el cliente pregunta acerca de las partes solamente sin mencionar servicios o si el servicio requerido no es ofrecido. Por ejemplo, ‘¿Tienen esta pieza en stock?’ o ‘¿Puedo comprar una batería para mi auto aquí?’

Categoría 8: Si no hay comunicación con un agente calificado. Por ejemplo, si la llamada se cortó antes de hablar con un representante o si se mantuvieron en espera durante mucho tiempo sin respuesta.

Given the transcript of a phone call between a customer and a service center, classify the call according to the following categories:

Helpful information:
Qualified agent: An employee that is able to assist a caller with his or her inquiry. The qualified employee may at times need to call back in order to provide an answer or solution. As long as the same employee is the one intending to return the call, it is still considered connected.
Unqualified agent: An employee that is not able to assist the caller with his or her inquiry. A caller may reach an unqualified employee and hold a conversation, but it is not considered a connected call unless the caller is connected to someone who can assist him or her with their inquiry.
Appointment opportunity: Connected calls about potential maintenance or repair service(s) the shop can perform, repair or installation of a part that the shop can perform, or confirmed open recalls that the service shop can perform.
Service opportunities include but are not limited to:
Oil changes
Fluid flushes
Key programming / key cutting / key battery replacement
Part installation
Tire installation
Battery installation
Car detailing
Call types that should NOT be considered service:
Body work or collision repair
Car washes
Finance, sales, etc.
Interactive systems and auto-attendants: Calls handled by an interactive system or auto-attendant will sound like interactive recordings that ask questions or request information and require the caller to interact by making phone selections. When a call is successfully handled by an interactive system or auto-attendant it should be considered a connected call, and proper review selections should be made according to the content and outcome of the call. When a caller leaves a call back number with the interactive system, instead of successfully handling their inquiry or need, then the call should be considered not connected.
Reminders:
Calls in this category need to be reviewed based on this category's instructions. Overview instructions for other appointment related categories do not apply to this category.
The service appointment time should be considered the time the vehicle can be serviced.
Here are the options:
Option 1. Specific appointment or walk-in time / range within 1 hour
Caller agrees to an appointment with a specific date and time.
Example call - Caller: "I need a tune-up."// Receptionist or agent: "We can fit you in at 11:45 tomorrow morning."// Caller: "Perfect. I'll see you then!"// Call ends.
Caller approximates a loose time range, but the agent puts down a firm time for the appointment. In these instances, the agent’s statement trumps the caller's.
Example - Caller: "I can be there between 2:00 and 4:00." // Agent: "I'll put you down for 3:00, and then if you show up a little earlier or later, that's fine."
Caller agrees to an appointment with a specific date and time but plans to drop the vehicle off before the scheduled appointment.
Example call - Caller: "I need an oil change."// Agent: "I will schedule you for 10:00 AM tomorrow."// Caller: "Can I drop my car off before my appointment?" // Agent: "Yes, you can drop your car off any time, and just leave your keys in the drop box."// Caller: "Great, thanks!" // Call ends.
Caller agrees to an approximate time within a 1 hour time range because they are able to be serviced at the time of arrival.
A walk-in time within an hour range, for a vehicle that can be serviced immediately, should be considered a specific appointment time. This is true because, even if an appointment is not put on the schedule, the service shop has an expected arrival time for the caller and the service can be completed at that arrival time.
Example call - Caller: "I need to get my brakes repaired. Do you have any openings today?"// Agent: "You can come in now if you'd like"// Caller: "Great! I'll be there in half an hour." // Call ends.
Example call - Caller: "My car is being towed there right now and should be there in about 20 minutes. Can it be looked at right away?" // Agent: "Yeah, that's no problem. We'll look at it as soon as it arrives."
Caller agrees to an approximate time of "around 1 hour".
Caller discusses an existing appointment and agrees to a new appointment during the same call.
Example call - Caller: "I'm checking on the status of my car that's in service, and I also wanted to know if I could bring my wife's car in for an oil change."// Agent: "Your car is ready to be picked up, we can get your wife's car in at 4:00 if that time works for you."// Caller: "That works. We'll be there at 4:00."
Option 2. Unscheduled walk-in or loose appointment time / range exceeding 1 hour
Caller gives a vague agreement to possibly come in.
Example call - Caller: Do you have availability tomorrow morning. // Agent: "Yes, we're pretty open all morning." // Caller: "Okay, I may drop it off in the morning." // Call ends.
Caller agrees to come in but approximates a time range that exceeds 1 hour.
Example call - Caller: "I'll be there in about 2 hours."
Caller agrees to come in before or after a specific time.
Example call - Caller: "I can be there sometime before 4:00 PM."
In this example, the caller could be there anytime before 4:00, making this a loose appointment time.
Example call - Caller: "I won't be able to get there until after 5:00."
In this example, the caller could be there anytime after 5:00.
Receptionist or agent tells the caller that it is first come, first served and the caller says "OK."
Example call - Caller: "Do I need an appointment for an oil change?"// Receptionist or agent: "It is first come, first served."// Caller acknowledges this and the call ends.
Caller agrees to be an unscheduled walk-in.
Example call - Caller - "Do you accept walk-ins?" // Agent: "We'll be accepting walk-ins all day Saturday." // Caller: "I'll be there sometime Saturday then!"
Caller agrees to come in at a certain time but no appointment time is guaranteed.
A walk-in time within an hour range, that can be serviced immediately, is a specific appointment time. However, a specific walk-in time with no specific service time cannot be considered a specific appointment, because the vehicle cannot be serviced immediately upon arrival. In the following example, the caller gives a specific arrival time, but the service time cannot be set for a specific time. Thus, it is a soft appointment time.
Example call - Caller: "I need to get my car serviced as soon as possible." // Agent: "We're all booked through the whole week." // Caller: "Can I just come in and have my car serviced between other appointments?" // Agent: "You can come in and possibly have your car serviced if they have time, but we cannot guarantee a service time and you may be here for a few hours." // Caller: "I'll just get there when you open tomorrow at 8:00, and I'll wait."
Caller is having his or her vehicle towed in but no appointment time is guaranteed.
Receptionist or agent tells the caller that no appointment is necessary, they can just show up.
Example call - Caller: "Can I get my tire rotated today?" // Receptionist or agent: "Absolutely. You don't need an appointment. Just come on in."// Caller acknowledges this and the call ends.
The time of the visit or walk-in is for a window of time that exceeds 1 hour.

Programme a modifier:
Sub RepartitionProductions()
Dim wsF1 As Worksheet, wsF2 As Worksheet, wsInputPAC As Worksheet
Dim i As Long, j As Long, heure As Long
Dim demande As Double, puissanceRestante As Double
Dim puissanceMin As Double, puissanceMax As Double, pas As Double
Dim utilisation As Double, utilisationOptimale As Double

Set wsF1 = ThisWorkbook.Worksheets("f1")
Set wsF2 = ThisWorkbook.Worksheets("f2")
Set wsInputPAC = ThisWorkbook.Worksheets("input_PAC")
' Parcourir chaque heure de la feuille f2
For heure = 1 To wsF2.Cells(wsF2.Rows.Count, 1).End(xlUp).Row Step 1
    demande = wsF2.Cells(heure, 2).Value
    puissanceRestante = demande
    'Parcourir chaque production de la feuille f1
    For i = 1 To wsF1.Cells(wsF1.Rows.Count, 1).End(xlUp).Row Step 1
        puissanceMin = wsF1.Cells(i, 4).Value * wsF1.Cells(i, 2).Value
        puissanceMax = wsF1.Cells(i, 5).Value * wsF1.Cells(i, 2).Value

        ' Si la ligne est dans les lignes 7, 8 et 9
        If i >= 7 And i <= 9 Then
            ' Appliquer les coefficients de la feuille input_PAC aux lignes 7, 8 et 9
            puissanceMin = puissanceMin * wsInputPAC.Cells(heure, 13 + i - 6).Value
            puissanceMax = puissanceMax * wsInputPAC.Cells(heure, 13 + i - 6).Value
        End If
        
        pas = wsF1.Cells(i, 6).Value
        utilisationOptimale = 0
        ' Calculer le pourcentage d’utilisation optimal
        For utilisation = puissanceMin To puissanceMax Step pas
            If puissanceRestante - utilisation >= 0 Then
                utilisationOptimale = utilisation
            Else
                Exit For
            End If
        Next utilisation

        ' Enregistrer le pourcentage d’utilisation sur la feuille f2
        wsF2.Cells(heure, 2 + i).Value = utilisationOptimale / wsF1.Cells(i, 2).Value

        ' Vérifier si la valeur dépasse 1, alors la fixer à 1
        If wsF2.Cells(heure, 2 + i).Value > 1 Then
            wsF2.Cells(heure, 2 + i).Value = 1
        End If

        ' Mettre à jour la puissance restante
        puissanceRestante = puissanceRestante - utilisationOptimale
    Next i

    '  Si la puissance restante est négative, enregistrer “-” sur la feuille f2
    If puissanceRestante < 0 Then
    wsF2.Cells(heure, 2 + i).Value = “ - ”
    End If
Next heure
End Sub

1. Specific appointment or walk-in time/range within 1 hour (as-is)
2. Unscheduled walk-in or loose appointment time/range exceeding 1 hour (as-is)
3. Appointment requested/mentioned but not set (as-is)
4. No appointment, walk-in, or drop-off discussed (as-is)
5. Upcoming scheduled appointment - Caller discusses an existing appointment already scheduled for an upcoming time and/or date, including cancellations or rescheduling.

1. “Specific appointment or walk-in within 1 hour”

Introduction
A crucial aspect of food microbiology is Hazard Analysis, which entails locating and evaluating potential risks during the food manufacturing process. By implementing control measures that reduce or eliminate the risks associated with these hazards, hazard analysis aims to avoid foodborne diseases. There are certain steps that must be followed during any Hazard Analysis. Hazard Identification, characterization, risk assessment, risk management, monitoring, and verification are the steps that get followed to ensure food safety and quality. 
A common condiment called tomato ketchup is made of ripe tomatoes, vinegar, sugar, and spices. A thorough risk analysis of each step in the product's manufacture, processing, and packaging is carried out as part of a high priority to ensure the product's quality and safety. Chemical and microbiological risks that can appear during these stages are carefully considered. 
Each danger is classified according to its seriousness so that the potential risks can be understood better and addressed. High-risk individuals are denoted by the color red, medium-risk individuals by the color yellow, and low-risk individuals by the color green.
Overall, risk analysis is important to main the quality and safety of the food and reduce foodborne illnesses.

Table 1: Hazard Analysis for Tomato Ketchup Production with Hazard Category Ratings and Control Measures

Process Steps	Hazard 	Hazard Explanation	Hazard Category	Control Measures
Receiving and inspecting raw tomatoes	Presence of pathogens (mold or microorganisms) such as Salmonella	When making ketchup, receiving and examining fresh tomatoes poses a risk of mold contamination or the presence of dangerous bacteria. This is because soil, where tomatoes are cultivated, has the potential to harbor dangerous bacteria and fungi. These viruses can represent a serious health danger to consumers if they are permitted to contaminate raw tomatoes and then used to make ketchup.	Yellow (Medium risk)	Tomatoes should be purchased from reputable vendors who follow good agricultural and handling procedures. Incoming tomato lots should also be routinely inspected and sampled using visual inspection and microbial testing. Finally, storage areas should be kept at a consistent temperature (4 to 10°C) and kept clean.
Raw material handling and storage	Contamination with heavy metals, pesticides and mycotoxins	The risk of pesticide, heavy metal, and/or mycotoxin contamination during the preparation of ketchup is connected to the use of sugar, vinegar, and spices. These chemicals can be made from raw sources that include potentially dangerous elements that could endanger human health. While mycotoxins can be created by fungi that grow on crops during storage or transportation, pesticides and heavy metals can enter the food chain via industrial or agricultural sources. These pollutants have the potential to impair the safety and quality of the ketchup if they are not found and eliminated before processing.	Yellow (Medium risk)	Get raw materials from reputable vendors and regularly test them for contamination.
Washing, sorting and grading	Contaminants or cross-contamination 	The risk of contamination or cross-contamination throughout the ketchup production process is connected to washing, sorting, and grading. Due to dirty equipment or improper handling procedures, contaminants including dirt, debris, or harmful microbes may be introduced throughout these processes. If the same tools and utensils are used for various batches of ketchup without being properly cleaned and sanitised, cross-contamination may result. This may lead to the transmission of undesirable chemicals, allergies, or dangerous bacteria to the ketchup, raising the possibility of consumer health hazards.	Green (low risk)	Maintain proper sanitation of the equipment and utensils using periodic cleaning and sanitising procedures; remove rotten or damaged tomatoes during sorting and grading to reduce microbial load; practise good personal hygiene by production staff, including handwashing, using gloves, and dressing appropriately.
Cutting and chopping	Cross-contamination (cutting equipment)	Cross-contamination from cutting instruments is the risk connected to cutting and chopping during the preparation of ketchup. If the cutting and chopping equipment is not thoroughly cleaned and sanitised or if there is cross-contamination between batches, bacteria or other dangerous germs may be introduced to the ketchup throughout the process. This may result in the ketchup becoming contaminated with germs, raising the danger of customers contracting a foodborne illness.	Yellow (medium risk)	Use proper handling and hygiene techniques during this process, such as avoiding the use of the same equipment for different allergens without cleaning, and regularly clean and sanitise cutting equipment using approved chemicals and adhering to the manufacturer's recommendations. Ensure the proper maintenance of equipment to prevent the buildup of foreign materials.
Heating (80 to 90 degrees) and cooking	Insufficient heating or cooking results in under processed ketchup with a chance of pathogenic bacteria surviving.	The risk of inadequate heating or cooking during the preparation of ketchup is that it will result in under-processed ketchup with a chance of harmful bacteria surviving. To get rid of any potentially hazardous germs in the ketchup, heat treatment is crucial. These microorganisms may survive and remain in the final product if the required heating and cooking temperatures are not reached or are not maintained consistently, potentially resulting in consumer sickness.	Red (high risk)	To ensure a constant cooking temperature, use automated cookers equipped with temperature sensors; periodically check and record the temperature to keep a cooking log; and create and adhere to standard operating procedures (SOPs) for cooking time and temperature.
Mixing (sugar, vinegar, and spices)	Cross-contamination with allergens (gluten or mustard)	To make the finished ketchup product, the cooked tomato mixture is mixed with sugar, vinegar, and spices. The possibility of cross-contamination with allergies, such as mustard or gluten, or other chemical dangers is one risk connected to this procedure.

If mixing tools, containers, or utensils have previously come into touch with allergen-containing substances without being thoroughly cleaned, cross-contamination may result. For people with allergies or sensitivities, this poses a danger and, when consumed, may result in mild or serious adverse responses.	Yellow (medium risk)	Implement an allergen management programme, which should include proper allergen handling, labelling, and storage. You should also clean and sanitise equipment between batches using the right cleaning supplies and techniques. Finally, you should use the right internal training and communication to ensure that allergen controls are understood and followed.
Homogenization, pasteurization, and consistency	Insufficient pasteurization temperature or uniformity, which allows thermophilic microbes to survive and produce foodborne illnesses like Bacillus or Clostridium.	Inadequate pasteurization temperature or consistency, which can allow thermophilic bacteria like Bacillus or Clostridium to survive and cause foodborne diseases, is a risk linked with homogenization, pasteurisation (95 to 100° C), and consistency during the preparation of ketchup. The removal of potentially hazardous germs from ketchup through pasteurisation is necessary, although thermophilic bacteria have been known to withstand this process if the temperature or consistency aren't right. These germs could live and stay in the finished product if the ketchup is not cooked to the proper temperatures or at regular intervals, potentially making consumers sick.	Red (high risk)	Establish validated critical control points (CCPs) for consistency, pasteurisation temperatures, and homogenization (e.g., minimum 12° Brix for ketchup); routinely track and record process parameters (e.g., with the aid of digital logging devices); validate and periodically confirm the effectiveness of the pasteurisation process.



Sampling and analysis	False-negative results for pathogen detection or inaccurate allergen quantification are examples of improper sampling or analysis that leads in wrong assessment of product safety and quality.	Inaccurate sampling or analysis that results in an incorrect assessment of the product's safety and quality is the risk connected with sampling and analysis during the production of ketchup. This may lead to erroneous allergen quantification or false-negative results for pathogen detection. To ensure that a ketchup product satisfies safety and quality criteria, sampling and analysis are essential. However if the sampling or analysis is not done correctly, it could produce false results that lead to incorrect assessments of the product's quality or safety. For instance, significant foodborne infections might result if a contaminated batch of ketchup is wrongly deemed safe.	Yellow (medium risk)	Establish a routine sampling schedule using a representative and random methodology; use approved equipment and techniques for analysis (such as ISO, AOAC, or FDA methods); instruct staff on sampling and testing procedures; and take part in proficiency testing schemes or other external quality assurance initiatives.
Cooling (below 5 degrees Celsius) 	Lack of cooling causes spoiling or the growth of harmful microbes like Listeria monocytogenes or Clostridium perfringens.	Inadequate cooling during the ketchup-making process poses a risk of spoiling or the growth of harmful microbes like Clostridium perfringens or Listeria monocytogenes. In order to keep germs from growing and potentially compromising the safety and quality of the ketchup, cooling is a crucial step. When ketchup is not properly and quickly chilled, it can provide the perfect environment for hazardous organisms to flourish. Foodborne infections may result from product spoilage or the proliferation of harmful bacteria as a result of this.	Yellow (medium risk)	Make sure that cooling equipment (such as fast chillers or ice jackets) is properly maintained and working; if necessary, alter the chilling process based on the product type or batch size. Monitor and control cooling temperatures using digital thermometers or temperature data recorders.
Filling and packaging	environmental or packaging contamination brought on by pests, extraneous objects, or leftover cleaning product residue.	Contamination from the environment or packing materials, such as insects, foreign objects, or leftovers from cleaning agents, poses a risk during filling and packaging during the preparation of ketchup. Ketchup can become contaminated by the environment or packaging materials during the filling and packaging process, posing major dangers to consumer health and safety. Insects or foreign objects in the plant area, as well as cleaning chemical residues on packaging materials like containers, lids, and seals, can all be sources of contamination.	Green (low risk)	Use automatic CIP (clean-in-place) systems to ensure that filling and packaging equipment is cleaned and sanitized correctly; use visual product inspection to find flaws or contaminants; use packaging materials that are suitable for use with food, such as BPA-free plastics; and adhere to regulatory requirements for material safety.
Storage	due to poor storage circumstances, such as high humidity, temperature swings, or extended storage times, mould or spoiling organisms might grow.	The risk involved with storage during the preparation of ketchup is the development of mould or spoiling organisms as a result of poor storage practises. Once the ketchup has been packaged, safe storage practises are essential to preserving the product's quality and safety. When ketchup is kept at high humidity levels, temperature swings or extended storage times may cause mould or spoilage organisms to thrive, which may compromise the product's safety and quality. It is possible for ketchup to become contaminated with these dangerous germs, which could result in a foodborne illness.	Yellow (medium risk)	In order to prevent product ageing, implement temperature and humidity controls in storage areas (e.g., keeping the temperature below 25° C and the relative humidity below 65%); regularly check and maintain storage conditions using digital sensors or data loggers; and adhere to FIFO (first-in, first-out) or FEFO (first-expired, first-out) inventory management practises.
Distribution	Damage or contamination that occurs during shipment, such as leaks, packing being crushed, or being pierced by insects or sharp items.	Distribution risks during ketchup manufacture include transportation damage or contamination, such as leaks, packaging damage from crushing, or penetration by insects or sharp things. May be exposed to dangers like vibrations or impacts, harsh weather, or other elements during transit that could affect the product's quality and safety. The materials used for packing could be harmed, allowing contamination from things like insects, dust, or dirt. Moreover, sharp items may cut through the packing, causing ketchup to flow out and perhaps contaminate other foods.	Green (low risk)	Implement traceability protocols for product tracking using barcodes, QR codes, or RFID tags to facilitate recalls or investigations if necessary. Use appropriate packaging materials and designs to ensure product integrity, such as robust secondary and tertiary packaging, tamper-evident seals, or shrink wraps.
