The High Priest died before work on the Great Sun Pyramid was completed, but the ageing Pharoah leant on his gnarled walking stick and admired his creation from the hill.

In the valley, thousands of slaves laboured to place the final capstone on the pyramid, scurrying up and down the scaffolding that completely covered one face of the monolithic structure. All were unaware of being watched by their Pharoah who, looking down from the hillside, regarded them with the same fascination that one might watch a swarm of ants building a nest.

It was early evening by the time the capstone reached the summit of the pyramid; the largest single stone in the entire structure. The Pharoah, looking out across the rapidly darkening valley, made a mental note of the cost of this project. One tenth of the entire Royal reserves had gone towards it along with the lives of seven men, not to mention countless slaves.

A thunderclap echoed across the valley. Everywhere, people stopped and turned. The capstone had dropped neatly into its carved bed at the apex of the pyramid. The work was done.

The Pharoah smiled contentedly, knowing that his shrine was complete. He got up, rubbing his chest whilst thinking to himself that the banquet he had enjoyed earlier in the day could have been a little less rich.

Two paces forward, he stumbled and fell. The blood clot that had passed unnoticed through his heart had reached his brain. The tranquil red sunset started to darken as the sun disappeared behind the western ranges.

The first Dark Age had begun...

Chapter 3

The dank old library looked as though it hadn't seen a duster for a month or two. Anyone with hay fever or of a house-proud nature would not have lasted five minutes in there. Albert 'Tiny' Dorliss, however, was made of sterner stuff. Looking at him, though, you probably would not have believed it. His nickname, far from being sarcastic, was apt almost to the point of being embarrassing. His horn-rimmed spectacles only added to his academic looks. This impression was very difficult to shake, unless you happened to wander down to the local gym when, on a Wednesday night, 'Tiny' Dorliss would be seen knocking seven bells out of someone twice his size in a boxing ring. Somehow, the image of one of England's leading theoretical Egyptologists also being one of its finest amateur flyweights seems somehow slightly incongruous.

This morning, as most mornings, he was sat at his small, leather-topped desk in the Egyptian section, the dustiest part of the library. Egypt had not really been fashionable for serious research since the late 1880's. Fifty years of neglect meant quite a lot of dust.

'Morning, Tiny. Found anything interesting lately?' I enquired.

'Hello.' He pushed his glasses up his nose with one finger and studied me. 'Where on earth have you been? I've been trying to contact you for weeks.'

'Well, you know how it is.' I shrugged. 'One minute I'm sitting at home; the next, I'm being asked by the British Museum to go to South America and, I might add, get paid for the priviledge.'

'You're incorrigible. Will you never learn? Money this, money that all the time. You never apply yourself to your full potential. Anyway, yes I have.'

'Have what?'

'Oh, come on. Pay attention. Yes, I have found something interesting. That's the reason behind me trying to contact you for the past week.'

'If this is going to be another of your damn fool trips to strange temples with supernatural powers and all that sort of thing, then you can count me out right now.'

'I don't believe in supernatural mumbo-jumbo about ancient curses. It only applies to superstitious primitives who...'

'All right, I get your point. But if you had been there the last time, I am willing to bet that even your unflappable certainty would have taken a nasty knock.' I shook my finger at him to emphasize my last point, but it did no good.

'I've translated a previously unknown fragment of papyrus from the last years of the Pharoah period of Egyptian history, discovered in the palace of the last Pharaoh before the empire was overrun. It was written in a dialectic variation of the private language used by the court astrologers...'

My attention began to wander. I could never keep up with Tiny once he started on language variations. I wouldn't know a dialect from a pidgin if it bit me on the nose. My mind started to drift.

'..and what it actually said was quite interesting. Apparently, the court astrologers had predicted the overthrow of their civilization and the rise of ours. They made some quite accurate guesses about us, you know.'

Guesses! There really is no convincing some people. 'They say that if we are not true worshippers of Ra, the Sun God, then they have set a trap for us which will wipe us all out. Something to do with the moon and the sun... I couldn't make out the rest of that part as there was a tear in the papyrus. It seems that the trap is a graded test, and that it swings both ways. If you succeed in..'

'Hold it one moment! What is this 'you' nonsense? Do you expect me to go back to Egypt at the drop of a hat after what happened the last time I was there? Surely you're not serious?'

'Think of the money if you succeed', he replied.

I thought of the money. I also thought of the curse. I returned my thoughts to the money.

'Okay, I'll go. What do I have to do?'

'There is a temple built into the top of a large pyramid. Although the river that it stood beside has now dried up, I have managed to find out where it was built.'

'So how do we stop the curse?'

'It's fairly simple really', he said. Liar, I thought. Nothing about this affair so far sounded simple. 'You just have to get to the temple, which is at the apex of the pyramid and destroy the trigger mechanism. It's a statue of some sort. It shouldn't be too difficult to spot. The records say that the room was built with the sole purpose of housing the statue only.'

I extracted myself from the buttoned leather armchair that had obviously seen better days and made to leave. 'Where are you going?' Tiny asked. 'You only just got here.'

'To pack. There's a total eclipse in Egypt in four days and it'll take at least three to get there so I'm going immediately. If what you say is true, we don't have much time before the curse takes effect. By the way, just what is the name of this place that I'm supposed to go to?'

Tiny told me the name of the nearest village. I paused at the door. 'And don't think that I'm only doing this for the money!'

He looked over the top of his glasses and raised a solitary eyebrow. 'The idea hadn't even entered my mind. Good luck.'

I grabbed my hat and coat from the doorman and ran out into the street, my mind overflowing with information and plans for the journey ahead. I hailed a taxi.

'Where to, Guv?'

'St. John's Road, please and as quickly as possible.'

As I sat back in my seat I was filled with excitement and dread in roughly equal amounts. After my last fiasco in Egypt, I had no doubt that the powers the Ancient Egyptian priesthood had at their disposal could quite easily bring about the sort of thing described in that papyrus. The taxi made a hasty U-turn in the street and lurched off to my destination.

Chapter 4

Shadows contrasted sharply with the almost white glare thrown up by the sand. I had long ago ceased to take any notice of the salty tang in my mouth as, unaccustomed as yet even to the so-called mild October heat, sweat enveloped my entire body. Clothes once crisply starched had long since wilted into a crumpled mass of cotton glued to my aching body. By the sight of it, my saddle had obviously seen better days and, judging by the bumps and jolts that jarred my spine, I had been correct in my initial misgivings.

I found myself becoming more and more uncomfortable as the journey wore on. Camels have never been my favourite mode of transport and nothing had happened in the past couple of hours that had brought about a change of mind. Still, I thought to myself, anything's better than walking. Then again, almost anything's better than riding a camel. I muttered oaths under my breath and forced a smile on the odd occasion that my camel driver bothered to look at his passenger. I began to regret ever having accepted this task. I tried to shut out my present surroundings by concentrating on the endless wealth with which I would be endowed if I were to succeed. The trouble was, the more I thought about it, the larger the 'if' seemed to become.

After what seemed an interminable ride, we finally arrived at Ankh-Arah village. A fairly typical Egyptian village, it consisted in the main of dry, dirt streets, square, whitewashed houses and a stone well in the main square.

I jumped clumsily from my mount and paid the camel driver his fare. Doing a quick calculation in my head, I came up with the same answer as when I started the journey. Twenty one shillings for a nineteen mile camel ride. Captive markets such as helpless English Archeologists obviously lend themselves to exploitation by the locals. At least I saved some face by getting off the camel without landing on my face, and that in itself probably lowered the price by sixpence or so.

The driver unstrapped my two cases and watched as they fell to the ground. Without any further ado, he wheeled about, spurred his camel and was gone, leaving me looking rather forlorn in a slowly settling cloud of dust. I retrieved my cases and went off in search of some accommodation.

It took me about twenty minutes to find the only inn in the village: a small sandstone building like all the others, with two bedrooms, a hole in the floor for a latrine and enough insect life to supply a museum. One of these was the owner, who charged in a similar vein to the camel driver, and only grudgingly showed me my room.

Although the straw-stuffed bed was lumpy and scratchy, I fell asleep almost immediately, the bed seeming like pure luxury compared to a camel's backside. I intended to make an early start the next morning in order to start my exploration of the pyramid which lay in the dried up river valley a few miles to the south of the village. That should at least give me a couple of hours before the eclipse. As I drifted off to sleep, I dreamily wished that I had remembered to bring an alarm clock.

I need not have worried. The innkeeper's cockerel woke me far too early in the morning for my liking. Any thoughts as to why the cockerel was still alive and crowing in a small village such as this were soon put to rest on looking out of the window. There wasn't enough meat on that bird for more than one or two scrawny sandwiches, let alone a proper meal, so I suppose the villagers put up with it out of pity. Silently cursing the multi-legged population of my bed, I dressed and packed my equipment for the day. In a sudden fit of self-reflection, I noted just how calmly I seemed to taking this matter. After all, the End of the World is not your usual run-of-the-mill problem. Panicking would have helped little in a situation such as this, so I resisted the urge to do so.

The sun was just creeping sleepily over the horizon as I left my room and turned south along the little-used track that ran towards the only airfield within twenty miles. The mechanic, who seemed to be the sole inhabitant of the entire place, showed me to the only aeroplane. Tiny had called ahead and arranged everything, so all I had to do was pay for it. Again.

It was a clapped-out Sopwith Camel. I didn't look too closely on my pre-flight inspection; to do so would have brought to my attention loose rigging wires, numerous oil leaks from within the engine bay, and more holes in the fabric than a tramp's jacket. As I climbed into the cockpit, I reflected that, in Egypt, you tended to find yourself traveling by Camel most of the time. The mechanic heaved on the propellor a couple of times before the engine slowly coughed itself to life, and he only just managed to jump clear of the blades as I rolled forward. I had never been what you would call an experienced aviator and that, coupled with the early hour, meant that things such as lack of wheel chocks were a minor inconvenience.

Still, he seemed unharmed and he gave me a friendly wave as I passed overhead. At least, I think it was friendly...

It was still early in the morning as I reached the pyramid. I was awed by the size of the task ahead of me; the pyramid was one of the largest that I had ever come across. All the other digs that I had been on previously were much smaller than this, and they had taken months of painstaking effort. I circled once or twice to find the best landing spot and, having decided that a strip of smooth-looking sand down one side of the pyramid looked suitable for putting the Camel down, I prepared to land.

Turning carefully onto the downwind leg I began the final checks. Dropping down to around three hundred feet, I throttled back and turned the mixture to fully rich. Flying parallel to the makeshift runway, I continued until I was level with the beginning of the strip. Gently banking the aircraft into a descending left turn, I put in a little bit of left rudder to balance out the Camel and throttled back slightly more. Thankful that there were no air pockets waiting to plummet the aircraft like a stone, I finally started to line up on my chosen landing spot.

The ground slowly came up to meet me and I throttled back completely and concentrated on keeping the aircraft level at about one or two feet off the ground. Gently trimming the aircraft to keep a slight nose up attitude as the speed scrubbed off, the Camel simply lost flying speed and lowered itself onto the sand. A quick flick of the rudder to compensate for a patch of rough sand that was attempting to upset the aircraft and I was down safely. I trundled to a halt and, on switching off the engine, I really began to feel the effect of three days continuous travelling. Slumped in my seat, it took all my energy to unbuckle the straps and extract myself from the cockpit. Pulling out my limited equipment that was wedged down deep within the cockpit, I jumped off the wing and felt the heat of the sand work its way through my boots.

I kept thinking that the task ahead was just too large to complete within the time available. However, no matter how corny it may sound, the fate of civilization really did rest fairly and squarely on my shoulders. I skirted around the base of the pyramid, searching for the door to the antechamber. The first test had begun...

They stopped their camels on top of the rise where, over three thousand years ago, the last of the Pharoahs had spent his final hour. Behind them, a tiny sliver of crescent moon moved immeasurably closer towards the golden disc of the sun.

The taller one spoke. 'Look.'

Together they watched with curiosity as a small figure worked its way, ant-like, around the base of the pyramid below them, stopping now and then to look more closely at the worn carvings. It disappeared out of sight around the corner. After a while, the two men tired of watching the blank face of the pyramid and, turning their camels, made their way back along the dusty track.

The moon took its first, tentative bite from the edge of the sun.

La bocca (o cavità orale) è delimitata superiormente dal palato (il cui scheletro è formato dalle ossa
mascellari e dall’osso palatino, sul bordo del quale è inserita l’arcata dentaria superiore,
costituita, nell’adulto, da 16 denti; lateralmente dalle guance, e inferiormente dalla mandibola
(nella quale è inserita l’arcata dentaria inferiore, anch’essa costituita, nell’adulto, da 16 denti)
e dalla lingua. La bocca è rivestita da un epitelio (mucosa orale), che, soprattutto in corrispondenza
della lingua, contiene particolari terminazioni nervose, le papille gustative, che percepiscono
i sapori dei cibi). Attorno a ciascun dente, la mucosa orale forma le gengive.
I denti sono gli organi più mineralizzati dell’organismo umano. Ciascun dente è inserito in una
cavità dell’osso mascellare o della mandibola detta alveolo dentale. In ciascun dente si distinguono
tre parti:
– la corona (la parte visibile del dente) che ha forma diversa a seconda del tipo di dente (appiattita
ed affilata negli incisivi; appuntita nei canini; allargata con diverse cuspidi nei premolari e nei
molari);
– il colletto, che forma la transizione tra corona e radice, attorno al quale la mucosa orale forma le
gengive;
– una o più radici, che si inseriscono nell’alveolo e sono ancorate alle sue pareti da legamenti di
tessuto connettivo.
I denti sono formati da dentina (o avorio), particolare tipo di tessuto osseo. Nella corona, la
dentina è rivestita da uno strato di smalto, particolare tessuto epiteliale molto resistente e mineralizzato,
mentre a livello del colletto e delle radici è rivestita da un altro tipo di tessuto osseo, detto cemento.
Nella dentina è presente una piccola cavità (cavità pulpale), che contiene la polpa del dente,
tessuto connettivo ricco di vasi sanguigni e di terminazioni nervose, e che si continua in un canalicolo
che percorre ciascuna delle radici (canale radicale). Il canalicolo sbocca nell’alveolo con un
piccolo foro, attraverso il quale penetrano nel dente i vasi sanguigni e i nervi.
Alla nascita, la bocca è priva di denti; la dentizione inizia (cioè i denti iniziano a spuntare) attorno
al 6°-8° mese di vita e porta alla comparsa dei 20 denti decidui (denti da latte). Questi sono gradualmente
sostituiti, a partire dal 6°-7° anno, dai 32 denti permanenti.

gonfiore in vicinanza dell’orecchio.). La produzione di saliva è continua, ma aumenta grandemente in seguito a stimoli

LA NUTRIZIONE UMANA. Per crescere e moltiplicarsi, ma anche solo per mantenersi, l’organismo umano, come tutti gli
esseri viventi, ha bisogno di materia e di energia: materia per costruire i composti che costituiscono
le sue cellule, energia sia per effettuare queste sintesi, sia per compiere gli altri tipi di lavoro
che i diversi organi e tessuti sono chiamati a svolgere. L’uomo è un organismo eterotrofo:
non è infatti capace di trasformare composti inorganici in composti organici, ma deve prelevare
dall’ambiente composti organici già sintetizzati da altri organismi, da cui trarre il materiale per
sintetizzare i propri componenti. L’uomo è anche un organismo chemiotrofo: i composti organici
prelevati dall’ambiente costituiscono infatti anche la fonte di energia per i suoi fabbisogni.
All’organismo sono necessari anche composti inorganici, quindi acqua e sali: questi vengono prelevati
come tali dall’ambiente e direttamente utilizzati. I composti organici ed inorganici prelevati
dall’ambiente sono gli alimenti di cui l’organismo si nutre e che, nel loro insieme, costituiscono
la dieta.
Per essere utilizzata, la miscela di composti diversi variamente strutturati, quindi organici: carboidrati,
lipidi, proteine, acidi nucleici, ed inorganici), che costituisce la dieta, deve anzitutto essere sminuzzata
ed omogeneizzata meccanicamente. D’altra parte essa è costituita in larghissima parte da molecole
complesse, spesso di grossissime dimensioni. Per divenire utilizzabili dall’organismo queste devono
venir scisse, cioè idrolizzate, nei composti più semplici che le costituiscono: i carboidrati , cioè oligo e polisaccaridi,
in monosaccaridi, i lipidi in acidi grassi e glicerolo, le proteine in amminoacidi, ecc. Solo
questi composti relativamente semplici possono essere assorbiti e distribuiti a tutto l’organismo. Il
processo di sminuzzamento e di idrolisi degli alimenti costituisce la digestione; i prodotti della digestione
vanno incontro all’assorbimento.
L’uomo è un organismo onnivoro, in quanto può nutrirsi di alimenti sia di origine vegetale, sia di
origine animale. Tuttavia la dieta deve non solo consentire di introdurre e di assorbire una quantità di
alimenti sufficiente a sopperire ai bisogni di materia e di energia dell’organismo, ma anche avere una
composizione qualitativa tale da rifornirlo di tutti quei composti che esso non è in grado di produrre a
partire da altri composti organici, ma che sono necessari al suo funzionamento e alla sua crescita.
Attraverso la complessa rete di reazioni chimiche che costituiscono il metabolismo (Biologia,
§ 3.4), monosaccaridi, acidi grassi, glicerolo, amminoacidi derivati dalla digestione di oligo e polisaccaridi,
di lipidi e di proteine, una volta assorbiti sono in parte ossidati dalle cellule producendo anidride
carbonica e acqua e liberando energia che viene immagazzinata sotto forma di adenosintrifosfato

Convert this shell script to python

#!/bin/bash

usage () {
    cat <<EOM
Usage: $(basename $0) [-h] [-m <archive_name> <input_directory>] [<input_directory> <output_directory>]
EOM
}

# Global variables
FILE_PATTERN='.*.[jpg|jpeg|JPG|JPEG|png|PNG]'
OUT_NAME='my_archive.cbz'

# Needs two arguments, the INDIR with the images to compress and OUTDIR
createArchive () {
	# Save input dir and output dir removing trailing /
	local INDIR="$1"
	local OUTDIR="$2"
	local TEMPDIR="$OUTDIR/temp"
	echo "Input dir = ${INDIR}"
	echo "Output dir = ${OUTDIR}"

	# Creates a temp/ folder inside OUTDIR if it does not exist, otherwise empties it.
	if [ ! -d "$TEMPDIR" ]
	then
		mkdir $TEMPDIR
	else
		echo "Warning: deleting ${TEMPDIR} content..."
		rm -rf $TEMPDIR/*
		echo "Warning: ${TEMPDIR} already existed and content has been deleted."
	fi

	# Finds number of images in subfolders
	local N_IMG=`find "$INDIR" -maxdepth 2 -type f -regex $FILE_PATTERN | wc -l`
	echo "Found $N_IMG images."
	# Finds number of digit to use to pad numbers
	local N_DIGIT=${#N_IMG}

	echo "Preparing files for compression..."
	# Initialises counter to number each page (first page is number 1)
	local COUNT=1
	# Lists all first level dirs sorted with version number sort
	# This command should return directories in the order in which they should be analyzed in order to produce the correct order of pages
	while IFS= read -r -d '' DIRNAME; do
		# Lists all first level files in every directory and returns them one by one in the correct order
		while IFS= read -r -d '' FILENAME; do
			# Copies and renames images inside TEMPDIR. Change 'cp' to 'mv' in order to delete original files.
			# Also applies zero padding as necessary (e.g. 1.jpg -> 0001.jpg)
			# Extension will be lowercase (e.g. JPG -> jpg)
			EXT=${FILENAME##*.}
			cp "${FILENAME}" "${TEMPDIR}/`printf \"%0${N_DIGIT}d\" ${COUNT}`.${EXT,,}"
			# Next page will have increasing number.
			COUNT=`expr $COUNT + 1`
			# I used process substitution to update COUNT correctly
		done< <(find "$DIRNAME" -maxdepth 1 -type f -regex $FILE_PATTERN -print0 | sort -z -V)
	done< <(find "$INDIR" -maxdepth 1 -type d -print0 | sort -z -V)

	COUNT=`expr $COUNT - 1`
	echo "Done."

if [ "$1" == "-h" ]
then
	# HELP MODE
	usage;
	exit 0
elif [ "$1" == "-m" ] || [ "$1" == "--merge" ]
then
	# MERGE MODE
	[ $# -ne 3 ] && { echo "Error: wrong number of arguments."; usage; exit 1; }
	[ ! -f "$2" ] && { echo "Error: merge option require the target archive in second parameter."; usage; exit 1; }
	INDIR=`realpath -s "$3"`
	[ ! -d "$INDIR" ] && { echo "Error: $INDIR is not a valid input directory."; exit 1; }
	echo "Merging $2 with $INDIR..."
	# Takes the directory of the archive to merge
	OUTDIR=`realpath -s $(dirname "$2")`
	TEMPDIR=$OUTDIR/tmpfolder
	TEMPDIR1=$TEMPDIR/tmp1
	TEMPDIR2=$TEMPDIR/tmp2
	if [ ! -d "$TEMPDIR1" ]; then mkdir --parents $TEMPDIR1; else rm -rf $TEMPDIR1/*; fi
	if [ ! -d "$TEMPDIR2" ]; then mkdir --parents $TEMPDIR2; else rm -rf $TEMPDIR2/*; fi
	# Unzip all archive files into tmp1
	unzip -j -q $2 -d $TEMPDIR1
	# Moves every file to add in tmp2
	find "$INDIR" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 2 -type f -regex $FILE_PATTERN -print0 | sort -V | \
		while IFS= read -r -d '' FILENAME; do
			cp "$FILENAME" $TEMPDIR2
		done
	# Creates the cbz file
	createArchive "$TEMPDIR" "$OUTDIR"
	# Deletes tmp folder
	rm -rf $TEMPDIR
	exit 0
elif [ $# -eq 2 ]
then
	# CREATION MODE
	INDIR=`realpath -s "$1"`
	[ ! -d "$INDIR" ] && { echo "Error: $INDIR is not a valid input directory."; exit 1; }
	OUTDIR=`realpath -s "$2"`
	# Creates OUTDIR if it doesn't exists
	if [ ! -d "$OUTDIR" ]; then mkdir --parents $OUTDIR;
	else
		# Asks for confirmation if the output file already exists
		if [ -f "$OUTDIR/$OUT_NAME" ]
		then
			echo "Warning: output file '$OUTDIR/$OUT_NAME' is already present and will be deleted."
			read -p "Do you want this to happen (y/n)? Press 'n' to abort. " -n 1 -r
			if [[ $REPLY =~ ^[Yy]$ ]]
			then
			    rm -f "$OUTDIR/$OUT_NAME"
			    echo "Deleted."
			else
				echo
				echo "Aborted."
				exit 0
			fi
		fi
	fi
	# Creates the cbz file
	createArchive "$INDIR" "$OUTDIR"
	exit 0
else
	echo "Wrong usage. See -h option."
	exit 1
fi

La IIIème République et l'enracinement républicain en France (1870-1900)

Introduction
La IIIème République joue un rôle essentiel, dans l'histoire de France, puisque c'est elle qui va enraciner le modèle républicain dans le cœur des Français et leur faire adopter un certain nombre de symboles et de valeurs qui sont encore les nôtres aujourd'hui. En effet, la IIIème République, malgré sa réputation d'instabilité, voire de corruption (largement exagérée par les Gaullistes pour faire adopter la Vème République), est celle qui a duré le plus longtemps (1870-1940). Et pourtant, lors de son adoption, rien ne laissait présager une telle longévité, tant les circonstances lui étaient peu favorables : défaite face à l'Allemagne, opinion majoritairement royaliste, etc...
problématique : comment les Français sont-ils devenus républicains ?

I.	Les débuts de la IIIème République : la lente adoption du régime républicain par les Français (1870-1879)
1. La naissance de la IIIème République et la majorité royaliste
a. La défaite et la proclamation de la République
En juillet 1870, la guerre éclate entre la Prusse et la France, alors gouvernée par Napoléon III. Le 2 septembre 1870, c'est la défaite française de Sedan : Napoléon III est capturé. Le 4 septembre, à Paris, la déchéance de Napoléon III est proclamée. Qui mettre à la place ? Les républicains ne sont pas pressés de proclamer une République dans un contexte de défaite, mais ils sont débordés par la foule, qui proclame Vive la République. 

Celle-ci est donc proclamée par Gambetta, Favre et Ferry le 4 septembre. Un gouvernement provisoire est donc mis en place. Ce gouvernement continue la guerre contre les Prussiens, mais la défaite est inévitable. Or, Bismarck ne veut signer la paix qu'avec un gouvernement légal. Il faut donc des élections.

b. L'Assemblée monarchiste
Ces dernières sont organisées précipitamment en février 1871, au suffrage universel. Les monarchistes l'emportent largement, car ils sont favorables à la paix, contrairement aux républicains. Et les Français veulent la paix. La nouvelle Assemblée compte 400 députés monarchistes, 30 bonapartistes et 200 républicains. Adolphe Thiers est choisi comme chef du gouvernement et il est décidé d'attendre d'avoir pacifié la France avant de décider du régime politique à adopter. Les républicains gagnent ainsi du temps.

c. La Commune
Le nouveau régime est rapidement confronté à sa première crise sérieuse avec la Commune de Paris. Les Parisiens avaient massivement voté en faveur des Républicains et de la poursuite de la guerre. Une garde nationale, composée de 250 000 volontaires s'était mise en place et avait combattu contre les Prussiens. Le retour au pouvoir des monarchistes exaspère les Parisiens et la Garde nationale refuse d'obéir au nouveau gouvernement. La crise éclate le 18 mars 1871, lorsque Thiers ordonne à la Garde nationale de rendre ses canons. Les Parisiens s'y opposent et Thiers ordonne alors à ses troupes d'assiéger Paris. La ville se révolte et élit des représentants : c'est la Commune de Paris, qui adopte le drapeau rouge et un programme révolutionnaire: calendrier révolutionnaire, programme scolaire laïque, etc... Une véritable guerre civile éclate entre Communards et Versaillais. Les combats sont violents et le gouvernement parvient finalement à reprendre Paris, en mai 1871, au terme de la semaine sanglante (21-28 mai 1871). 30 à 35 000 communards sont tués.
Point de passage : Louise Michel

Mais le nouveau régime sort renforcé de cette épreuve : c'est la 1ère fois depuis 1789 qu'un pouvoir résiste à une insurrection parisienne. L'idée qu'un pouvoir républicain peut aussi bien maintenir l'ordre qu'une monarchie fait son chemin dans la population.

2. Mac Mahon et l'ordre moral : l'échec de la restauration monarchique
a. Les difficultés des monarchistes
Les monarchistes, majoritaires à l'Assemblée, souhaitent restaurer la monarchie. Mais ils sont divisés en deux courants : 
- les légitimistes, qui souhaitent voir couronner Henri V, comte de Chambord. Ils veulent revenir à l'Ancien régime
- les orléanistes, habitués du pouvoir, qu'ils ont exercé pendant la Monarchie de Juillet (1830-48), et qui soutiennent Louis XIX, comte de Paris. Eux, sont davantage libéraux, attachés au parlementarisme et conservateurs sur le plan social.

Finalement, un arrangement est trouvé : Henri V régnera d'abord, puis Louis XIX lui succédera. Mais le comte de Chambord fait tout capoter en refusant de renoncer au drapeau blanc, celui de la royauté sous l'Ancien régime. Les monarchistes savent que les Français y sont attachés. Il leur faut donc attendre la mort du comte de Chambord (1883) pour pouvoir placer le comte de Paris au pouvoir. En attendant, ils renversent le gouvernement de Thiers et mettent à sa place le maréchal Mac Mahon (mai 1873).

b. L'ordre moral
La présidence de Mac Mahon est placée sous le signe de la restauration de l'ordre moral. La religion y prend une place très importante : vote de la loi qui décide l'édification du Sacré-Coeur ; création des facultés catholiques : Lille, Paris, Angers, Lyon, Toulouse ; développement de la presse catholique : La Croix, Le Pélerin. 
En réaction, les républicains vont s'éloigner davantage de la religion.

3. La consolidation du régime : les lois constitutionnelles de 1875 et la crise du 16 mai 1877
a. Les lois constitutionnelles de 1875 ou comment gagner du temps
L'Assemblée élue en 1871 était constituante. Les députés cherchent alors à mettre en place une constitution. Cette dernière donne lieu à des marchandages très serrés entre monarchistes et républicains : les premiers veulent un système qui laisse la porte ouverte à une restauration monarchique. Tandis que les seconds veulent gagner du temps. Le nouveau régime est mis en place par les lois constitutionnelles de 1875 qui créent un régime bicaméral avec un président de la République à sa tête :

Président de la République (élu pour 7 ans par les 2 chambres))

ministres

chambre des députés					Sénat : - 75 sénateurs inamovibles
(élus pour 4 ans au suffrage universel)			- 225 sénateurs élus par grands électeurs

Les ministres doivent obtenir la confiance des 2 chambres et le président peut dissoudre la chambre des députés avec l'accord du Sénat. Ce système peut aussi bien fonctionner avec un roi à la place d'un président.

b. La crise du 16 mai 1877 : le renforcement du parlementarisme
Aux élections de 1875, les républicains emportent la majorité à la chambre des députés : petit à petit, ils ont progressé dans l'opinion, contrairement aux monarchistes. Seul le Sénat demeure à faible majorité monarchiste. Mac Mahon fait alors appel à Jules Simon pour gouverner en tant que président du Conseil, car celui-ci est républicain. Une fois au pouvoir, Simon mène une politique anti-cléricale et épure le corps des magistrats et des préfets de tous les monarchistes. 

Cela agace Mac Mahon, tenant convaincu de l'ordre moral. Il pousse Jules Simon à la démission le 16 mai 1877 et fait appel à un président du conseil de droite. La Chambre lui refuse la confiance et Mac Mahon dissout alors la Chambre, comme il en a le droit.

De nouvelles élections sont convoquées et les républicains emportent la majorité. Mac Mahon est désavoué et c'est désormais une conception parlementariste du pouvoir qui va l'emporter : c'est la Chambre qui décide et le président n'a qu'un rôle symbolique. Plus aucun président de la IIIème République n'osera désormais dissoudre la Chambre.

Mac Mahon démissionne en janvier 1879 et il est remplacé par un républicain. A partir de là, ces derniers vont conquérir petit à petit tous les postes. A ce stade, les monarchistes sont éliminés du jeu politique. Gambetta peut déclarer : « le danger est passé, les difficultés commencent ».

II.	La République opportuniste (1879-99)
1. Les grandes réformes des Républicains
a. Opportunistes et radicaux
Les Républicains, au pouvoir, sont divisés en deux grandes tendances : opportunistes et radicaux. Ces deux groupes sont à peu près d'accord sur le programme politique qu'ils souhaitent mettre en place : réformes économiques, réforme de l'armée, école laïque et obligatoire, suffrage universel. Mais ils ne le sont pas sur la méthode : les opportunistes veulent aborder les réformes de manière progressive et réaliste. Les radicaux veulent tout changer tout de suite.

b. La législation réformatrice des opportunistes
Les opportunistes, une fois au pouvoir, vont mettre en place toute une législation réformatrice et anti-cléricale :
- 1879 : la Marseillaise est adoptée comme hymne national 
- 1880 : loi qui supprime le repos obligatoire du dimanche et des fêtes religieuses
- 1880 : le 14 juillet devient la fête nationale 
- 1881 : liberté de réunion publique, sans autorisation, mais avec une simple déclaration
- 1881 : loi sur la liberté de la presse. N'importe qui peut fonder un journal. Les journaux peuvent publier ce qu'ils veulent, le seul risque est d'être attaqué en diffamation
- 1884 : les conseils municipaux, désormais, élisent les maires (qui ne sont plus désignés par le préfet). L'apprentissage de la démocratie va se faire dans les villages.
- 1884 : loi Waldeck-Rousseau qui établit la liberté syndicale
- 1884 : la loi Naquet autorise le divorce
- 1884 : révision constitutionnelle qui rend intangible la forme républicaine du gouvernement. Tous les membres de familles ayant régné sur la France sont inéligibles à la présidence de la République
- 1901 : loi sur la liberté de création des associations
Point de passage : les funérailles de Victor Hugo

c. Les lois scolaires
A partir de 1880, l'objectif des opportunistes, c'est de former des citoyens républicains, arrachés à l'influence très forte de l'Eglise. En effet, celle-ci était devenue incontournable dans l'enseignement, à tous les niveaux.
- en 1880, les facultés catholiques perdent la collation de grades : désormais, c'est l'Etat qui délivre les diplômes
- 1881 : l'enseignement primaire est rendu public et gratuit
- 1882 : l'enseignement primaire devient laïc et obligatoire

Ces deux lois, connues sous le nom de lois Ferry, aboutissent à une laïcisation progressive de l'enseignement. 

2. L'anticléricalisme
L'école devient ainsi le relais, dans la population, du courant de pensée rationaliste et positiviste des Républicains. Le positivisme d'Auguste Comte est, en effet, le courant de pensée dominant chez les Républicains : il affirme la foi en la science, dans le progrès (ex : devise du Brésil, tirée d'Auguste Comte : « Ordre et Progrès). Tout est explicable par la science. 
La religion n'est donc qu'obscurantisme ignorant et les Républicains l'accusent d'essayer de dominer les foules par l'ignorance. Les instituteurs sont souvent très en pointe dans ce combat. Surnommés les hussards noirs de la République, ils ont pour mission de répandre la pensée positiviste et de combattre la religion. Dans les villages, ils sont donc souvent l'ennemi du prêtre.

La République opportuniste est donc anti-cléricale. Mais peu à peu, les choses vont s'apaiser et les catholiques vont se rallier à la République. En effet, le nouveau pape Léon XIII, plus ouvert, va considérer que l'Eglise ne doit pas s'attacher aux monarchistes. En 1890, la cardinal Lavigerie, évêque d'Alger, porte un toast à la République, de façon publique. Puis, en février 1892, le pape publie l'encyclique « Au milieu des sollicitudes », qui appelle à accepter la République et à y participer pour changer la législation.

3. La colonisation et le relèvement de l'orgueil national 
Les premières années de la République sont des années de prudence, sur le plan diplomatique et militaire : la reconquête de l'Alsace-Lorraine n'est évoquée qu'à mots couverts. L'orgueil national, blessé par la défaite de 1870, va être soigné par une politique coloniale dynamique, à partir des années 1880. Cette politique, au départ, suscite des résistances, en particulier de la part des radicaux. Pour eux, cette politique « nous prend notre or et le meilleur de notre sang ». De plus, elle détourne de « la ligne bleue des Vosges ». Petit à petit, cependant, ces résistances vont diminuer et la politique coloniale française va enthousiasmer la population : l'Afrique noire, Madagascar, l'Indochine, l'Afrique du Nord sont tour à tour conquis, faisant de la France le second empire colonial après celui des Britanniques. Ces conquêtes, certes, servent des ambitions économiques et politiques, mais participent également du positivisme républicain : il faut apporter les lumières de la civilisation aux peuples ignorants.

4. Des crises qui renforcent le régime
a. Crise boulangiste (1886-89)
L'armée, sous la République opportuniste, demeure un bastion monarchiste. Le général Boulanger est l'un des rares généraux républicains. Nommé ministre de la guerre, il s'attaque à une réforme de l'armée qui assure sa popularité. Cette dernière augmente encore avec l'incident Schnaebelé (avril 1887) : un officier de police français, soupçonné de contre-espionnage par les Allemands, est attiré en territoire allemand et arrêté. Boulanger adopte une attitude très dure avec l'Allemagne et obtient sa libération de la part de Bismarck. Il devient celui qui a fait reculer le chancelier allemand. On le surnomme général Revanche.
Le gouvernement décide alors de l'écarter et le nomme à Clermont-Ferrand. Au moment de son départ, la foule l'entoure et l'empêche pendant plusieurs heures de partir.

De ce moment, Boulanger en vient à rassembler autour de lui tous les déçus et les critiques de la République : monarchistes, bonapartistes, radicaux. Ces soutiens de Boulanger souhaitent que ce dernier prennent le pouvoir et modifie la constitution. Le gouvernement, inquiet, réagit en mettant Boulanger à la retraite. Mais cela n'aboutit qu'à lui permettre de se présenter à des élections : il est alors élu député, à Paris, en janvier 1889. La foule l'acclame, l'invite au coup d'Etat, qui aurait sans doute été facile. Mais ce n'est pas un aventurier, il laisse passer sa chance et se préoccupe davantage de sa liaison avec Mme Bonnemain. Le gouvernement en profite pour lui intenter un procès. Boulanger s'enfuit en Belgique, rejoindre sa maîtresse. En septembre 1891 il se suicide sur la tombe de cette dernière.

La crise boulangiste a discrédité les radicaux, dont certains s'étaient associés à Boulanger. Cela renforce la République opportuniste, qui est modérée.


b. Affaire Dreyfus (1894)
Fin septembre 1894, le service de renseignements de l’armée française prend connaissance d’une lettre (connue sous le nom de « bordereau ») prouvant des envois de documents militaires confidentiels aux services allemands. Une enquête est ouverte et les soupçons se portent rapidement sur le capitaine Alfred Dreyfus, officier brillant, mais de famille juive dans un milieu où c’est très rare. Le seul élément permettant de l’accuser est la ressemblance entre son écriture et celle du bordereau.
Dreyfus est alors arrêté le 15 octobre. Il passe en conseil de guerre en décembre. Tout plaide pour son innocence, mais la haute hiérarchie militaire est décidée à le faire condamner pour sauver l’honneur de l’armée. Le ministre de la guerre fait donc passer au président du tribunal, en toute illégalité, un dossier secret, forgé de toute pièce par les services de renseignement, pour prouver la culpabilité de Dreyfus. Ce dernier est alors condamné le 22 décembre 1894. Il est dégradé le 5 janvier 1895 et part en déportation le 21 février pour l’Ile du Diable. Toute la presse applaudit, car Dreyfus est considéré comme un traître.

- 1897, Mathieu Dreyfus, qui cherche à innocenter son frère, découvre l’identité du véritable espion : Esterhazy, un officier endetté mais protégé. Mathieu Dreyfus écrit un article dans le Figaro, pour accuser Esterhazy, le 16 novembre 1897. 
- 13 janvier 1898, 2 jours après qu’Esterhazy, qui avait demandé à être jugé pour laver son honneur, est acquitté par le tribunal militaire, l’Aurore publie à 300 000 exemplaires une « Lettre au président de la République », signée Zola et surmontée par Georges Clémenceau, rédacteur en chef, d’un « j’accuse ! ». L’intervention de Zola et de Clémenceau va donner un grand retentissement à l’affaire. D’autant que Zola met au défi le pouvoir de le traîner en justice pour diffamation.
EN février 1898, Zola comparaît devant une cour d’assise pour diffamation. Le procès a un grand retentissement. Zola est condamné à un an de prison et 3000F d’amende. Il s’enfuit en Angleterre.
Le 3 juin 1899, la cour de cassation, saisie par Lucie Dreyfus, casse le jugement de 1894. Dreyfus doit être rapatrié de Guyane et rejugé. Le lendemain, le président de la République, Emile Loubet, qui vient d’être élu, est pris à partie par des anti-dreyfusards qui portent un œillet blanc à la boutonnière et il reçoit un coup de canne. Le 11 juin, une contre-manifestation est organisée par les socialistes, pour la défense républicaine (œillet rouge). L’affaire fait chuter le gouvernement et le nouveau prend le nom de « défense républicaine ».

 Dreyfus, encouragé par le président de la République demande sa grâce, qui est acceptée et signée le 19 septembre 1899. Dreyfus est alors libéré. L’affaire est terminée. Le 2 juin 1900, le Sénat vote l’amnistie. Et le 12 juillet 1906 la Cour de cassation casse le jugement de Rennes et lave Dreyfus de toute accusation.  Dreyfus meurt en 1935.

L’affaire Dreyfus va avoir deux grands types d’effets, en France,  :
Les affrontements entre droite et gauche : l’affaire Dreyfus cristallise une opposition,  entre deux camps antagonistes : une gauche républicaine, intellectuelle, représentée par Zola, Clémenceau, mais aussi les élèves de l’Ecole normale (Blum, Péguy, etc…). Ils publient dans la Revue blanche, participent à la Ligue des droits de l’homme et du citoyen (fondée en 1898). Les Dreyfusards militent à la fois pour le respect de la loi, le maintien de la République.

De l’autre côté, une droite nationaliste, antisémite, se structure autour de personnages comme Maurice Barrès, Charles Maurras, Jules Verne, Léon Daudet, Auguste Renoir, Degas, etc… Eux militent pour la patrie, pour l’honneur de l’armée, contre tout ce qui, à leurs yeux, affaiblit la France : les juifs, le parlementarisme, etc… Ils constituent des ligues : Ligue des patriotes (Déroulède), Ligue antisémitique (Guérin et Drumont), Ligue de la Patrie française. Les antidreyfusards sont antirépublicains. Ils suscitent des manifestations, parfois violentes et certains prônent le renversement de la République. Ex : au moment des obsèques de Félix Faure (février 1899), alors que le procès de Dreyfus est en cours de révision, les militants de la Ligue des patriotes (Déroulède) manifestent contre le nouveau président (Loubet), accusé d’affaiblir le pays. Les manifestants tentent même de marcher sur l’Elysée.

Les conséquences politiques de l’affaire, à long terme, sont également importantes :
- les socialistes éliminent de leur discours toute référence antisémite. L’affaire les pousse aussi à adhérer davantage au modèle républicain, mis en danger par les antidreyfusards. Les socialistes deviennent, également, antimilitaristes.
- le nationalisme prend un nouveau visage, avec des thèmes comme la crainte de la décadence, le retour sur les valeurs nationales.

Conclusion
La IIIème République, de façon progressive et opportuniste a donc réussi à imposer une forme de régime républicain, dans un pays qui, par tradition et conviction, était largement monarchiste. L'habileté des Républicains a été de prouver aux Français que la forme républicaine était capable de s'adapter à toutes les circonstances et à toutes les crises. Et puis, la force de la IIIème République a été aussi de proposer plus qu'un mode de gouvernement : une véritable philosophie politique, reposant sur le positivisme et la démocratie. Enfin, la IIIème République a su utiliser le relais très puissant de l'éducation pour enraciner cette philosophie politique dans la population française.

Ces trente premières années de la IIIème République vont toutefois aussi porter les germes de l'affaiblissement de cette dernière : des scandales comme celui des décorations (1887 : le gendre du président Grevy vendait la légion d'honneur!), ou de Panama (1892) vont nourrir un antiparlementarisme tenace dans l'opinion, tandis que la crise de mai 1877 n'est que le début d'un long affaiblissement de la fonction présidentielle, qui ne fait que renforcer la place essentielle du Parlement dans le paysage politique.

def insert_face_in_frame(face_image_path, frame_image_path, landmarks_model_path='shape_predictor_68_face_landmarks.dat'):
    # Load images
    face_image = cv2.imread(face_image_path, cv2.IMREAD_UNCHANGED)
    frame_image = cv2.imread(frame_image_path, cv2.IMREAD_UNCHANGED)

    # Convert face_image to grayscale for face detection
    gray_face_image = cv2.cvtColor(face_image, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)

    # Initialize face detector
    detector = dlib.get_frontal_face_detector()

    # Detect face in the face_image
    faces = detector(gray_face_image)
    if len(faces) == 0:
        print('No face detected in the face_image. Please provide a different image.')
        return

    # Get face boundaries
    x1, y1, x2, y2 = faces[0].left(), faces[0].top(), faces[0].right(), faces[0].bottom()

    # Resize face_image to frame size (keep aspect ratio)
    # Calculate scale factor
    frame_height, frame_width = frame_image.shape[:2]
    face_height, face_width = (y2-y1), (x2-x1)

    if face_height/frame_height > face_width/frame_width:
        scale_factor = frame_height / face_height
    else:
        scale_factor = frame_width / face_width

    resized_face_image = cv2.resize(face_image, (0,0), fx=scale_factor, fy=scale_factor)
    resized_height, resized_width = resized_face_image.shape[:2]

    # Position for face in the frame
    pos_x = (frame_width - resized_width) // 2
    pos_y = (frame_height - resized_height) // 2

    # Combine images (Adjust colors too)
    face_roi = frame_image[pos_y:pos_y+resized_height, pos_x:pos_x+resized_width].copy()
    alpha_face_roi = cv2.addWeighted(face_roi, 0.5, resized_face_image, 0.5, 0)

    frame_image_with_face = frame_image.copy()
    frame_image_with_face[pos_y:pos_y+resized_height, pos_x:pos_x+resized_width] = alpha_face_roi

    # Save as a new image file
    cv2.imwrite('combined_image.png', frame_image_with_face)

    # Display output
    cv2.imshow('Combined Image', frame_image_with_face)
    cv2.waitKey(0)
    cv2.destroyAllWindows()

- Brief introduction of adidas

Adidas AG, a multinational corporation founded in Germany in 1949, is one of the world’s leading sportswear, footwear, and equipment manufacturers. Adidas has its global headquarters in Herzogenaurach, Germany, and employs over 60,000 people globally. Adidas has a long and illustrious history in the sports and fashion industries. The brand’s logo is iconic, consisting of three parallel stripes that represent strength, speed, and endurance. The stripes were originally added to sports shoes to provide greater stability but were soon incorporated into the brand’s identity.

Adidas operates under a mission “to be the best sports company in the world.” It illustrates this by maintaining innovative product designs, using advanced technologies, and investing in sustainability initiatives. - Importance of brand management for businesses
Effective brand management is crucial for any business, as it helps shape customer perceptions and sets the foundation for robust relationships between a brand and its customers. A well-managed brand can help a company stand out from competitors, strengthen its market position, and drive growth.

Slides 4-6 : Brand Heritage 

- Overview of the adidas brand’s historical development
Adidas, founded by Adolf “Adi” Dassler in 1949, has a rich history rooted in innovation, quality, and a passion for sports. Its origins date back to the 1920s when Adi Dassler and his brother Rudolf started a shoe company, Gebrüder Dassler Schuhfabrik, in their mother’s laundry room. The brothers’ innovative sports shoes gained recognition at the 1936 Olympics, where Jesse Owens wore them while winning four gold medals.

However, disagreements between the two brothers led to the dissolution of their partnership, and Adi Dassler formed adidas while Rudolf established PUMA. The iconic three-stripe logo made its debut on adidas shoes in 1949, and the brand continued to gain fame through endorsements with prominent athletes and national teams.

Over the decades, adidas has evolved and diversified its product offerings, targeting various sports categories, including running, football, basketball, and training. The acquisition of Reebok in 2006 reinforced the company’s position in the sports market, and partnerships with designers such as Yohji Yamamoto and Stella McCartney added a high-fashion dimension to the brand.

- Key milestones in the adidas brand’s evolution
1. 1949: Adi Dassler establishes adidas and introduces the three-stripe logo.
2. 1954: The German national football team wins the World Cup wearing adidas’ screw-in stud shoes, further bolstering the brand’s reputation in sports innovation.
3. 1970: Adidas becomes the official ball supplier for the FIFA World Cup.
4. 1980s-1990s: The brand expands from sports shoes into the broader sportswear and equipment market, including apparel, accessories, and sports equipment.
5. 2006: Acquisition of Reebok bolsters the adidas Group’s presence within North America and strengthens its position in the global sports market.
6. 2010s: Continued expansion of adidas’ product offerings, with notable partnerships including Y-3 with Yohji Yamamoto, collaboration with Kanye West on Yeezy, and partnerships with high-profile athletes such as Lionel Messi and James Harden.
7. 2015: Introduction of the Parley for the Oceans initiative, showcasing adidas’ commitment to sustainability by using ocean plastic waste to create performance footwear and apparel.
8. 2020: Adidas announces a partnership with Allbirds, another sustainability-focused footwear brand, aimed at creating the lowest carbon footprint sports shoe possible.

- The adidas brand’s mission, values, and beliefs
Adidas’ mission is to be the best sports company in the world, expressing this through the brand’s three-pillar strategy: Speed, Key Cities, and Open Source. These pillars aim to foster innovation, focus on crucial urban markets, and encourage collaboration among athletes, consumers, and partners.

The brand seeks to empower people through sports by adhering to its core values – passion, integrity, innovation, and teamwork. These values are reflected in numerous initiatives, including sustainable product design, inclusive sizing and representation in campaigns, and investments in employee development and well-being.

Adidas is a brand that believes in the transformative power of sports, working tirelessly to create products and experiences that enable people to harness this power and improve their lives.

- Visual representation using elements of the brand heritage model
An effective framework for examining adidas’ brand heritage is Keller’s Brand System Model. It comprises four components
1. Brand Identity (Adidas Logo and Three-Stripe Mark): Adidas’ iconic logo, featuring three stripes, represents the unity, quality, and performance associated with the brand.
2. Brand Meaning (Innovation, Quality, and Passion for Sports): The key elements of adidas’ brand meaning include innovation in sports equipment and apparel, high-quality products, and a genuine love for sports in all forms.
3. Brand Response (Customer Loyalty, Recognition, and Emotion): Adidas elicits strong responses from consumers, including loyalty, recognition of the brand and its values, and emotional connections to sports, performance, and self-improvement.
4. Brand Relationship (Athletes, Teams, Designers, and Partnerships): Adidas has cultivated robust relationships with professional athletes, sports teams, designers, and partners, fostering collaboration and contributing to the brand’s continued growth and relevance.

This slide provides a high-level overview of adidas’ brand heritage, encompassing both its history and the key elements that contribute to its current identity, meaning, response, and relationships in the global sports industry.


Slide 7&8: Market Positioning

Adidas occupies a prominent position in the sports and athleisure market, targeting consumers who prioritize performance, innovation, style, and sustainability. - Analysis of competitors in the market landscape

5. - Differentiation strategy for the value proposition
Adidas differentiates itself from competitors primarily through product innovation, collaborations with influential designers and celebrities, and sustainability initiatives. These unique selling points create a compelling value proposition for the adidas brand:

        if not self.settings_dialog:

        QtWidgets.QApplication.quit()

import numpy as np
def trajectory(horizontal_speed, initial_height, xmax, nmax):
    # Define physical parameters
    g = 980  # cm/s^2
    kappa = 0.5  # 1/s
    a = 1  # cm
    b = 0.25  # cm

    # Define step size
    dx = xmax / (nmax - 1)

    # Initialise arrays
    x = np.linspace(0, xmax, nmax)
    y = np.zeros(nmax)
    y[0] = initial_height
    y[1] = y[0] - (g * (1 - np.exp(-(y[0] - a) / b)) * (dx ** 2)) / (2 * (horizontal_speed ** 2))

    # Iterate to compute the rest of the y values
    for n in range(1, nmax - 1):
        y[n + 1] = (-2 * dx ** 2 * g * (1 - np.exp(-(y[n] - a) / b)) + dx * kappa * horizontal_speed * y[
            n - 1] + 4 * horizontal_speed ** 2 * y[n] - 2 * horizontal_speed ** 2 * y[n - 1]) / (
                               2 * horizontal_speed ** 2 + kappa * dx * horizontal_speed)
    return x, y

def residual(horizontal_speed, initial_height, x_teacup, y_teacup, nmax):
    # Compute the trajectory of the ball using the given parameters
    x, y = trajectory(horizontal_speed, initial_height, x_teacup, nmax)

    # Compute the residual as the difference between the final y-value and the target y-value
    residual = y[-1] - y_teacup

    return residual

import math
from scipy.optimize import bisect

def find_horizontal_speed(initial_height, x_teacup, y_teacup, nmax, bounce=False):
    # Define physical parameters
    g = 980  # cm/s^2

    # Compute the initial guess for u0 based on the parabolic trajectory
    h = initial_height - y_teacup
    u0_guess = x_teacup * math.sqrt(g / (2 * h))

    # Define the bracketing interval for the root-finding algorithm
    lower_bound = 0.8 * u0_guess
    upper_bound = 1.2 * u0_guess

    # Define the residual function F(u0) for a given horizontal speed u0
    def F(u0):
        return residual(u0, initial_height, x_teacup, y_teacup, nmax)

    # Find the root of F(u0) using the bisection method with a tolerance of 0.1cm
    u0_root = bisect(F, lower_bound, upper_bound, xtol=0.1)

    return u0_root

Strategy
In the bounce case, the interaction with the floor produces unpredictable results. However, we know that friction always reduces the motion, and the interaction with the floor produces most of the damping (also true with real objects).
However, we can pretend there is exactly zero damping, which gives us an estimate that will undershoot the mark when we include friction.
In this case, we estimate that the marble falls to the floor with a parabolic trajectory. It then bounces back and returns to its original height with a mirror-image trajectory. After that, the marble continues to fall toward the target but with a reduced distance.
Putting everything together, produces a lower bound for the speed estimate. The zero-bounce estimate from Task 3c now gives us an upper bound, and we can bracket our solution with:
((xteacup*sqrt(g/(2h)))/(1+2*sqrt(y0/h))) < u0 < xteacup*sqrt(g/(2h)) where h=y0-yteacup
Starting from this interval [umin,umax], it's possible to use a modified version of the bisection method,which also counts the total number of bounces and peaks for the trajectory with the midpoint umidpoint=(umin+umax)/2.

Another important theme in "Train to Busan" is the bioethical principle of beneficence. The characters make heroic sacrifices to protect others from harm, highlighting the importance of solidarity and cooperation in public health crises. This principle is particularly relevant in today's world, where COVID-19 has underscored the need for collective action to combat infectious diseases.

The bioethical principle of non-maleficence is also a central concern in "Train to Busan." The movie raises thought-provoking questions about the risks and benefits of various public health measures, such as quarantine and vaccination. Overall, "Train to Busan" is an exciting and thought-provoking movie that raises important ethical questions related to public health and human rights. It is a timely reminder of the importance of balancing individual autonomy with the needs of the community and promoting the well-being of all.

Ownership
The ownership component within Dunning’s eclectic paradigm (OLI) framework emphasizes the assessment of a firm’s competitive advantages based on its unique resources or capabilities (Dunning, 2000). These competitive assets determine the extent to which a firm can exploit its ownership advantages or disadvantages in the foreign market. In the case of Walmart’s investment opportunity or operations in Italy, it is essential to evaluate its ownership strengths and weaknesses, and also examine the competition in the Italian retail sector.
Walmart, as the world’s largest retailer, has historically leveraged its considerable resources and capabilities to achieve global success (Fortune Global 500, 2021). Some of these resources include its economies of scale, vast distribution networks, and advanced supply chain management techniques (Pappas et al., 2020). In theory, these ownership advantages should offer Walmart significant growth potential within the Italian market. However, this perspective may overlook some critical limitations that could challenge Walmart’s ability to replicate its success in Italy.
One of the ownership disadvantages Walmart may encounter is the difficulty in adapting to the culturally-sensitive Italian market. Unlike the American retail landscape, which emphasizes low prices, convenience, and a wide selection of products (De Nisco et al., 2014), Italian consumers place greater value on the quality and authenticity of locally-sourced products (Pellegrini et al., 2016). Walmart’s primary competitive advantage, its low-price guarantee, may not resonate as strongly with Italian consumers (Javalgi et al., 2011). This suggests that Walmart may need to reevaluate its approach to attract Italy’s consumer base.
Furthermore, Italy’s retail sector comprises numerous small, family-owned businesses that have survived despite the growing presence of larger retail chains, reflecting the importance of tradition and loyalty to the Italian market (Caputo & Pellegrini, 2019). As a foreign entrant, Walmart faces the challenge of competing against these deeply-rooted, domestic retailers (Hitt et al., 2011). Despite its ownership advantages, Walmart’s American identity may pose a barrier to success in Italy.
The Italian market is also characterized by a highly competitive and concentrated retail sector, with well-established players like Coop Italia and Conad leading the market share (Statista, 2020). In such a competitive environment, Walmart must differentiate itself through strategic alliances, mergers, or acquisitions to gain a foothold in the market. For instance, the company worked with Grupo Éxito in 1994 to enter the Colombian market (Gaviria & Meléndez, 2006), which could serve as a reference for the Italian market. Nevertheless, Walmart’s ownership advantages alone may not guarantee success. According to Buckley et al. (2007), a firm’s international expansion depends on adequate combinations of ownership, location, and internalization advantages.
In Sum, although Walmart possesses considerable ownership advantages, its success in the Italian market may be limited by several factors, including cultural differences, the entrenched nature of local businesses, and the highly competitive landscape. A comprehensive analysis of Walmart’s investment opportunity or operations within Italy requires a critical evaluation of these ownership factors, considering both the advantages and disadvantages that may emerge in the foreign market.

import numpy as np
def trajectory(horizontal_speed, initial_height, xmax, nmax):
    # Define physical parameters
    g = 980  # cm/s^2
    kappa = 0.5  # 1/s
    a = 1  # cm
    b = 0.25  # cm

    # Define step size
    dx = xmax / (nmax - 1)

    # Initialise arrays
    x = np.linspace(0, xmax, nmax)
    y = np.zeros(nmax)
    y[0] = initial_height
    y[1] = y[0] - (g * (1 - np.exp(-(y[0] - a) / b)) * (dx ** 2)) / (2 * (horizontal_speed ** 2))

    # Iterate to compute the rest of the y values
    for n in range(1, nmax - 1):
        y[n + 1] = (-2 * dx ** 2 * g * (1 - np.exp(-(y[n] - a) / b)) + dx * kappa * horizontal_speed * y[
            n - 1] + 4 * horizontal_speed ** 2 * y[n] - 2 * horizontal_speed ** 2 * y[n - 1]) / (
                               2 * horizontal_speed ** 2 + kappa * dx * horizontal_speed)
    return x, y

def residual(horizontal_speed, initial_height, x_teacup, y_teacup, nmax):
    # Compute the trajectory of the ball using the given parameters
    x, y = trajectory(horizontal_speed, initial_height, x_teacup, nmax)

    # Compute the residual as the difference between the final y-value and the target y-value
    residual = y[-1] - y_teacup

    return residual

import math
from scipy.optimize import bisect

def find_horizontal_speed(initial_height, x_teacup, y_teacup, nmax, bounce=False):
    # Define physical parameters
    g = 980  # cm/s^2

    # Compute the initial guess for u0 based on the parabolic trajectory
    h = initial_height - y_teacup
    u0_guess = x_teacup * math.sqrt(g / (2 * h))

    # Define the bracketing interval for the root-finding algorithm
    lower_bound = 0.8 * u0_guess
    upper_bound = 1.2 * u0_guess

    # Define the residual function F(u0) for a given horizontal speed u0
    def F(u0):
        return residual(u0, initial_height, x_teacup, y_teacup, nmax)

    # Find the root of F(u0) using the bisection method with a tolerance of 0.1cm
    u0_root = bisect(F, lower_bound, upper_bound, xtol=0.1)

    return u0_root

Strategy
In the bounce case, the interaction with the floor produces unpredictable results. However, we know that friction always reduces the motion, and the interaction with the floor produces most of the damping (also true with real objects).
However, we can pretend there is exactly zero damping, which gives us an estimate that will undershoot the mark when we include friction.
In this case, we estimate that the marble falls to the floor with a parabolic trajectory. It then bounces back and returns to its original height with a mirror-image trajectory. After that, the marble continues to fall toward the target but with a reduced distance.
Putting everything together, produces a lower bound for the speed estimate. The zero-bounce estimate from Task 3c now gives us an upper bound, and we can bracket our solution with:
((xteacup*sqrt(g/(2h)))/(1+2*sqrt(y0/h))) < u0 < xteacup*sqrt(g/(2h)) where h=y0-yteacup

from flask import Flask, Response, render_template, request, make_response
from typing import Dict, Union


app = Flask(__name__)

PASSWORD: str = os.getenv(

)

JWT_TYPE = Dict[str, Union[str, bool]]
DEFAULT_TOKEN = {"admin": False}
TOKEN_NAME = "auth_token"
ALGORITHM = "HS256"


def encode_jwt(data: JWT_TYPE) -> str:
    """Encode Dict to JWT"""
    return jwt.encode(data, PASSWORD, ALGORITHM)


def decode_jwt(jwt_token: str) -> JWT_TYPE:
    """Decode JWT into Dict"""
    return jwt.decode(jwt_token, PASSWORD, ALGORITHM)


JWT_DEFAULT_TOKEN = encode_jwt(DEFAULT_TOKEN)


@app.route("/")
def index() -> Response:
    """The main website for the challenge"""
    raw_cookie = request.cookies.get(TOKEN_NAME, JWT_DEFAULT_TOKEN)
    auth_token = decode_jwt(raw_cookie)

    if auth_token.get("admin"):
        return render_template("flag.html", flag=FLAG)

    response = make_response(render_template("index.html"))
    response.set_cookie(TOKEN_NAME, encode_jwt(auth_token))

    return response

    # Do not do this in prod.
    app.run(debug=True)

Hi! Now I will describe to you my sketch of the structure of the world through a fictional legend of representatives of this world. The legend is called MHIWYA. After the legend, I will ask you a few questions about how to complement it and the world of people who could invent it.

The text of the legend MHIWYA: Once The Supreme-God-Demiurge created the world — the World-of-the-Children-of-God — from several dimensions, and each of the dimensions was inhabited by The Children of God. Nature, weather and conditions on the planet are similar to those on Earth (so far, I think so)

A full-fledged connection between dimensions would be impossible if there were not two ways to implement it:

Way 1: Carriers. A social class of The Children of God who can take the forms of birds and have the ability to Transcale: instant adaptation to any dimension in which the Carrier may be. Carriers are able to give this ability to their passengers at the time of joint travel.

Way 2: Engineers' Devices. Engineers are another social class of The Children of God, capable of producing special electronic devices that allow simulating the external senses of representatives of different dimensions, so that the connection between them, even at a distance in time and space, is fast and complete in terms of the coincidence of the organs of perception of all participants in the act of communication.

One of the Carriers was the eagle Altair: a storyteller whose voice and stories fascinated. He had a special instrument, let's temporarily call it the Altair Lyre, a six-stringed elegant lyre with a body resembling a swirling sea wave. At night, retreating into the rocks, Altair took on a form that allowed him to play an instrument. During the day, being a Carrier, Altair did not accompany his voice in any way, and his sweet speech was everything that should have delighted enthusiastic passengers.

One day, a young Daughter of God Vega came to the Carrier and asked to take her several dimensions ahead. She had never felt those places before, and she wanted to find out how it was possible to learn with the help of a completely different understanding of the world, as she thought, more complete and unusual.

Vega and Altair started talking. They were concerned that since the time when their world was created (the faith of The Children of God in The Supreme-God-Demiurge was unshakable and there were several artifacts confirming its existence), no one talks about whether other worlds similar to theirs were created. And is it possible for simple Child of God to become like The Supreme-God-Demiurge? Can Vega or Altair achieve such perfection in their art that they can create worlds themselves? Once Altair heard from one of the passengers that it was possible to combine the attributes of several social classes so that the result would be “something inexpressible". For example, an element for a combination could be Altair's Lyre or his fairy tales. And Vega's…

Vega continued the craft of the Weavers' class: The Weavers planned the trajectories of the Carriers. One of her tools were Needles — they marked points in the multidimensional space of their world that Carriers had to pass through to activate their abilities and reach the right tools. Accordingly, the attributes of Vega for the necessary combination that could lead to the creation of a new world could be Needles.

Altair and Vega spent a lot of time together: Vega often traveled, and Altair seemed to inevitably, by fate itself, find himself on her way. Vega listened attentively to all his fairy tales and once admitted that she would like to hear them at night: at a time when Altair was changing his external form and playing the Lyre. Altair agreed, and from then on, once every few weeks or months, they spent a Night of Songs together. Vega brought Needles to these meetings and, instead of plotting the trajectories of future interdimensional movements with them, she clung to Altair's words, the overtones of his voice, and connected them to the place where they were. Now, with the help of Needles, pebbles, leaves of rare shrubs, sand and even fog seemed to enter into a dialogue with Altair. Vega felt almost like an Engineer: what if she and Altair could create a new world? It seems that they already have almost everything for this…

One day Altair received a special task and realized that he had to leave the dimension where Vega lived for a long time. They met again at the moment when Vega decided to go on one of her interdimensional journeys, and Altair told her the sad news: “Perhaps we will never feel each other with you again, only if the Engineers don't come to the rescue ... but now I can't tell you where to look for me, and how to contact me.” Vega was stunned, but tried to restrain herself. At parting, Altair presented her with a great gift: “without you, I don't see the point of singing. Take this Lyre and, if destined, create a new world alone.”

Vega accepted Altair's Lyre as a gift. She saw Altair off and returned home, looking at the Needles with hatred: “Am I really going to be forced to help lay routes for the rest of my days, on which we will never cross again?”

Vega plunged into the study of the art of pairing attributes — alchemy. In the end, she succeeded: by putting together the music of Altair's Lyre, Altair's songs, which Vega performed herself from now on, and what she turned into Needles, turning to Engineers for help — a toy car for transporting passengers moving along the rails (The Train) — Vega got a completely new living space. The movement of the Train for transportation, which Vega named after her attributes — the Needle, under her songs, created a special field around itself, which turned into the atmosphere of a new small planet — MHIWYA (it was in honor of her that I gave the name to the whole legend). on this planet, as Vega learns later, the seed of future life was also born.

The first people who appeared on MHIWYA were called Nomads or Voices, which is a more general term. Each of Nomads had a voice of fabulous beauty and depth, the ranges of which coincided with the ranges of the six strings of the Altair Lyre. From now on, the tales and songs of the Nomads will maintain the state of MHIWYA from the inside, while Vega continues her Eternal Divine Song of abandonment and loneliness from the outside. The nomads founded the City, and everyone they spawned became Citizens. Also, every Citizen was a Voice along the branch of the Nomad he was born with.

MHIWYA, as well as the World-of-the-Children-of-God, turned out to be multidimensional, but now communication between residents of different dimensions was carried out with the help of an Needle Train, transporting people to each other along looped rails that permeate the entire new planet. Tiny villages formed around the rails at special points where the Train moved from one dimension to another. The villages were inhabited by Fishermen — those who, at the right moment, turned the arrows on the rails and ensured the correct transition of the Train from dimension to dimension.

The Needle rails were unstable: since the Train moves forever, the rails are constantly being rebuilt, but the path along them remains looped. Necessarily on its way, the Needle falls into many Points where space allows you to move from one dimension to another.

This is the end of the MHIWYA legend. What I managed to write.

environmental performance, while a larger product size seems to have better

environment, and business flexibility, while plastic materials have a better cost

However, it is hard to generalize from these findings and comment on the future
of the technology since every day we see technological advances in equipment and

6.3 Economic Analysis
In order to understand the size of cost-effective production volume, break-even
points can be considered as a useful measure. This measure is generally used to
determine when a business will be able to cover all its expenses and begin to make a
profit. In this case, the break-even points tell us the maximum size of production
volumes below which AM technologies represent a more cost-effective manufacturing process compared to conventional manufacturing. However, the break-even
point of production is case-specific, depending on technological aspects such as part
complexity, material and build volume.
In an early attempt to compare the cost per part of additive and conventional
processes, Hopkinson and Dickens (2003) studied SLS (additive) and injection
molding (conventional). The curve of injection molding (Fig. 6.12) clearly shows
cost-effective production at larger volumes because the initial costs (for instance of
the mold) are amortized across the production, whereas the cost per part for the
additive process remains constant from a single production to a larger production.

Ruffo et al. (2006) overcame the limitations of the previous study, by considering further components of the cost of production such as labor, materials,
machine, and administrative overheads. In contrast to the last study, the new
analysis has a curve with a saw-tooth shape to the filling of the machine bed space
(Fig. 6.13). It also shows the higher cost per part for single or lower production
volumes due to the initial costs of setting up. The break-even point moved from
14,000 parts in the previous study of 2003–9000 parts in the current study, thanks
to the newly developed cost estimation model.
Then, Ruffo and Hague (in 2007) looked at the capability of AM technologies in
the simultaneous production of different components, which may affect the cost per
part at lower production volumes. In other words, as seen in Fig. 6.14, the study
compared the production of copies of the same parts and parallel printing of mixed
components, both with an SLS system. The results demonstrate the efficient operational costs when simultaneously printing mixed components. The optimized mixing
of the components in the building platform also results in further cost savings.
The previously mentioned experiments considered objects that were additively
manufactured with plastic materials. So, for parts made of plastic, the results
demonstrate that the competitiveness of AM in comparison with conventional
manufacturing is well established. However, when considering the design optimization offered by AM, more cost effective operation can be expected as previous
studies did not consider the possible optimization, and the design file was that used
in conventional manufacturing. The potential design optimization comes from the
